records.name: The Shire
records.description: The homeland of the Hobbits, a fertile agricultural country in north-western Eriador between the Far Downs and the Brandywine River, settled in T.A. 1601 by Fallohide brothers Marcho and Blanco under charter from the King at Fornost. Divided into four Farthings around Michel Delving, it later gained Buckland and the Westmarch. Its Hobbits are famously insular and unaware of the wider world's perils.

chronicle.description: Marcho and Blanco lead Hobbits across the Brandywine to found the Shire.
Battle of Greenfields; Bandobras Took repels an Orc-invasion.
Battle of Bywater ends Sharkey's occupation, the only other battle fought in the Shire.

records.name: Northfarthing
records.description: The northernmost and least populous of the Shire's four Farthings, a cold hilly country of moorland, stone-quarries and scattered villages such as Oatbarton, Long Cleeve and Hardbottle. Sparsely settled compared to the rest of the Shire, it bordered the site of the Battle of Greenfields in T.A. 2747 and later saw ruffians occupy its villages during the Scouring.

records.name: Southfarthing
records.description: The mildest and southernmost Farthing of the Shire, bordering the Green Hill Country and Woody End. Its warm slopes around Longbottom produce the Shire's famous pipe-weed, first cultivated there by Tobold Hornblower around T.A. 2670. Sparsely populated, it stretches toward empty southern moors beyond the settled lands.

records.name: Eastfarthing
records.description: The eastern quarter of the Shire, running from the Three-Farthing Stone to the Brandywine River, encompassing Frogmorton, Whitfurrows, Woodhall, Stock and the marshy Marish. Crossed by the East Road, it borders Buckland across the river and includes the wooded uplands of Woody End and the stony hills of Scary in its north.

records.name: Westfarthing
records.description: The western quarter of the Shire, containing Michel Delving, the Shire's chief town, upon the White Downs, together with Hobbiton, Tookland and the Green Hill Country. It stretches west to the Far Downs and, after the Fourth Age began, the Westmarch beyond. Its rolling farmland made it the Shire's most prosperous and populous quarter.

records.name: The Yale
records.description: A small district of the Eastfarthing around Willowbottom and Deephallow, near where the Shirebourn joins the Brandywine. Rarely mentioned beyond Shire maps, it names the gentle river-country between the Woody End and the Overbourn Marshes, inhabited by farming Hobbits close to the Southfarthing border.

records.name: Westmarch
records.description: A tract between the Far Downs and the Tower Hills, granted to the Shire by King Elessar and formally added early in the Fourth Age as thanks for the Hobbits' part in the War of the Ring. Warden Fastred of Greenholm and his wife Elanor Gardner settled it from Undertowers; the Red Book of Westmarch takes its name from this region.

chronicle.description: The Westmarch is added to the Shire by grant of King Elessar.

records.name: Buckland
records.description: A narrow strip of the Shire east of the Brandywine, settled in T.A. 2340 when Gorhendad Oldbuck crossed the river and began delving Brandy Hall, taking the name Brandybuck. Protected from the Old Forest by the High Hay, it has its own customs, boats, and a Master of Buckland; its folk are hardier and more adventurous than most Hobbits.

chronicle.description: Gorhendad Oldbuck founds Buckland and begins Brandy Hall.
Frodo Baggins settles briefly at Crickhollow before departing for Rivendell.

records.name: The Marish
records.description: A rich, low-lying farmland in the south-east Eastfarthing along the Brandywine, drained by generations of hard-working Hobbits, many of Stoor descent. Famous for mushrooms and thick-set, sturdy folk such as the Maggot family of Bamfurlong, it lies between Stock, Rushey and the river, and floods easily in wet seasons.

records.name: Bridgefields
records.description: A district of the Eastfarthing surrounding the Shire end of the Brandywine Bridge, seat of the Bolger family at Budgeford. A prosperous farming region, it marks the Shire's easternmost settled land before the East Road crosses into Buckland and, beyond, Bree-land.

records.name: Green Hill Country
records.description: A range of low green hills in southern Westfarthing, rising south of Tuckborough and Michel Delving and running toward the Southfarthing border. The Tookland lies along its northern slopes, and villages such as Whitwell, Tookbank and Pincup dot its skirts; Bilbo Baggins was of Took stock from this country on his mother's side.

records.name: Tookland
records.description: The folkland of the Took family in the Green Hill Country of the Westfarthing, centred on Tuckborough and the Great Smials. Home of the hereditary Thain, it is more prosperous and adventurous than most of the Shire, having produced Bullroarer Took, Bilbo's mother Belladonna, and Peregrin Took.

records.name: Woody End
records.description: A pleasant wooded upland in the south of the Eastfarthing, between the Green Hill Country and the Shirebourn, favoured by Hobbits for picnics and by wandering Elves. Frodo, Sam and Pippin camped here on their first night out of Hobbiton and met Gildor Inglorion's Elves journeying to the Grey Havens in T.A. 3018.

chronicle.description: Frodo meets Gildor Inglorion and his Elves passing through Woody End.

records.name: Overbourn Marshes
records.description: A boggy tract where the River Shirebourn empties into the Brandywine below Deephallow, opposite the southern end of the High Hay. Named for lying beyond ("over") the Shirebourn, it forms the south-eastern corner of the Eastfarthing and is treacherous for travellers straying from the Ferry road.

records.name: The Bounds
records.description: The unmarked but well-known boundary of the Shire proper, watched in the years before the War of the Ring by the Shirriffs and, more quietly, by the Rangers of the North, who guarded it unthanked for generations so that Hobbits could live in untroubled peace within it.

records.name: Bree-land
records.description: A small, ancient settled land around Bree-hill at the crossing of the East Road and the Greenway, the last inhabited country before the Wild for travellers heading east. Home to both Big Folk and Hobbits living amicably side by side, it comprises Bree, Staddle, Combe and Archet, ringed by the Chetwood and the Midgewater Marshes.

records.name: Hobbiton
records.description: A prosperous village in the Westfarthing built along the Water below the Hill, on whose slope stands Bag End. Home of Bilbo and Frodo Baggins, it hosted Bilbo's Long-Expected Party in T.A. 3001. Under Sharkey's rule it was despoiled and its old mill replaced, before Sam Gamgee restored it after the Scouring in T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: Bilbo Baggins holds his eleventy-first birthday party and vanishes using the One Ring.
Ruffians occupy and despoil Hobbiton until the Battle of Bywater frees it.

records.name: Bag End
records.description: The Baggins family smial dug into the Hill above Hobbiton by Bungo Baggins around T.A. 2880 with his wife Belladonna Took's money. Home in turn to Bilbo and Frodo Baggins and later Sam Gamgee, it was the starting point of both The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings, and is famed for its round green door.

position.note: Small Hobbiton locations are separated on this schematic map for readability; this is not a measured plan of the Hill.

chronicle.description: Bilbo departs from Bag End on the quest of Erebor.
Frodo leaves Bag End, sold to Lobelia Sackville-Baggins, to begin his journey to Rivendell.

records.name: Bagshot Row
records.description: A row of humbler Hobbit-holes dug into the bank below Bag End, home of the Gamgee family, including Hamfast "Gaffer" Gamgee and his son Samwise. Sharkey's ruffians tore it down and built ugly brick houses during the Scouring; Sam had it replanted and renamed New Row afterward, using Galadriel's gift of earth.

records.name: The Hill
records.description: The low hill above Hobbiton into which Bag End is delved, overlooking the Water and Bywater Pool. Its slopes were felled and built over by Sharkey's men in T.A. 3019 before being restored by Sam Gamgee, who planted seedlings from Lothlórien including the Mallorn that grew where the Party Tree once stood.

records.name: Bywater
records.description: The last village of the Westfarthing, standing where the Bywater road crosses the Water beside Bywater Pool, a few miles south-east of Hobbiton. Home to the Green Dragon inn, it gave its name to the Battle of Bywater in T.A. 3019, the final battle of the Scouring of the Shire, fought at its crossroads.

chronicle.description: The Battle of Bywater is fought here, ending Sharkey's rule of the Shire.

records.name: Bywater Pool
records.description: A wide pool of the Water beside Bywater, overlooked by the Hill, into which Sharkey's new mill discharged filth during the occupation of the Shire, to the Hobbits' disgust. It was cleaned and restored after the Battle of Bywater in T.A. 3019.

records.name: The Green Dragon
records.description: A popular inn at Bywater where Sam Gamgee and his friends drank and traded gossip, notably hearing tales of Outsiders and strange folk on the roads in the spring of T.A. 3018. Closed under Sharkey's rule, it reopened after the Scouring of the Shire.

records.name: The Ivy Bush
records.description: An old inn on the Bywater road a little below Hobbiton, where the Gaffer and his neighbours gossiped about Bilbo's wealth and odd habits at the opening of The Lord of the Rings, setting the tone for the Shire's love of talk about its own affairs.

records.name: The Water
records.description: A modest river rising in the Westfarthing near Hobbiton, widening into Bywater Pool, and flowing east past Frogmorton and Whitfurrows to join the Brandywine near the Bridgefields. Its Hobbiton mill was rebuilt larger and dirtier by Sharkey's men before Sam Gamgee restored it after the Scouring.

records.name: Overhill
records.description: A small village north of Hobbiton, beyond the Hill, from which the fireworks of Bilbo's Long-Expected Party could be seen lighting up the sky in T.A. 3001. It lies near the southern eaves of Bindbole Wood in the Westfarthing.

records.name: The Mill
records.description: The old water-mill on the Water below the Hill, long run by the Sandyman family. Sharkey's ruffians tore it down in T.A. 3019 and raised an ugly, smoke-belching replacement to feed Saruman's schemes; after the Scouring, Sam Gamgee had it pulled down and a proper mill rebuilt.

chronicle.description: The old mill is demolished and replaced by an ugly steam-mill under Sharkey's rule.

records.name: Party Field
records.description: A field beside Bagshot Row and the Hobbiton road where Bilbo Baggins held his enormous birthday party for one hundred and forty-four guests in T.A. 3001, pitching a great pavilion over and around the old Party Tree. Sharkey's men felled the tree in T.A. 3019; Sam later planted a Mallorn sapling there from Galadriel's gift, the only one to bloom west of the Sea.

position.note: The field is shown separately from Bag End for readability. Its map spacing is illustrative, not a measured distance.

chronicle.description: Bilbo's Long-Expected Party is held in the Party Field.

records.name: Battle of Bywater (site)
records.description: On a banked stretch of the Bywater Road on 3 November T.A. 3019, Hobbits led by Merry and Pippin trapped Sharkey's ruffians. Nearly seventy ruffians were killed and twelve captured; nineteen Hobbits died and about thirty were wounded. This was the last battle of the War of the Ring.

chronicle.description: Hobbits defeat Saruman's ruffians, ending the occupation of the Shire.

records.name: Oatbarton
records.description: A farming village of the Northfarthing linked to the East Road by the Northway, its name recalling the great oat-farms of the surrounding moorland. One of the Shire's more remote settlements, it lies well north of Long Cleeve and the other Northfarthing villages.

records.name: Long Cleeve
records.description: The northernmost village of consequence in the Shire, seat of the North-took family, a branch of the Tooks descended from Bandobras "Bullroarer" Took. Diamond of Long Cleeve, who married Peregrin Took in the Fourth Age, came from here.

records.name: Hardbottle
records.description: A village of the stony northern Shire, home of the Bracegirdle family. Lobelia Sackville-Baggins, born a Bracegirdle, returned here to her kin after her release from the Lockholes at Michel Delving following the Scouring of the Shire in T.A. 3019.

records.name: Gamwich
records.description: A village of uncertain location near the Westfarthing's northern border, from which the roper Hamfast Gamwich took his name — later softened to "Gammidge" and, through his descendants' move to Tighfield, ultimately giving rise to the surname Gamgee borne by Samwise Gamgee.

records.name: Tighfield
records.description: A village of unrecorded location, home for generations to the Gammidge and Roper families' rope-walk. Wiseman Gamwich settled here about two centuries before the War of the Ring; his descendant Hamfast "the Gaffer" Gamgee left Tighfield's ropery for a gardener's life in Hobbiton, and became father to Samwise Gamgee.

records.name: Norbourn
records.description: A stream of the Northfarthing whose full course is imperfectly recorded, running near the Green Hills of the far north toward the Brandywine. Greenfields, site of the Battle of Greenfields in T.A. 2747, lay between the Norbourn and the Brandywine.

records.name: Greenfields
records.description: Open country of the Northfarthing between the Norbourn and the Brandywine where, in T.A. 2747, an Orc-band down from Mount Gram invaded the Shire and was destroyed by Bandobras "Bullroarer" Took, who felled the goblin-chieftain Golfimbul with a club — the only battle fought in the Shire before the War of the Ring.

chronicle.description: Bandobras "Bullroarer" Took defeats an Orc-invasion at the Battle of Greenfields, slaying Golfimbul.

records.name: Bindbole Wood
records.description: A small wood in the southern Northfarthing, north of Hobbiton and Overhill, whose name blends "bind" and "bole" (tree-trunk). It marks the transition from the settled Westfarthing farmland to the wilder northern moors of the Shire.

records.name: Hills of Scary
records.description: A stony, cave-riddled upland forming the northern part of the Eastfarthing, honeycombed with quarries that supplied much of the Shire's building stone. The village of Scary and the hidden burrows of Brockenborings lie among its rock-holes, which sheltered Fredegar Bolger's resistance during Sharkey's occupation.

records.name: Scary
records.description: A quarrying village amid the Hills of Scary in the northern Eastfarthing, which gave the hills their name. During the occupation of the Shire in T.A. 3019, Sharkey's ruffians stored plunder in its quarries, until Fredegar Bolger's rebels harried them from the surrounding rock-holes.

records.name: Brockenborings
records.description: A cluster of badger-burrow-like tunnels in the hilly Scary district of the northern Eastfarthing, whose name means roughly "badger-diggings." Fredegar Bolger and a band of Hobbit outlaws hid here from Sharkey's ruffians during the occupation of the Shire in T.A. 3019.

records.name: Quarry
records.description: A stone-quarry, or perhaps a small settlement, in the northern Eastfarthing between Scary and the Brandywine. Its unusually Westron-sounding name has puzzled scholars, since most Shire place-names derive from Old English or Celtic roots.

records.name: Dwaling
records.description: The Shire's northernmost village of note, lying just north of the Hills of Scary in the far Eastfarthing. Remote even by Northfarthing standards, it marked the edge of settled Hobbit country before the empty northern moors.

records.name: Needlehole
records.description: A village in a deep valley of the north-western Westfarthing, near the source of the Water and not far from Nobottle and Rushock Bog. One of the quieter, more out-of-the-way corners of the Shire.

records.name: Nobottle
records.description: A remote village west of Needlehole in the Westfarthing, its Old Hobbitish name suggesting a "new dwelling." Small and poor, tucked near the Far Downs, it exemplifies the Shire's habit of naming even its humblest hamlets.

records.name: Little Delving
records.description: A village near Michel Delving in the Westfarthing, its name distinguishing it as the smaller of the two "Delvings." Connected to Waymeet and Michel Delving by local roads, it lies in the gentle downland west of Hobbiton.

records.name: Michel Delving
alternateNames: Michel Delving on the White Downs
records.description: The chief town of the Shire, built into the White Downs and seat of the Mayor, the Shire's only elected official. Its Mathom-house holds the Shire's museum of curiosities, and its Lockholes were used as a prison by Sharkey's ruffians during the occupation of T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: Mayor Will Whitfoot is imprisoned in the Lockholes by Sharkey's ruffians.

records.name: The Mathom-house
records.description: The Shire's only museum, at Michel Delving, where Hobbits deposited "mathoms" — things they had no use for but could not bear to throw away. It once displayed the gilded mail-shirt Bilbo Baggins brought back from Erebor and gave to the town, until Frodo later reclaimed it for the road to Mordor.

records.name: The Lockholes
records.description: Storage-tunnels dug near Michel Delving, never before used for their grim purpose until Sharkey's ruffians turned them into a prison during the occupation of the Shire in T.A. 3019, holding Mayor Will Whitfoot, Lobelia Sackville-Baggins, and other resisters until their liberation after the Battle of Bywater.

chronicle.description: The Lockholes are used as a prison by Sharkey's men; freed after the Battle of Bywater.

records.name: White Downs
records.description: A range of chalky hills in the Westfarthing overlooking Michel Delving, into whose slopes the town is delved. Their pale soil gives them their name, and their high ground traditionally hosts the Shire's Free Fair at Midsummer.

records.name: Waymeet
records.description: A crossroads settlement in the Westfarthing where the East Road meets a road down from Little Delving and another up from Tookland and the Southfarthing — hence its name, "the meeting of three ways." Ruffians mustered here before marching on Bywater in T.A. 3019, only to be crushed at the Battle of Bywater.

chronicle.description: Ruffians muster at Waymeet before their defeat at the Battle of Bywater.

records.name: Whitwell
records.description: A village on the chalky Green Hills south of Waymeet and west of Tookbank, its name recalling the whitish soil of the district. Thain Paladin Took II, father of Peregrin Took, kept a farm here.

records.name: Greenholm
records.description: A village of the Westmarch, home of Fastred, who wedded Elanor "the Fair" Gardner, daughter of Samwise Gamgee, in the early Fourth Age. The couple later moved to Undertowers near the Tower Hills, becoming the first Warden and Lady of the Westmarch.

records.name: Undertowers
records.description: The seat of the Fairbairn family, Wardens of the Westmarch, built near the Tower Hills after Fastred of Greenholm and Elanor Gardner settled there around F.A. 41 (S.R. 1462). One of the Shire's three great archive-houses alongside Brandy Hall and the Great Smials, it kept a copy of the Red Book of Westmarch.

chronicle.description: Fastred and Elanor Fairbairn found Undertowers as seat of the Wardens of Westmarch.

records.name: Far Downs
records.description: A range of hills marking the old western boundary of the Shire before the Westmarch was added, lying between the Tower Hills and the White Downs. From their heights the Tower Hills, and on clear days a distant gleam of the Sea beyond, could reputedly be glimpsed.

records.name: Tower Hills
records.description: A range of hills west of the Far Downs, crowned by the three White Towers built by the Elves of Lindon, the tallest of which, Elostirion, held a palantír that looked only west across the Sea. After the Westmarch was granted to the Shire, the hills lay within Hobbit country for the first time.

records.name: Elostirion
records.description: The tallest and westernmost of the three White Towers on the Tower Hills, built by Gil-galad as a gift to Elendil. It alone held one of the palantíri, which looked only toward Tol Eressëa across the Sea; the stone remained there until Círdan removed it near the Third Age's end for Elrond and Galadriel's departure. Hobbits believed the Sea could be glimpsed from its summit.

records.name: Rushock Bog
records.description: A swampy stretch of the Water in the Westfarthing, south of Needlehole and north-west of Hobbiton, marked on the map "A Part of the Shire." A minor hazard for travellers off the main roads rather than a place of any settlement.

records.name: Tuckborough
records.description: The chief village of Tookland in the Green Hill Country, seat of the Took family and the Thain of the Shire, built around and beneath the Great Smials. Merry Brandybuck and Pippin Took mustered the Shire's resistance from here during the Battle of Bywater in T.A. 3019.

records.name: The Great Smials
records.description: The vast ancestral hall of the Took family at Tuckborough, one of the Shire's three great archive-houses alongside Brandy Hall and Undertowers. Seat of the Thain, it was home to the Old Took (Gerontius), Paladin Took II, and, after the War of the Ring, Thain Peregrin I.

records.name: Tookbank
records.description: A small village of Tookland in the Green Hill Country, not far west of Tuckborough, its name recalling its position on land held by the Took family. Like its larger neighbour, it lay within the Thain's own folkland and shared in Tookland's reputation for producing the Shire's more adventurous Hobbits.

records.name: Pincup
records.description: A village on the southern slopes of the Green Hill Country, in the northern corner of the Southfarthing a few miles south of the Three-Farthing Stone, linked to Longbottom by a single road.

records.name: Longbottom
records.description: A village in the warm Southfarthing where Tobold Hornblower first grew the true pipe-weed in his garden around T.A. 2670. Longbottom Leaf became the finest and most celebrated pipe-weed of the Shire, famous even beyond its borders — Saruman himself was known to enjoy it.

chronicle.description: Tobold Hornblower first cultivates pipe-weed at Longbottom.

records.name: Sackville
records.description: A minor locality of the Southfarthing lending its name to the well-to-do Sackville family, whose marriage into the Bagginses produced Otho and Lobelia Sackville-Baggins, longtime rivals of Bilbo and Frodo for Bag End. Little else is recorded of the place itself in the old chronicles beyond its name.

records.name: Frogmorton
records.description: A village on the East Road in the Eastfarthing, fourteen miles east of the Three-Farthing Stone, with a good inn well known to travellers. Frodo and his companions, disguised, passed anxiously through it in T.A. 3018 while being pursued, and Sharkey's men later held it during the occupation of the Shire.

records.name: The Floating Log
records.description: An inn at Stock in the Eastfarthing, mentioned by Merry Brandybuck as a stop where he and Fredegar Bolger planned to await Frodo before his abrupt change of route toward the Old Forest in September T.A. 3018.

records.name: Whitfurrows
records.description: A village on the East Road in the Eastfarthing, south of Budgeford and the Bridgefields, along the Water. A quiet farming settlement between Frogmorton and the Brandywine Bridge, it saw ruffian traffic pass along the Road during Sharkey's occupation of the Shire in T.A. 3019.

records.name: Budgeford
records.description: The seat of the Bolger family in the Bridgefields district of the Eastfarthing, north of Whitfurrows on a tributary of the Water, close to the Brandywine Bridge. Home village of Fredegar "Fatty" Bolger, who led Hobbit resistance from Brockenborings during the Scouring.

records.name: Brandywine Bridge
records.description: The great stone bridge carrying the East Road over the Brandywine into Buckland, the only crossing for wheeled traffic between the Shire and Bree-land. Sharkey's ruffians fortified a gate here during their occupation in T.A. 3019, barring Hobbits' return until Frodo and his companions broke through.

chronicle.description: Frodo, Sam, Merry and Pippin force the ruffians' gate at the Bridge on their return.

records.name: Girdley Island
records.description: A small island in the Brandywine north of the Bridge, on the Buckland side of the river, of little note beyond its appearance on Shire maps as one of the few named islands of the river.

records.name: Stock
records.description: A village of the Eastfarthing near the Marish, close to the Bucklebury Ferry, on the road Frodo's party used to slip quietly out of the Shire in T.A. 3018 rather than take the open East Road. Home of the Golden Perch, reputed to serve the best beer in the Eastfarthing.

records.name: The Golden Perch
records.description: An inn at Stock famed throughout the Eastfarthing for its beer — Pippin Took called it the best in the Shire, though Sam thought it a long walk for a drink. It featured in Frodo's cover story of moving to Buckland in T.A. 3018.

records.name: Bamfurlong
records.description: Farmer Maggot's farmstead in the Marish, ringed by mushroom-fields he guarded fiercely with his dogs. Frodo, Sam and Pippin sheltered here fleeing a Black Rider in September T.A. 3018, and Maggot ferried them onward to the Bucklebury Ferry with news for Buckland.

chronicle.description: Frodo and his companions take refuge with Farmer Maggot from a Ringwraith.

records.name: Woodhall
records.description: A village on the Stock road in the Eastfarthing near the edge of Woody End, passed by Frodo's company on their way toward the Bucklebury Ferry in T.A. 3018, avoiding the watched East Road.

records.name: Rushey
records.description: A small village of the Marish on the Stock road between Woodhall and the Bucklebury Ferry, in the low, rush-grown country near the Brandywine. Frodo's company passed near it cross-country in September T.A. 3018 on their quiet route out of the Shire toward Buckland.

records.name: Deephallow
records.description: A village on the Brandywine's western bank just north of where the Shirebourn flows in, opposite Haysend at the southern tip of Buckland, on the Shire's eastern border. Its name, meaning a deep hollow or nook, describes its low-lying position among the river's marshy margins.

records.name: Willowbottom
records.description: A village of the Eastfarthing near Woody End, standing where Thistle Brook flows into the River Shirebourn, in the gentle valley country known as the Yale. Its willow-lined banks and low ground give the settlement its descriptive Old English name.

records.name: Thistle Brook
records.description: A stream of the Eastfarthing flowing south-east around Woody End and through Willowbottom before joining the River Shirebourn, draining the wooded uplands south of the Three-Farthing Stone into the gentle river-country of the Yale.

records.name: Shirebourn
records.description: A lesser river rising in the Green Hill Country and running south-east to form the border between the Eastfarthing and Southfarthing, joined by Thistle Brook at Willowbottom before emptying into the Brandywine beneath Deephallow, where its mouth forms the Overbourn Marshes.

records.name: Sarn Ford
records.description: The stony ford where the Greenway crosses the River Baranduin south of the Shire, once guarded by a small fort of the Dúnedain of Cardolan, later watched by the Rangers of the North. In T.A. 3018 the Black Riders skirmish here with Rangers guarding the crossing before turning north toward the Shire.

chronicle.description: The Nazgûl force the ford, scattering its Ranger guard, during the hunt for the Ring.
The Nazgûl fight and scatter a party of Rangers guarding the ford.

records.name: Stockbrook
records.description: A minor stream of the Eastfarthing running past Stock toward the Marish and the Brandywine, giving the village its name. It waters the low farmland between Woodhall and the Bucklebury Ferry before losing itself among the marshy Marish.

records.name: Three-Farthing Stone
records.description: A stone beside the East Road marking the point where the Eastfarthing, Westfarthing and Southfarthing meet, five miles south-east of Bywater and fourteen miles west of Frogmorton — reckoned the very centre of the Shire.

records.name: Brandy Hall
records.description: The vast ancestral smial of the Brandybuck family, dug into Buck Hill above the Bucklebury Ferry from T.A. 2340 onward by Gorhendad Oldbuck, who founded Buckland. With three great doors and a hundred windows, it housed the orphaned Frodo Baggins from T.A. 2980 to 2989, and was later one of the Shire's three great archive-houses.

chronicle.description: The orphaned Frodo Baggins comes to live at Brandy Hall.

records.name: Bucklebury
records.description: The chief village of Buckland, standing above the Bucklebury Ferry on the east bank of the Brandywine, beneath Brandy Hall. Home of the Brandybuck family and the Master of Buckland, it was the last settled place Frodo's company passed before entering the Old Forest in T.A. 3018.

records.name: Bucklebury Ferry
records.description: The chief crossing of the Brandywine between the Shire and Buckland, near Bucklebury and Stock. Frodo, Sam, Pippin and Merry crossed here on the night of 26 September T.A. 3018, narrowly outrunning a Black Rider on the Shire shore.

chronicle.description: Frodo's company narrowly escapes a Black Rider by crossing the Ferry.

records.name: Crickhollow
records.description: A house in central Buckland near the High Hay, secretly bought by Frodo Baggins as a cover for his departure from the Shire. Merry and Pippin prepared it in T.A. 3018 to receive Frodo and Sam before the company slipped away into the Old Forest instead, evading a pursuing Black Rider.

chronicle.description: Frodo's company gathers at Crickhollow before fleeing into the Old Forest.

records.name: Newbury
records.description: A village in the north of Buckland near the Brandywine Bridge, one of the settlements founded as the Brandybucks' land grew after Gorhendad Oldbuck first crossed the river in T.A. 2340.

records.name: Standelf
records.description: A small village in southern Buckland, its name meaning "stone-delving." The road south from Bucklebury toward Haysend was said on published maps to end here, though some accounts extend Hobbit habitation further south still.

records.name: Haysend
records.description: The southernmost point of Buckland, where the High Hay meets the Brandywine and the Withywindle flows out of the Old Forest into the river. Its few Hobbits were reputed fiercer and more wary than most, living so near the Forest's uncanny edge.

records.name: The Hay Gate
records.description: A gate in the High Hay near Crickhollow through which Merry Brandybuck led Frodo, Sam and Pippin into the Old Forest at dawn on 26 September T.A. 3018, drawing suspicious looks from other Bucklanders for tempting fate.

chronicle.description: Frodo's company passes through the Hay Gate into the Old Forest.

records.name: The High Hay
records.description: A great, thick hedge planted by the Brandybucks to shield Buckland's western and southern border from the malice of the Old Forest, running from Haysend in the south to near the Brandywine Bridge in the north. It has mostly kept the trees' hostility at bay since Buckland's founding in T.A. 2340.

records.name: Buck Hill
records.description: The hill above Bucklebury and the Ferry into which Brandy Hall has been delved since T.A. 2340, growing over generations until the hall honeycombed the entire hill, giving the Brandybuck family and their followers the popular nickname "the Bucklanders of Buck Hill."

records.name: Bonfire Glade
records.description: A permanently open, treeless clearing deep in the Old Forest, kept bare since angry Bucklanders felled and burned hundreds of hostile trees here in reprisal after the trees attacked the High Hay. Merry led Frodo, Sam and Pippin through it in T.A. 3018.

records.name: The Old Forest
records.description: A dark, ancient wood east of Buckland beyond the High Hay, the last remnant of the vast primeval forests that once covered Eriador. Its trees, resentful of two-legged folk, are said to be half-awake and hostile; Tom Bombadil alone holds mastery within it. Frodo's company was nearly lost here in T.A. 3018 before Tom rescued them from Old Man Willow.

chronicle.description: Frodo, Sam, Merry and Pippin are trapped and rescued from Old Man Willow by Tom Bombadil.

records.name: Withywindle
records.description: A slow, mysterious river winding through the Old Forest from the Barrow-downs to the Brandywine at Haysend, whose banks breed a heavy drowsiness in travellers. Old Man Willow grew beside it, and Tom Bombadil's house stands near its upper course.

records.name: Old Man Willow
records.description: A vast, malevolent willow-tree on the banks of the Withywindle, the oldest and most powerful tree in the Old Forest, whose will lay behind much of the wood's hostility. In T.A. 3018 it sang Merry and Pippin to sleep and trapped them in its trunk, until Tom Bombadil's song forced it to release them.

chronicle.description: Old Man Willow traps Merry and Pippin until Tom Bombadil intervenes.

records.name: Tom Bombadil's House
records.description: The home of Tom Bombadil and Goldberry, standing between the Old Forest and the Barrow-downs above the Withywindle. Frodo's company sheltered here for two nights in T.A. 3018, receiving warning and counsel, and were saved a second time by Tom after their ordeal in the Great Barrow.

chronicle.description: Frodo's company rests here, sheltered by Tom Bombadil and Goldberry.

records.name: Barrow-downs
records.description: A range of grassy hills east of the Old Forest, crowned with ancient burial-mounds raised in the First and Second Ages, later reused by the Dúnedain of Cardolan. After Cardolan fell to Angmar around T.A. 1409, evil spirits from Angmar entered the empty barrows and lingered there as Barrow-wights into the Third Age's final years.

chronicle.description: Frodo, Sam, Merry and Pippin are captured by a Barrow-wight and rescued by Tom Bombadil.

records.name: The Great Barrow
records.description: The largest and most feared of the Barrow-downs' mounds, haunted by a Barrow-wight that entrapped Frodo, Sam, Merry and Pippin in T.A. 3018, dressing them as if for burial with ancient treasure. Tom Bombadil banished the wight and gave each Hobbit a barrow-blade from its hoard, one of which Merry later used to help wound the Witch-king at the Pelennor Fields.

chronicle.description: Frodo's company is trapped by the Barrow-wight and freed by Tom Bombadil.

records.name: Bree
records.description: The chief town of Bree-land, built on and about Bree-hill at the crossing of the East Road and the Greenway, with some hundred stone houses of Men and many Hobbit-holes on the hillside. Home to the Prancing Pony, it was settled by Men in the Elder Days and later joined by Hobbits fleeing east around T.A. 1300, remaining prosperous under the hidden watch of the Rangers.

chronicle.description: Frodo and his companions meet Aragorn at the Prancing Pony.

records.name: The Prancing Pony
records.description: The famous inn of Bree, run by Barliman Butterbur, a rambling old house of many chimneys where Men and Hobbits drink together. Here in T.A. 3018 Frodo Baggins accidentally slipped on the Ring before a room full of suspicious eyes, and met Aragorn, who guided the Hobbits onward toward Rivendell after Black Riders raided the inn that same night.

chronicle.description: Frodo puts on the Ring by accident; the Hobbits meet Strider (Aragorn).

records.name: Bree-hill
records.description: The hill on whose slopes and summit the town of Bree is built, at the crossing of the East Road and the Greenway, giving the whole surrounding land its name.

records.name: Staddle
records.description: The largest of Bree-land's outlying villages, on the far side of Bree-hill, home mostly to Hobbits alongside a scattering of Men. Together with Combe and Archet it made up the wider Bree-land beyond Bree itself.

records.name: Combe
records.description: A village of Bree-land in a valley ("combe") east of Bree, inhabited chiefly by Men, one of the four settlements — with Bree, Staddle and Archet — that made up the ancient homeland of the Bree-folk.

records.name: Archet
records.description: The northernmost village of Bree-land, standing close by the eaves of the Chetwood, inhabited by Men. Its name and the forest's share a root meaning "wood," and its woodcutters and charcoal-burners worked the fringes of the Chetwood for the whole of Bree-land.

records.name: Chetwood
records.description: A wood on the northern edge of Bree-land, near Archet, sharing its name's root. Black Riders lurked at its fringes in the autumn of T.A. 3018, and Bree-landers avoided it after dark, though it held nothing so old or malicious as the Old Forest far to the west.

records.name: The Greenway
records.description: The ancient North-South Road of Arnor, once linking Fornost to Tharbad and the south, long since grass-grown and disused save by the Bree-folk, who call it the Greenway. It crosses the East Road at Bree, and Frodo's company avoided it for fear of pursuit in T.A. 3018.

records.name: The East Road
records.description: The great highway of Eriador, running from the Grey Havens through the Shire, Bree, and past Weathertop to Rivendell and, ultimately, over the Misty Mountains toward Rhovanion. Built in the days of Arnor, by the Third Age's end it was quiet and lonely east of Bree, but remained the Shire's principal link to the wider world.

records.name: Midgewater Marshes
records.description: A wide, midge-infested fen in the Lone-lands east of Bree, through which the East Road picks a winding causeway. Frodo's company flounders through its stagnant pools and clouds of biting insects for two miserable days on the way toward Weathertop in T.A. 3018.

chronicle.description: Aragorn leads Frodo's company through the marshes, harried by clouds of midges.
Frodo and his companions struggle through the marshes en route to Weathertop.

records.name: Weather Hills
records.description: A line of bare hills running north from Weathertop along the old borders of Arnor's successor-kingdoms, remnants of the eastern march of Arthedain and Rhudaur. Largely empty of habitation by the Third Age's end, they lie between the Shire's East Road and the wilder Angle further east.

chronicle.description: King Argeleb I falls defending the fortified Weather Hills against Rhudaur and Angmar.

records.name: Weathertop
records.description: The southernmost and greatest of the Weather Hills, once crowned by a watch-tower of Arnor holding one of the palantíri, raised not long after Elendil founded the North-kingdom. Destroyed by Angmar in T.A. 1409, its ruin remained a landmark and refuge; here on the night of 6 October T.A. 3018, the Nazgûl attacked Frodo's company, and the Witch-king wounded Frodo with a Morgul-knife.

chronicle.description: The tower of Amon Sûl is destroyed by the forces of Angmar.
The Nazgûl attack Frodo's camp; the Witch-king wounds Frodo with a Morgul-blade.

records.name: The Forsaken Inn
records.description: The last inn on the East Road east of Bree, a day's journey out and about a quarter of the way to Weathertop, marking the true edge of settled country. Thorin's company camped near it in T.A. 2941 before crossing the Last Bridge; by the time of the War of the Ring it stood as a lonely landmark on an otherwise empty road.

chronicle.description: Thorin's company camps near the inn on the road to Rivendell.

records.name: Brandywine
records.description: The great river forming the Shire's eastern border, called Baranduin ("long golden river") by the Elves and anglicised affectionately by Hobbits as "Brandywine." It rises from Lake Evendim, is crossed by the Brandywine Bridge and the Bucklebury Ferry, and passes Sarn Ford before reaching the Sea, marking the boundary between the Shire and Buckland and the Old Forest.

records.name: Eriador
records.description: The wide land between the Misty Mountains and the Blue Mountains, once part of the realm of Arnor. By the end of the Third Age it is thinly peopled, home to the Shire, Bree-land, scattered Dúnedain Rangers, and many ruins of a vanished kingdom. Eriador is bounded north by Forodwaith, south by Enedwaith and Dunland.

chronicle.description: Elendil and the Faithful settle Eriador after the Downfall of Númenor.
Fall of Arthedain, last Dúnedain kingdom of Eriador.

records.name: Arnor
records.description: The northern realm founded by Elendil in Eriador, twin kingdom to Gondor, ruled from Annúminas and later Fornost. Weakened by war with Angmar, it split in T.A. 861 into Arthedain, Rhudaur and Cardolan, all eventually destroyed; its royal line survives to become the Chieftains of the Dúnedain and, in Aragorn, King Elessar.

chronicle.description: Founded by Elendil.
Splits into Arthedain, Rhudaur and Cardolan on the death of King Eärendur.
The North Kingdom's line, Angmar's destroyer, is avenged; Arnor's heritage passes to the Chieftains.

records.name: Arthedain
records.description: The northernmost of the three splinter-kingdoms of Arnor, holding the line of Isildur's heirs and the North-kingdom's palantíri, ruled from Fornost. It absorbed Cardolan and outlasted Rhudaur, but was overrun by Angmar in T.A. 1974; the Witch-king's host was destroyed the next year, too late to save the kingdom.

chronicle.description: Formed at the division of Arnor.
King Argeleb I claims lordship over all Arnor's former lands.
Fornost falls to the Witch-king; King Arvedui flees north and drowns off Forochel.

records.name: Cardolan
records.description: The southern splinter-realm of Arnor, between the Baranduin, the Hoarwell and the Greyflood, encompassing the Barrow-downs, South Downs and Tharbad. Its princes fought Angmar alongside Arthedain until the Great Plague of T.A. 1636 destroyed nearly all its people, after which Angmar sent evil spirits to haunt its barrows.

chronicle.description: Formed at the division of Arnor.
Angmar invades; the last prince of Cardolan is slain and buried in the Barrow-downs.
The Great Plague all but empties the realm.

records.name: Rhudaur
records.description: The easternmost splinter-realm of Arnor, between the Ettenmoors, the Weather Hills and the Misty Mountains, including the Angle and the Trollshaws. Its scant Dúnedain population was overwhelmed by evil hill-men allied with Angmar, and by T.A. 1409 the kingdom's remaining Dúnedain were dead or fled; only Orcs and hill-folk lingered after.

chronicle.description: Formed at the division of Arnor.
An Angmar-allied hill-lord seizes Rhudaur; King Argeleb I is slain fighting it.
Angmar overruns Rhudaur outright.

records.name: Lindon
records.description: The last Elvish realm west of the Misty Mountains, a green coastal strip of ancient Ossiriand and East Beleriand left above the waves when the rest of Beleriand drowned at the end of the First Age. Ruled by Gil-galad until S.A. 3441 and afterward by Círdan the Shipwright from the Grey Havens, it remains sparsely peopled by Elves departing over the Sea.

chronicle.description: Gil-galad's Elves and the Númenóreans defeat Sauron in the War of the Elves and Sauron.
Gil-galad leads the Last Alliance east from Lindon against Sauron.

records.name: Angmar
records.description: The evil realm founded around T.A. 1300 by the Lord of the Nazgûl, straddling the northern Misty Mountains from Carn Dûm, gathering Orcs, evil Men and hill-tribes to destroy the Dúnedain of the North. Angmar overthrew Rhudaur, Cardolan and finally Arthedain before a combined host of Gondor, Lindon and Rivendell annihilated it in T.A. 1975.

chronicle.description: Founded by the Witch-king.
Angmar destroys Amon Sûl and overruns Cardolan.
Angmar conquers Fornost and Arthedain.
Angmar's host is destroyed at the Battle of Fornost; the realm ends.

records.name: Forodwaith
records.description: The vast frozen wilderness of the far north, beyond Angmar and the Ice-bay of Forochel, home in ancient days to remnants of Men who fled southward before the cold or the ill-will of Angmar. By the Third Age it is desolate but for the hardy Lossoth of Forochel's coasts.

records.name: Forochel
records.description: The icy coastland at the north-western edge of Eriador, comprising the great Icebay and the Cape of Forochel, named from Sindarin for 'northern ice'. It is the home of the Lossoth, or Snow-men, who alone endure its bitter winters, and the place where King Arvedui of Arthedain perished in T.A. 1975.

chronicle.description: Arvedui, last King of Arthedain, shelters here with the Lossoth before drowning at sea.

records.name: Minhiriath
records.description: The land 'between the rivers' Baranduin and Gwathló, once covered by a vast forest that the Númenóreans felled for ship-timber during the Second Age, provoking the enmity of its Men. By the Third Age it is largely empty fen and downland, part of ruined Cardolan, with only Eryn Vorn left of its ancient wood.

chronicle.description: Númenórean shipwrights begin the great felling of Minhiriath's forests.

records.name: Enedwaith
records.description: The 'middle-march' between the Greyflood and the Isen, claimed by neither Arnor nor Gondor and so left masterless after Númenórean deforestation drove out its Men in the Second Age. Its scattered folk became ancestors of the Dunlendings; by the Third Age it is wild, crossed only by the crumbling Old South Road.

records.name: Dunland
records.description: The hill-country on the western slopes of the southern Misty Mountains, between the Glanduin and the Isen, home to the Dunlendings, a remnant of the Men driven from Enedwaith and Minhiriath by Númenórean tree-felling. Long resentful of Rohan's founding on lands they once roamed, they besiege Helm's Deep in the War of the Ring at Saruman's urging.

chronicle.description: Rohan is granted to the Éothéod, hemming in Dunlending expansion east of the Isen.
Dunlendings, incited by Saruman, besiege the Hornburg and are defeated.

records.name: Eregion
records.description: The 'Land of Holly', an Elven realm founded around S.A. 700 by Galadriel and Celeborn on the west slopes of the Misty Mountains beside Moria, home to the Gwaith-i-Mírdain, greatest of Elven smiths. Sauron's deception of its craftsmen led to the forging of the Rings of Power and, in S.A. 1697, to the realm's utter destruction.

chronicle.description: Sauron, as Annatar, comes among the smiths of Eregion.
Sauron's armies storm and destroy Ost-in-Edhil; Eregion ceases to be.

records.name: Misty Mountains
records.description: The great range of Hithaeglir, running north from Mount Gundabad to Methedras above Fangorn, dividing Eriador from Rhovanion. Raised by Melkor in the Elder Days to hinder Oromë's riding, it is riddled with Orc-holds and the ancient Dwarf-mansion of Moria, and crossed only by the High Pass and the Redhorn Pass.

records.name: Blue Mountains
records.description: The long range separating Lindon from the rest of Eriador, all that remains above water of the mountains that once bordered Beleriand in the west. Beneath Mount Dolmed the Firebeards and Broadbeams first awoke; the War of Wrath broke the range's centre, letting in the sea to form the Gulf of Lune. Dwarves of Durin's line still delve there in the Third Age.

chronicle.description: c. The Firebeards and Broadbeams awaken beneath Mount Dolmed.
The War of Wrath breaks the range and floods the Gulf of Lune.

records.name: Forlindon
records.description: The northern half of Lindon, lying north of the Gulf of Lune between the sea and the northern arm of the Blue Mountains, with the small haven of Forlond on its coast. It is sparsely peopled even by Elvish standards, a quiet green land facing the Sundering Seas.

records.name: Harlindon
records.description: The southern half of Lindon, south of the Gulf of Lune between the sea and the southern arm of the Blue Mountains, holding the haven of Harlond. Together with Forlindon it formed Gil-galad's and later Círdan's realm, the last Elf-land in Middle-earth west of the mountains.

records.name: Grey Havens
records.description: The great Elven haven at the head of the Gulf of Lune, seat of Círdan the Shipwright, from which ships bearing the Three Rings' keepers and the Ring-bearers sail west over the Sea. It is the last Elvish city in Middle-earth and the point of departure for all who leave these shores for Aman.

chronicle.description: Founded soon after the War of Wrath as Gil-galad's chief port.
Frodo, Bilbo, Gandalf, Galadriel and Elrond sail from here into the West.

records.name: Forlond
records.description: The lesser of the two harbours of the outer Gulf of Lune, on the coast of Forlindon north of the Grey Havens' inlet. Little is recorded of it beyond its name and place on the map of the Third Age, a quiet Elven haven in the northern arm of Lindon.

records.name: Harlond
records.description: The southern harbour of the Gulf of Lune, on the coast of Harlindon, not to be confused with the Harlond of Minas Tirith far to the south. It served the Elves of southern Lindon as a lesser haven alongside Mithlond.

records.name: Gulf of Lune
records.description: The great sea-inlet driven into the coast of Lindon when the War of Wrath broke the Blue Mountains at the end of the First Age, drowning the valley of the River Lhûn. The Grey Havens stand at its head, and Forlond and Harlond upon its outer shores.

chronicle.description: Formed when the sea breaks through the Blue Mountains at the War of Wrath's end.

records.name: River Lune
records.description: The river that rises in the Blue Mountains and flows down through Lindon into the Gulf of Lune at the Grey Havens, the only river of Middle-earth named for the Vala-touched land it drains toward. Its valley was drowned to form the Gulf when the mountains were broken in the War of Wrath.

records.name: Belegaer
records.description: The Great Sea separating Middle-earth from Aman, upon whose eastern shore Lindon lies. Across it lies Tol Eressëa and, beyond the Straight Road opened after the Downfall of Númenor, the Undying Lands themselves, reachable only by the ships that sail from the Grey Havens.

records.name: Thorin's Halls
records.description: Halls established by Thráin II in T.A. 2802 in the eastern side of the southern Ered Luin after the wandering years following the loss of Erebor. Thorin worked iron here before his quest. The exact location is unrecorded, and whether the description places them north or south of the Gulf of Lune is debated; the marker is conjectural.

chronicle.description: Thráin II establishes the realm.
Thorin Oakenshield departs with his company on the Quest of Erebor.

records.name: Nogrod
records.description: One of the two great Dwarf-cities of the First Age, home of the Firebeard clan, delved beneath the Blue Mountains near Mount Dolmed. Its craftsmen forged the Nauglamír and slew Thingol of Doriath in a quarrel over the Silmaril set within it. Ruined by the War of Wrath, only broken halls remain by the Third Age.

position.note: A First Age location projected onto the changed Third Age coastline. Its relationship to Dolmed is retained, not an exact surviving site.

chronicle.description: Nogrod's Dwarves slay King Thingol at Menegroth over the Nauglamír.

records.name: Belegost
records.description: The greater of the two First Age Dwarf-cities beneath the Blue Mountains, home of the Broadbeam clan, whose warriors under Azaghâl of Belegost fought and wounded Glaurung the dragon at the Nirnaeth Arnoediad. Broken like Nogrod by the War of Wrath, its ruins lie forgotten beneath the mountains by the Third Age.

position.note: A First Age location projected onto the changed Third Age coastline. Its relationship to Dolmed is retained, not an exact surviving site.

chronicle.description: Azaghâl of Belegost wounds Glaurung at the Nirnaeth Arnoediad and is slain.

records.name: Mount Dolmed
records.description: A great peak of the Blue Mountains beneath which the Dwarf-fathers of the Firebeards and Broadbeams are said to have first awoken in the deeps of time, and near which the cities of Nogrod and Belegost were delved. It remains a landmark of the range through the Third Age.

records.name: Annúminas
records.description: The first capital of Arnor, built by Elendil on the south-eastern shore of Lake Evendim, holding the Sceptre of Annúminas and a palantír. Losses in war and the Gladden Fields disaster emptied it long before the Third Age's end, when it stands abandoned — until King Elessar restores it as a northern seat after his coronation.

chronicle.description: Founded by Elendil as Arnor's capital.
Long since abandoned, it falls within Arthedain at Arnor's division.
King Elessar begins Annúminas's restoration.

records.name: Fornost Erain
records.description: 'Royal Fornost', the later capital of Arnor and then of Arthedain, on the North Downs about a hundred miles north of Bree. Captured by the Witch-king in T.A. 1974, it was avenged the next year when Eärnur's host broke Angmar on the plain before its gates; feared afterward as 'Deadmen's Dike', it lies in ruin at the end of the Third Age.

chronicle.description: The Witch-king captures Fornost; King Arvedui flees north.
Battle of Fornost: Eärnur's host from Gondor and Lindon destroys Angmar's army before the city.

records.name: Lake Evendim
records.description: 'Lake of Twilight', a broad lake in north-western Eriador on whose south-eastern shore Elendil built Annúminas. Fed among other springs by waters draining the Emyn Uial, it is the traditional source of the River Baranduin, and the site in T.A. 1975 of Angmar's final overthrow between its shores and the North Downs.

chronicle.description: Angmar's host is finally broken between Evendim and the North Downs.

records.name: Emyn Uial
records.description: The 'Hills of the Twilight' ringing the north and west shores of Lake Evendim, from whose slopes streams feed the lake and, by tradition, the infant Baranduin. A quiet upland of Arnor's heartland, little touched by the wars that ruined the kingdom around it.

records.name: North Downs
records.description: A range of chalk downs in northern Eriador on whose southern spur Fornost was built, long the heartland of Arthedain. Aragorn as a boy roamed these hills learning lore of old Arnor, and their slopes still bear faint marks of ancient fortification from the wars with Angmar.

records.name: South Downs
records.description: A range of downs in southern Eriador, west of the Greenway and south of the Barrow-downs, once part of Cardolan. The narrow gap called Andrath, between these downs and the Barrow-downs' spur, carries the old road south toward Tharbad and Gondor.

records.name: Lone-lands
records.description: The empty wild country east of Bree-land, stretching from the Weather Hills to the Trollshaws and Rivendell, crossed by the East Road but otherwise unpeopled save for the occasional Ranger or wandering Troll. Frodo and his companions pass through this wilderness on the road to Rivendell in T.A. 3018.

chronicle.description: Frodo and his companions cross the Lone-lands, pursued by the Nazgûl, en route to Rivendell.

records.name: The Angle
records.description: The wedge of land in Rhudaur between the Rivers Hoarwell and Loudwater above their confluence, once home to the Stoor Hobbits before the terror of Angmar and the Great Plague drove them west to settle Bree-land and later the Shire around T.A. 1150–1300.

chronicle.description: Stoor Hobbits settle in the Angle.
c. Angmar's wars in Rhudaur drive the Stoors from the Angle westward.

records.name: Andrath
records.description: The narrow land where the Greenway runs between the end of the Barrow-downs and a spur of the South Downs, hedged and laned in later ages. Merry, Pippin, Frodo and Sam pass through it on their journey from the Shire toward Bree and the Barrow-downs in T.A. 3018.

records.name: Eryn Vorn
records.description: The 'Black Wood', a dark and little-explored forest on a headland between the mouths of the Baranduin and the Greyflood, the last surviving remnant of the great primeval forest that once covered Minhiriath before the Númenóreans felled it. Shy woodland folk, distrustful of all outsiders, are said to linger there still.

position.note: The marker names the wooded cape south of the Baranduin mouth. It is an area label, not a surveyed point; the woodland and estuary were checked together.

records.name: Forest of Minhiriath
records.description: The vast wood that once covered Minhiriath and much of Enedwaith, home to Men who fled Sauron's ruin in the Second Age. Aldarion's Númenórean shipwrights felled it for timber over centuries from S.A. 750 onward, embittering its people; only Eryn Vorn survives of it by the Third Age.

chronicle.description: c. Great felling of the forest begins for Númenórean shipbuilding.

records.name: Fens of Minhiriath
records.description: Marshy lowland in Cardolan-Minhiriath crossed by long causeways carrying the North-South Road toward the bridge at Tharbad. Built firm by Númenórean engineers, the causeways crumbled after the Great Plague of T.A. 1636 left too few hands to maintain them, leaving the road treacherous by the Third Age's end.

records.name: Tharbad
records.description: A fortified river-town and bridge on the Greyflood where the North-South Road crosses, once jointly maintained by Arnor and Gondor as the vital link between the Two Kingdoms. Its bridge fell to ruin after T.A. 2050, and the great flood following the Fell Winter of T.A. 2911 finally emptied Tharbad, leaving only crumbling walls in marsh by the War of the Ring.

chronicle.description: Tar-Aldarion of Númenor sails up the Gwathló to Tharbad and meets Galadriel.
Great floods ruin and empty Tharbad.

records.name: Bridge of Tharbad
records.description: The great stone bridge raised by Arnor and Gondor across the Greyflood at Tharbad to carry the North-South Road, essential to communication between the Two Kingdoms. Neglected after the kingdoms' decline, it became so ruinous by T.A. 2050 that travellers were forced to ford the river instead.

chronicle.description: The bridge becomes so ruinous that the river must be forded.

records.name: Lond Daer
records.description: 'Vinyalondë', the New Haven founded by Prince Aldarion of Númenor at the mouth of the Gwathló around S.A. 750–800, later renamed Lond Daer Enedh, the Great Middle Haven. A major Númenórean port supplying the felling of Minhiriath's forests, it declined after the Downfall of Númenor as Tharbad rose in its place, and lies ruinous by the Third Age.

chronicle.description: c. Aldarion founds Vinyalondë at the Gwathló's mouth.

records.name: Greyflood
records.description: 'Shadowy River', formed by the union of the Hoarwell and Glanduin and flowing south-west through Enedwaith to the Sea past Tharbad and Lond Daer. The Númenóreans used it to ship timber felled from Minhiriath and Enedwaith, and its bridge at Tharbad long carried the great North-South Road.

records.name: Hoarwell
records.description: 'Grey-cold', a river rising in the Ettenmoors and flowing south past the Last Bridge to join the Loudwater and form the Greyflood. It marked the border between Rhudaur and Cardolan, and its crossing at the Last Bridge is the only way over for travellers on the East Road.

records.name: Loudwater
records.description: A swift river flowing down from the Misty Mountains past Rivendell to join the Hoarwell and form the Greyflood. Its Ford of Bruinen guards the approach to Elrond's house, and Elrond and Gandalf can summon a sudden flood from it to overwhelm enemies who try to cross uninvited.

chronicle.description: Elrond raises the river in flood to sweep away the pursuing Nazgûl at the Ford.

records.name: Last Bridge
records.description: The last bridge on the East Road before Rivendell, spanning the Hoarwell where it runs deep and swift between the Weather Hills and the Trollshaws. In T.A. 3018 the company finds Gandalf's rune-mark here, and the Nazgûl watch it before the company slips past through the Trollshaws instead.

chronicle.description: Frodo's company finds Gandalf's token here and avoids the watching Black Riders.

records.name: Trollshaws
records.description: A wild, thinly-wooded hill country east of the Last Bridge and west of Rivendell, named for the stone-trolls that once lurked there, including the three encountered by Bilbo, Gandalf and Thorin's company. The company of the Ring skirts these hills warily in T.A. 3018 to avoid the Nazgûl on the road.

chronicle.description: Bilbo, Gandalf, and Thorin's company outwit and turn to stone the three trolls here.

records.name: Trolls' Cave
records.description: The hidden cave above a clearing in the Trollshaws where the trolls Tom, Bert and William hoarded stolen gold and the blades later named Sting, Glamdring and Orcrist, before Gandalf tricked them into squabbling past sunrise and they turned to stone. The company of the Ring pass the stone trolls again in T.A. 3018.

chronicle.description: Bilbo finds Sting in the trolls' hoard here.
The Fellowship passes the same stone trolls, now grown over with brambles.

records.name: Ford of Bruinen
records.description: The last crossing of the Loudwater before Rivendell, watched over by Elrond's power. Here in T.A. 3018 Frodo, on the edge of succumbing to his Morgul-wound, turns at bay against the Nine Riders, and Elrond and Glorfindel raise the river against them, sweeping away most of their horses.

chronicle.description: Frodo defies the Nazgûl at the Ford; the river rises and scatters them.

records.name: Rivendell
alternateNames: The Last Homely House East of the Sea
records.description: 'The Last Homely House East of the Sea', Elrond Half-elven's hidden refuge in a deep valley of the Loudwater beneath the Misty Mountains, founded in S.A. 1697 as a stronghold against Sauron. A haven of healing and lore, it hosts the Council of Elrond in T.A. 3018 that decides the fate of the One Ring, and the muster of the Fellowship that departs from it.

references.label: Foundation: The Lord of the Rings, Appendix B, Second Age (1697)
references.scope: Foundation year; reference located through Tolkien Gateway

references.label: Location and Bilbo's visit: The Hobbit, A Short Rest
references.scope: Valley and visit; chapter reference, not a claim that map coordinates are canonical

references.label: Council: The Fellowship of the Ring, The Council of Elrond
references.scope: Council and decision to destroy the Ring

chronicle.description: Elrond founds Rivendell as a refuge from Sauron's armies.
Thorin's company and Bilbo rest here on the way to Erebor.
The Council of Elrond meets and the Fellowship of the Ring is formed.

records.name: Hall of Fire
records.description: A great hall in Elrond's house at Rivendell where a fire burns always and songs and tales are told at need. Here Frodo first meets Bilbo again after nine years and hears Aragorn sing of Beren and Lúthien, on the evening before the Council of Elrond in T.A. 3018.

chronicle.description: Frodo is reunited with Bilbo and hears the lay of Beren and Lúthien sung.

records.name: Coldfells
records.description: A bleak upland between the Ettenmoors and Angmar, north-east of Rivendell, part of the wild borderland once claimed by Rhudaur. Little inhabited even in Arnor's day, it remains desolate and dangerous through the Third Age, avoided by travellers on the roads below.

records.name: Ettenmoors
records.description: A wild troll-haunted moorland north of Rivendell and the Last Bridge, source of the River Hoarwell, named for the Trolls ('Ettens') that range there. Gandalf and Aragorn both hunt Trolls come down from these moors, and Radagast reports rumours of Nazgûl gathering nearby to Gandalf in T.A. 3018.

records.name: Ettendales
records.description: The valleys within the Ettenmoors where Trolls are said to make their lairs, a deeper and still wilder part of that troll-haunted moorland north-east of Rivendell. Few venture there, and fewer still return with clear report of what dwells within.

records.name: North-South Road
records.description: The great road built by the Númenóreans of Arnor and Gondor by T.A. 2, running from Fornost through Bree, Andrath and the fens of Minhiriath to the bridge at Tharbad and on to Gondor. After the North Kingdom's fall it grew overgrown and was called simply the Greenway, still walked by Bree-folk and the occasional Dúnedain.

records.name: Old South Road
records.description: The southward continuation of the North-South Road beyond Tharbad, running on through Enedwaith and Dunland toward the Fords of Isen. Shown as a broken, dotted track on the oldest maps, it fell into deep disuse after Arnor's fall and Tharbad's ruin left the Two Kingdoms with little cause to travel it.

records.name: Dwarf-road
records.description: An ancient road said to have run from the Dwarf-cities of the Blue Mountains east to Khazad-dûm in the deeps of the Second Age, before the Elves of Eregion built their own paved way from Ost-in-Edhil to Moria's West-gate. Little of its course is remembered by the Third Age.

records.name: Carn Dûm
records.description: The Witch-king's stronghold at the north-western end of the Mountains of Angmar, capital of the realm of Angmar from its founding around T.A. 1300. When the allied host of Gondor, Lindon and Rivendell shattered Angmar's army in T.A. 1975, the Witch-king fled north toward Carn Dûm but was cut off and driven away before reaching it; whether the fortress itself was ever destroyed is not recorded.

chronicle.description: Founded as the seat of the Witch-king's realm of Angmar.
The Witch-king is driven from the field before he can reach the fortress; Angmar falls.

records.name: Mount Gram
records.description: A peak on the borders of Angmar, home in later ages to a settlement of Orcs. Bilbo mentions Gram in his verses on Orc-hunting, and it stands as one of the enduring Orc-holds of Eriador even after Angmar's fall in T.A. 1975.

records.name: Mount Gundabad
records.description: A three-peaked mountain at the northern end of the Misty Mountains, sacred to the Dwarves as the place where Durin the Deathless, eldest of their Fathers, is said to have first awoken. Seized by Orcs after Sauron's assault on Khazad-dûm in S.A. 1697 (the sacking itself is undated), it became their northern stronghold and capital, fought over again in the War of the Dwarves and Orcs and at the Battle of Five Armies.

chronicle.description: Second Sacking of Gundabad during the War of the Dwarves and Orcs.
Orcs of Gundabad march to the Battle of Five Armies.

records.name: Mountains of Angmar
records.description: The northward continuation of the Misty Mountains beyond Mount Gundabad, within whose north-western end Carn Dûm was built. These heights formed the core of the Witch-king's realm and remained an Orc-haunted borderland even after Angmar's overthrow in T.A. 1975.

records.name: Icebay of Forochel
records.description: A great bay of the Northern Sea biting into Forochel, ringed by ice for much of the year and home to the Lossoth, who travel it by sledge and bone skates when it freezes solid. King Arvedui of Arthedain took refuge on its shores after Fornost's fall and drowned in T.A. 1975 when the rescue ship sent for him was crushed by ice.

chronicle.description: Arvedui, sheltered here by the Lossoth, boards an Elven ship that is wrecked in the ice; he and the last two palantíri of the North are lost.

records.name: Cape of Forochel
records.description: The great hook of land curling around the Icebay of Forochel, the chief dwelling-place of the Lossoth even in the depths of winter when much of the bay itself freezes over. A remote and little-known corner of Middle-earth, seldom visited by outsiders.

records.name: Camps of the Lossoth
records.description: The scattered snow-house settlements of the Lossoth, or Snowmen, descendants of the ancient Forodwaith who retreated to Forochel's cold coasts to escape the growing power of Angmar. Skilled with sledges and bone skates, they sheltered and fed King Arvedui in the terrible winter of T.A. 1974–75, for which he rewarded their chief with the ring of Barahir.

chronicle.description: The Lossoth shelter Arvedui and warn him against trusting the sea; he does not heed them.

records.name: Northern Waste
records.description: The desolate frozen lands stretching beyond Forochel and Angmar into the utmost north of Middle-earth, largely unmapped and unvisited by the Free Peoples of the Third Age. In ancient days it held the remnants of the Forodwaith and, further still, the ruins of Melkor's first northern strongholds.

records.name: High Pass
records.description: The chief northern pass over the Misty Mountains above Rivendell, used since ancient days by travellers between Eriador and the Vales of Anduin. Goblin-town lies beneath it, and both Thorin's company in T.A. 2941 and Gandalf's party in T.A. 3018 are waylaid by Orcs while attempting its crossing.

chronicle.description: Thorin's company is captured by Goblins beneath the High Pass.

records.name: Goblin-town
records.description: A vast warren of tunnels and caverns beneath the High Pass, home to a numerous tribe of Orcs ruled in T.A. 2941 by the Great Goblin. Thorin's company is captured here after sheltering in a cave on the pass, and Bilbo, separated from the others, finds the One Ring in its depths and first meets Gollum.

chronicle.description: Thorin's company is captured; Bilbo finds the Ring and escapes via riddles with Gollum.

records.name: Eagles' Eyrie
records.description: The lofty aerie on the eastern face of the Misty Mountains where Gwaihir the Windlord and his people nest, from which the Great Eagles rescue Thorin's company from wolves and Goblins in T.A. 2941 and later carry word and rescue to Gandalf and to the Ring-bearers at other turns of the story.

chronicle.description: The Eagles rescue Thorin's company from Goblins and Wargs below.

records.name: Caradhras
records.description: 'Redhorn', a cruel and malevolent peak of the Misty Mountains above Moria, whose sudden snows and reputedly hostile will drive back the Fellowship of the Ring in T.A. 3019 as they attempt the Redhorn Pass, forcing them to seek the road through Moria instead.

chronicle.description: The Fellowship is turned back by snow and storm attempting to cross Caradhras.

records.name: Celebdil
records.description: 'Silvertine', the middle and highest of the three mountains above Moria's east side, capped in perpetual snow, on whose peak stood Durin's Tower reached by the Endless Stair. Gandalf casts down the Balrog on its summit in T.A. 3019 after ten days of climbing combat, breaking the tower and shattering the mountainside.

chronicle.description: Gandalf slays the Balrog atop Celebdil after a battle up the Endless Stair, destroying Durin's Tower.

records.name: Fanuidhol
records.description: 'Cloudyhead', the easternmost of the three peaks called the Mountains of Moria, its summit generally wreathed in cloud. Together with Caradhras and Celebdil it stands sentinel over the hidden valley of Dimrill Dale and the West-gate of Khazad-dûm below.

records.name: Redhorn Pass
records.description: The high pass over the Misty Mountains between Caradhras and the valley beyond, the more southerly of the two great crossings from Eriador to the Vales of Anduin. Deep, unnatural snow and Caradhras's ill will defeat the Fellowship's attempt to cross it in T.A. 3019, sending them instead beneath the mountains through Moria.

chronicle.description: The Fellowship of the Ring is defeated by snow attempting this crossing.

records.name: Durin's Tower
records.description: An ancient watchtower of the Dwarves crowning the summit of Celebdil, reached from Moria's depths by the Endless Stair. Here in T.A. 3019 Gandalf finally overthrows the Balrog after their long fall and climb, and in the struggle the tower itself is thrown down and the mountainside riven.

chronicle.description: Gandalf casts down the Balrog and the tower is destroyed in the struggle.

records.name: Endless Stair
records.description: A vast spiral stairway of the Dwarves winding up from the lowest reaches of Moria to Durin's Tower on Celebdil's peak, one of the deepest and highest works of Khazad-dûm's builders. Gandalf and the Balrog fight their way up its whole length in T.A. 3019, and its top is broken in their final struggle.

chronicle.description: Gandalf pursues the fleeing Balrog up the entire stair to the mountain-top.

records.name: Moria
records.description: The greatest mansion of the Dwarves, delved by Durin beneath the Misty Mountains. The Balrog killed Durin VI in T.A. 1980 and Náin I in 1981, after which the Dwarves fled. Balin briefly recolonised it in 2989–2994. It is a haunt of Orcs and worse when the Fellowship crosses it in 3019.

chronicle.description: c. Durin the Deathless founds Khazad-dûm.
The Dwarves awaken a Balrog; Durin VI is slain.
Náin I is slain; the surviving Dwarves flee Moria.
Balin leads Dwarves to recolonise Moria.
Balin's colony is destroyed by Orcs.
The Fellowship of the Ring passes through Moria; Gandalf falls fighting the Balrog.

records.name: Doors of Durin
records.description: The magical western entrance to Moria, wrought by Narvi of Khazad-dûm and Celebrimbor of Eregion in the Second Age, opening only to the password 'Mellon' ('friend'). The Fellowship, delayed by the Watcher in the Water before its threshold, enters here in T.A. 3019 after Gandalf solves the riddle of the door.

chronicle.description: Gandalf opens the Doors after realising the password is simply the Elvish word for 'friend'.

records.name: Dimrill Gate
records.description: The eastern entrance of Moria, opening upon Dimrill Dale below the peaks of Celebdil and Fanuidhol. The surviving Fellowship flees out through this gate in grief after Gandalf's fall, and it was here in T.A. 2799 that Dáin Ironfoot slew Azog before the gate to end the Battle of Azanulbizar.

chronicle.description: Dáin Ironfoot slays the Orc Azog before the gate, ending the Battle of Azanulbizar.
The Fellowship escapes Moria through this gate after Gandalf's fall.

records.name: Dimrill Dale
records.description: The great valley below Moria's East-gate, holding Mirrormere and watered by the Silverlode, called Azanulbizar by the Dwarves. Here in T.A. 2799 the Dwarves of Durin's line under Dáin Ironfoot won a costly victory over Azog's Orcs, ending the War of the Dwarves and Orcs, though the Balrog within Moria kept them from reclaiming the halls.

chronicle.description: Battle of Azanulbizar: the Dwarves defeat the Orcs of Moria but cannot retake the mansion.

records.name: Mirrormere
records.description: A still, dark lake in Dimrill Dale beneath the eastern face of the Misty Mountains, in whose black waters, it is said, a crown of stars can be seen reflected even by day — the vision Durin the Deathless beheld when he first looked into it and so chose the site of Khazad-dûm.

records.name: Durin's Stone
records.description: A worn, rune-carved standing stone beside Mirrormere marking the spot where Durin the Deathless first gazed into the lake's black waters and beheld the Crown of Durin reflected among the stars, and so was moved to found Khazad-dûm. The Fellowship pauses here in T.A. 3019 as Gimli sings of Durin's Day.

chronicle.description: Gimli recites the lay of Durin's Day beside the stone.

records.name: Sirannon
records.description: The 'Gate-stream' that once ran down from the mountains past Moria's West-gate to join the Glanduin, along whose course the Elves of Eregion built a road up to the Doors of Durin. By T.A. 3019 the stream has been dammed by some evil dweller in the pool before the gate, and its bed lies dry along the old road.

records.name: Stair Falls
records.description: A cascade where the Sirannon once tumbled down over broken stairs cut by the Elves of Eregion, on the road up to the Hollin Gate and Moria's West-gate. By the time the Fellowship passes in T.A. 3019 the falls run dry, the stream's water having been diverted into the pool below the Doors by the Watcher.

records.name: Hollin Gate
records.description: The gap in the hills of Hollin through which the ancient Elven road from Ost-in-Edhil climbed to Moria's West-gate. The Fellowship follows the dry course of the Sirannon up through this gate in T.A. 3019, finding the ruined stair and the pool before the Doors of Durin beyond it.

records.name: Watcher's Pool
records.description: A dark, dammed pool of black water lying before the Doors of Durin, formed when some creature blocked the Sirannon's course. Home to the tentacled Watcher in the Water, which drags Frodo under and then seals the Doors behind the fleeing Fellowship as they enter Moria in T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: The Watcher in the Water attacks Frodo and seals the Fellowship into Moria.

records.name: Chamber of Mazarbul
records.description: The Chamber of Records deep in Moria, on the seventh level near the First Hall, where the Dwarves kept their books and Balin's colonists made their last stand. The Fellowship finds Balin's tomb here in T.A. 3019 along with the ruined Book of Mazarbul, moments before Orcs and a cave-troll attack.

chronicle.description: Balin's colony makes its last stand here against Orcs; the Book of Mazarbul is left unfinished.
The Fellowship reads the Book of Mazarbul and is attacked by Orcs and a cave-troll.

records.name: Balin's Tomb
records.description: A white marble tomb in the Chamber of Mazarbul bearing a runic inscription naming Balin, Lord of Moria, son of Fundin, of Durin's Folk. Gandalf reads its epitaph aloud to the Fellowship in T.A. 3019, confirming the fate of Balin's ill-starred colony moments before Orcs assault the chamber.

chronicle.description: Balin is entombed here after being slain by an Orc-arrow at the Mirrormere's edge.

records.name: Second Hall of Old Moria
records.description: A vast pillared hall of Moria that the Fellowship crosses fleeing the Chamber of Mazarbul, its roof lost in shadow above ranks of carved pillars 'like the trunks of great trees'. Beyond it lie the passages leading down toward the First Hall and the Bridge of Khazad-dûm.

chronicle.description: The Fellowship flees through this hall pursued by Orcs and the Balrog.

records.name: Bridge of Khazad-dûm
records.description: A narrow bridge of stone spanning a deep chasm in Moria's First Hall, crossable only single-file. Here in T.A. 3019 Gandalf the Grey confronts the Balrog of Morgoth, breaking the bridge beneath it with his staff — but the Balrog's whip drags him down into the abyss as well.

chronicle.description: Gandalf duels the Balrog on the bridge and both fall into the chasm below.

records.name: Twenty-first Hall
records.description: A hall of the North-end of Moria, marked on Balin's map as holding a passage to a door out to the Dimrill Dale side of the mountains and a window facing east.
