Gandalf briefly loses his bearings among Moria's many identical crossroads before recalling the way past this hall in T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: Gandalf recalls the route past the Twenty-first Hall after a night lost in the dark.

records.name: Methedras
records.description: The southernmost peak of the Misty Mountains, its name meaning 'Last Peak', overlooking the northern eaves of Fangorn Forest and Nan Curunír beyond. Beyond Methedras the range gives out into the lowlands of the Gap of Rohan, marking the traditional southern limit of the Hithaeglir.

records.name: Ost-in-Edhil
records.description: The Elven-Fortress of the Elves, capital of Eregion, founded c. S.A. 750 by Galadriel and Celeborn near the Sirannon within sight of Moria's West-gate. Here the Gwaith-i-Mírdain under Celebrimbor forged the Rings of Power, deceived by Sauron disguised as Annatar; Sauron's armies stormed and utterly destroyed the city in S.A. 1697.

chronicle.description: c. Celebrimbor completes the Three Rings of the Elves here.
Sauron's armies storm and raze Ost-in-Edhil; Celebrimbor is slain.

records.name: Sack of Ost-in-Edhil
records.description: The climactic assault of the War of the Elves and Sauron, in which Sauron's armies overran Eregion, razed Ost-in-Edhil, slew Celebrimbor and seized the Nine and Seven Rings, though the Three escaped him. It marks the end of Eregion as an Elven realm.

chronicle.description: Ost-in-Edhil falls; Celebrimbor is captured, tortured, and slain.

records.name: Glanduin
records.description: A river rising in the southern Misty Mountains near Dunland and flowing west through the marshes of Swanfleet before joining the Greyflood, marking part of Eregion's southern border in the Second Age. Its lower course spreads into the wide fen called Nîn-in-Eilph.

records.name: Swanfleet
records.description: 'Waters of the Swans', a broad marshland where the Glanduin spreads before joining the Greyflood, once the southern march of Eregion and later a refuge of swans and waterfowl. By the Third Age it lies at the edge of Enedwaith's wild borderland, seldom crossed by travellers.

records.name: Battle of Fornost
records.description: The decisive battle of T.A. 1975 on the plains west of Fornost, in which Eärnur of Gondor, aided by Elves of Lindon under Círdan and Rivendell under Glorfindel, destroyed the army of the Witch-king of Angmar. The victory came too late to save Arthedain, whose last king had already perished, but it ended Angmar forever.

chronicle.description: Eärnur's combined host annihilates Angmar's army; the Witch-king flees the field.

records.name: First Hall of Old Moria
records.description: A great chamber near Moria's East side, in which the chasm crossed by the Bridge of Khazad-dûm lies. The Fellowship passes through it fleeing the Chamber of Mazarbul in T.A. 3019, moments before Gandalf turns at the bridge to face the Balrog alone.

chronicle.description: The Fellowship crosses the First Hall fleeing toward the Bridge of Khazad-dûm.

records.name: Chasm of Moria
records.description: The deep, unplumbed fissure beneath the Bridge of Khazad-dûm in Moria's First Hall, into which Gandalf and the Balrog of Morgoth both fall in T.A. 3019 after the bridge breaks beneath them, plunging into darkness and fire far below the mountain's roots.

chronicle.description: Gandalf and the Balrog fall together into the chasm's depths.

records.name: Battle of Azanulbizar
records.description: The last and greatest battle of the War of the Dwarves and Orcs, fought in T.A. 2799 in Dimrill Dale before Moria's East-gate. Dáin Ironfoot slew Azog and avenged Thrór, but the Dwarves, victorious yet unwilling to face the Balrog within, did not retake Moria; Thorin Oakenshield earned his name 'Oakenshield' here.

chronicle.description: Dáin Ironfoot defeats and slays Azog, ending the war, but Moria is left unclaimed.

records.name: First Sacking of Gundabad
records.description: After Sauron's assault on Khazad-dûm in S.A. 1697, Orcs harried the Dwarves and sacked Gundabad, beginning a long occupation. The exact year of the sacking is not recorded.

records.name: Second Sacking of Gundabad
records.description: A battle of the War of the Dwarves and Orcs, T.A. 2793, in which Durin's Folk under Thrór's kin attempted to retake Mount Gundabad from its Orc-garrison in revenge for Thrór's murder at Moria. Though the mountain changed hands, Orcs eventually reclaimed it as their northern capital.

chronicle.description: Dwarves briefly retake Gundabad during the War of the Dwarves and Orcs.

records.name: Mouths of the Baranduin
records.description: The marshy estuary where the River Baranduin (Brandywine) empties into the Great Sea beside the headland of Eryn Vorn, at the south-western edge of old Cardolan. A wild, seldom-visited coast far south of the Shire the river also waters, shadowed by the last remnant of Minhiriath's ancient forest.

records.name: Great East Road
records.description: The ancient highway running from the Grey Havens eastward across Eriador through the Shire and Bree to Rivendell and beyond over the Misty Mountains, in places called simply 'the Road'. Built in the Elder Days and maintained in part by the Dúnedain, it is the chief artery of travel through Eriador at the end of the Third Age.

records.name: Fall of Rhudaur
records.description: The final overthrow of Dúnedain rule in Rhudaur, c. T.A. 1409, when Angmar's invading host, aided by the evil hill-men who had already seized the kingdom, killed or drove out the last of its Dúnedain population. Rhudaur was never again ruled by the heirs of Isildur.

chronicle.description: The last Dúnedain of Rhudaur are killed or flee west; the land passes wholly under Angmar's shadow.

records.name: Rhovanion
records.description: The wide lands east of the Misty Mountains, called Rhovanion in Sindarin and Wilderland in Westron — essentially the same country under two names. It runs from the Grey Mountains south to the Emyn Muil and east to the River Running, embracing the Vales of Anduin, Mirkwood, Lothlórien, the Iron Hills and the borders of Rhûn.

chronicle.description: The Northmen of Rhovanion are broken by the Wainriders at the Battle of the Plains
Eorl the Young rides from the north to victory at the Field of Celebrant

records.name: Vales of Anduin
records.description: The long valley of the Great River east of the Misty Mountains, stretching from the Carrock and Gladden Fields south toward Lothlórien. Home in the Third Age to the Beornings and Woodmen, and formerly to Stoor-hobbits and the early Éothéod, with Silvan Elves, Northmen and the Dwarves of Khazad-dûm all passing through its meadows over the ages.

records.name: Anduin
records.description: The greatest river of Middle-earth, rising from the Langwell and Greylin below the Grey Mountains and flowing over a thousand miles south to the Bay of Belfalas. It divides Wilderland from the Misty Mountains, skirts Mirkwood and Lothlórien, and marks Gondor's ancient border, gathering the Gladden, Silverlode, Limlight, Entwash and Celduin among its many tributaries.

records.name: Carrock
records.description: A great isolated hill of stone rising from the middle of the Anduin, with steep steps cut into its side, close by Beorn's house. Its name, given by Beorn, simply means 'rock' in his own tongue. Thorin's Company rested here after the Eagles bore them from the Misty Mountains in T.A. 2941, and a ford crosses the river nearby.

chronicle.description: Thorin's Company rests here after escaping the Misty Mountains goblins

records.name: Old Ford
records.description: An ancient crossing of the Anduin near the Carrock, where the Old Forest Road fords the river on its way from the High Pass into Mirkwood. Long watched over by the Beornings, it remained by T.A. 3019 one of the few safe crossings of the Great River in northern Wilderland.

records.name: Beorn's House
records.description: The wooden hall of the skin-changer Beorn, standing amid an enclosure of hives and pastures east of the Carrock. Thorin's Company sheltered here in T.A. 2941 before entering Mirkwood, and Gandalf later returned here bearing news of Sauron's growing power. After Beorn's death his son Grimbeorn ruled here, guarding the Old Ford and the High Pass.

chronicle.description: Beorn shelters Thorin's Company before their journey through Mirkwood

records.name: Beornings
records.description: The land of Beorn's descendants, a hardy people of skin-changers and Men who multiplied greatly and held both banks of the Anduin between the High Pass and the eaves of Mirkwood. By T.A. 3019 they and the Woodmen kept the Old Forest Road and the Old Ford clear of Orcs, and Beornings fought at the Battle of Five Armies.

records.name: Éothéod
records.description: The northern homeland of the Éothéod, a hardy Northman people, lying between the Misty Mountains and the Forest River and reaching south to where the Greylin and Langwell join to form the Anduin. Settled from T.A. 1977, it was abandoned in T.A. 2510 when Eorl the Young led his people south to found Rohan.

chronicle.description: Frumgar leads the Éothéod north to this land
Eorl the Young departs south with the Éothéod to found Rohan

records.name: First Home of the Éothéod
records.description: The land between the Carrock and the Gladden Fields where Marhwini led fleeing Northmen after the disastrous Battle of the Plains in T.A. 1856, giving rise to the people later called the Éothéod. They dwelt here bordering Mirkwood until T.A. 1977, when Frumgar led them further north to new lands by the Grey Mountains.

records.name: Framsburg
records.description: The only fortified stronghold of the Éothéod, raised north of the confluence of the Greylin and Langwell rivers and probably named for Fram, son of Frumgar, who slew the dragon Scatha. It was abandoned around T.A. 2510 when Eorl led the Éothéod south to Calenardhon, and its walls fell into ruin thereafter.

records.name: Langwell
records.description: One of the two head-streams that join to form the River Anduin below the Grey Mountains, flowing down from the north near the western Misty Mountains. Its confluence with the Greylin, just south of Framsburg, marked the true source of the Great River and lay at the heart of the Éothéod's northern homeland.

records.name: Greylin
records.description: The eastern of the two head-streams of the Anduin, rising in the Grey Mountains and flowing down to join the Langwell south of Framsburg. Together the two rivers' union was reckoned the source of the Great River, in country the Éothéod made their home from T.A. 1977 until their migration south to Rohan.

records.name: Gladden Fields
records.description: A wide marshy delta where the Gladden River spreads into the Anduin, thick with golden iris (gladden). Here in T.A. 2 Isildur was slain and the One Ring lost, and here in T.A. 2463 Déagol found it in the riverbed before Sméagol murdered him for it. Stoor-hobbits fished these fens for centuries after.

chronicle.description: The Disaster of the Gladden Fields: Isildur is slain and the One Ring is lost
Déagol finds the One Ring and is murdered by Sméagol

records.name: Gladden River
records.description: A river flowing down from the Misty Mountains through the Vales of Anduin to join the Great River amid the marshy Gladden Fields, for which it is named after the golden iris flowers growing thickly along its lower banks and delta.

records.name: Rhosgobel
records.description: The house of Radagast the Brown, standing at the edge of Mirkwood near the Old Forest Road and the Field of Celebrant. Gandalf sought Radagast's aid here in T.A. 3018 to send word to the Eagles and the White Council of Sauron's growing power and Saruman's treachery.

chronicle.description: Gandalf visits Radagast at Rhosgobel to send word to the Eagles

records.name: Woodmen's Settlements
records.description: Scattered homesteads of the Woodmen, a hardy people who cleared land south of the Old Forest Road near Mirkwood's western eaves. Orcs and wargs raided them for slaves before the Battle of Five Armies; afterward the Woodmen felled trees and rebuilt in safety, and some joined Beorn's folk at Yule.

chronicle.description: Orcs raid the Woodmen, mistaking Thorin's Company for their scouts

records.name: Stoor-holes of the Gladden
records.description: Riverside hobbit-holes dug into the banks of the Gladden Fields by Stoors who returned to Wilderland around T.A. 1356 and became a fisher-folk, boating and swimming on the Anduin. Ruled by a matriarch when Sméagol and Déagol lived there, the dwindling community vanished from history before the War of the Ring.

records.name: Field of Celebrant
records.description: The green plain between the Silverlode and the Limlight, south of Lothlórien, where in April T.A. 2510 the Balchoth and their Orc allies nearly destroyed Gondor's army of Calenardhon until Eorl the Young arrived with the Éothéod's riders and won a great victory, leading to the founding of Rohan.

chronicle.description: Battle of the Field of Celebrant: Eorl the Young's riders save Gondor's army from the Balchoth

records.name: Limlight
records.description: A river flowing down from the Misty Mountains to join the Anduin below Lothlórien, marking the northern boundary of Rohan and the southern edge of the Field of Celebrant and the Wold. No bridge or ford crossed it, leaving the wild land beyond largely unwatched.

records.name: Undeeps
records.description: A pair of great horseshoe bends where the Anduin loops back on itself south of the Wold, shallow enough at times to be forded. The Balchoth and other peoples of the plains crossed the Great River here, making the Undeeps a point Gondor and later Rohan had to watch closely.

records.name: Brown Lands
records.description: A wide expanse of barren, treeless country east of the Anduin between the Wold and the Emyn Muil, once tilled and gardened by the Northmen of Rhovanion before the Wainriders and Balchoth overran and abandoned it. By the Third Age's end it was a dry, dusty waste avoided by travellers on the river.

records.name: The Wold
records.description: The open, grassy northernmost reach of the Eastemnet of Rohan, lying between the Anduin, the Limlight and Fangorn Forest. Sparsely peopled and used mainly for summer grazing, it bordered the Brown Lands and the Undeeps and was patrolled by the Riders of Rohan against incursions from the east.

records.name: Northmen of Rhovanion
records.description: The Edain-descended Men who settled the plains of Rhovanion in the early Third Age, allies and kinsmen of Gondor and forebears of both the Éothéod and the Rohirrim. Their kings, including Vidugavia, farmed and grazed the open country until the Wainriders and Balchoth conquered and scattered them in the 1800s and 1900s of the Third Age.

records.name: Kingdom of Vidugavia
records.description: A realm of the Northmen of Rhovanion under King Vidugavia around T.A. 1250, who styled himself 'King of Rhovanion' and was Gondor's staunch ally against the growing threat from the East. His daughter Vidumavi married Prince Valacar of Gondor, a match whose consequences later sparked Gondor's Kin-strife.

chronicle.description: c. Vidugavia allies with Gondor and weds his daughter Vidumavi to Prince Valacar

records.name: The Plains
records.description: The open grasslands south of Mirkwood where the Northmen of Rhovanion long grazed their herds, until the Wainriders swept over them in T.A. 1856. In the Battle of the Plains that year King Narmacil II of Gondor was slain and his people driven back across the Anduin, ending Gondor's dominion over Rhovanion.

chronicle.description: Battle of the Plains: Narmacil II falls and the Wainriders seize Rhovanion

records.name: Mirkwood
records.description: The vast forest east of the Anduin, once fair Greenwood the Great but darkened after Sauron secretly took Dol Guldur around T.A. 1050, breeding giant spiders, wargs and Orcs within it. Thranduil's Silvan Elves held its northern reaches while the shadow spread from the south. Cleansed after the War of the Ring and renamed Eryn Lasgalen.

chronicle.description: A shadow falls upon the forest and it becomes known as Mirkwood
Bilbo and Thorin's Company cross the forest by the Elf-path
Galadriel drives Sauron from Dol Guldur; the forest is renamed Eryn Lasgalen

records.name: Greenwood the Great
records.description: The ancient name of the great forest later called Mirkwood, in the fair days before Sauron's shadow crept over it around T.A. 1050. Silvan Elves under Oropher dwelt at Amon Lanc in its south, and the wood was full of birdsong and open to travellers, unlike the dark tangle it later became.

records.name: Eryn Lasgalen
records.description: The name given to Mirkwood after its cleansing at the end of the War of the Ring in T.A. 3019, when Galadriel and the White Council cast down Dol Guldur for good. Thranduil kept the northern part, Celeborn took the southern part as East Lórien, and the Woodmen and Beornings held the western marches.

chronicle.description: Mirkwood is renamed Eryn Lasgalen after Dol Guldur's fall

records.name: Forest Gate
records.description: The western entrance of the Elf-path into northern Mirkwood, framed by two great trees. Thorin's Company entered here in T.A. 2941 after Beorn warned them to stay on the path. The Old Forest Road lay farther south.

chronicle.description: Thorin's Company enters Mirkwood here

records.name: Old Forest Road
records.description: The ancient Dwarf-road across Mirkwood, south of the Elf-path. By T.A. 2941 its eastern reaches were unsafe and disused; Beorn directed Thorin's Company to the northern path instead. Bombur's fall into the Enchanted River occurred on that northern journey.

records.name: Elf-path
records.description: A narrow path through northern Mirkwood from the Forest Gate toward the Elvenking's Halls. Thorin's Company followed it in T.A. 2941, crossing the Enchanted River in a small boat before later straying toward the Wood-elves' feasts. Its course on this map is reconstructed.

records.name: Enchanted River
records.description: A black, swift stream flowing down from the Mountains of Mirkwood to the Forest River, its waters bearing a spell of drowsiness and forgetfulness. Bombur fell in crossing it with Thorin's Company in T.A. 2941 and slept for weeks, dreaming of Elvish feasts, before being carried on by his companions.

chronicle.description: Bombur falls asleep after touching the river's water

records.name: Mountains of Mirkwood
records.description: A range running some 100 miles east-west across north-eastern Mirkwood, between the Old Forest Road and the Forest River, renamed 'Mountains under Night' after Sauron's shadow spread through the forest around T.A. 1000. The Silvan Elves withdrew here and further north-east to escape the growing darkness spreading from Dol Guldur.

records.name: Emyn Duir
records.description: The earlier name of the range later called the Mountains of Mirkwood, given for the dense dark fir-forest on its slopes rather than any evil reputation. Oropher and his Silvan folk withdrew here from Amon Lanc as Sauron's power began to trouble them, before the range took on its darker later name.

records.name: Thranduil's Halls
records.description: A vast cave-palace carved into a hill above the Forest River, seat of Thranduil, Elvenking of the Wood-elves, with feasting halls, dungeons and cellars for wine floated up from Dorwinion. Thorin's Company was imprisoned here in T.A. 2941 until Bilbo freed them through the water-gate hidden in empty barrels.

chronicle.description: Thorin's Company is imprisoned here, then escapes hidden in empty wine-barrels
Gollum is held prisoner here and later escapes

records.name: River-gate of the Elvenking's Halls
records.description: A guarded water-gate beneath Thranduil's halls, through which empty wine-barrels from Dorwinion were flushed out into the Forest River to be rafted back to Esgaroth. In T.A. 2941 Bilbo Baggins used it to smuggle Thorin's Company out of captivity, hidden inside the returning barrels, while the drunken guards slept.

chronicle.description: Bilbo smuggles Thorin's Company out through this gate in empty barrels

records.name: Woodland Realm
records.description: The kingdom of the Silvan Elves in northern Mirkwood, ruled first by Oropher and then by his son Thranduil from halls beside the Forest River. Its people warred against Sauron's forces from Dol Guldur for centuries and fought at both the Battle of Five Armies and the final Battle of Dol Guldur in T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: Oropher falls leading his people at the Battle of Dagorlad
Thranduil's forces fight in the Battle of Five Armies

records.name: Forest River
records.description: A river rising in the Mountains of Mirkwood and flowing past the Elvenking's halls east to the Long Lake, spreading into the Long Marshes near its mouth. Wood-elves floated empty wine-casks down it to Lake-town, and in T.A. 2941 Thorin's Company escaped Thranduil's halls hidden inside the returning barrels.

records.name: East Bight
records.description: A great square indentation, some 50 miles across, cut into Mirkwood's south-eastern edge where Northmen felled the trees for homes and farmland in earlier centuries. Later overrun by the Wainriders, who displaced its settlers, it remained open, treeless country bordering the Narrows of the Forest by the Third Age's end.

records.name: Narrows of the Forest
records.description: The waist of Mirkwood in the south, where the forest narrows to less than 100 miles across between the East Bight and the western eaves near Dol Guldur. Travellers crossing between Rhovanion's plains and the Vales of Anduin often skirted this narrower stretch rather than the deep forest further north.

records.name: Dol Guldur
records.description: A fortress on a wooded hill in southern Mirkwood where Sauron, disguised as 'the Necromancer', secretly dwelt from around T.A. 1050, breeding evil into the forest. The White Council drove him out in T.A. 2941, but he had already prepared to return openly to Mordor; Galadriel and Celeborn finally cast down its walls in T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: Sauron secretly takes up residence, disguised as the Necromancer
The White Council assaults Dol Guldur and drives Sauron out
Galadriel and Celeborn finally cast down Dol Guldur

records.name: Amon Lanc
records.description: The highest hill of the highlands in south-western Greenwood, home to Oropher's Silvan Elves until he abandoned it, troubled by Sauron's rising power, and led his people north. About a thousand years later Sauron himself took the abandoned hill and raised Dol Guldur upon it.

records.name: Spiders' Colony
records.description: A reconstructed location off the Elf-path in eastern Mirkwood, beyond the Enchanted River, where giant spiders captured Thorin's companions in T.A. 2941. Bilbo fought the spiders and named his sword Sting while rescuing the Dwarves.

chronicle.description: Bilbo battles the spiders and frees Thorin's Company

records.name: Long Marshes
records.description: A region of pools and islets straddling the lower Forest River as it nears the Long Lake, grown much wider by floods and earthquakes by T.A. 2941. The river's main channel remained the only safe passage through the marshes, which claimed many travellers and horses who strayed from it.

records.name: Erebor
records.description: A great isolated peak on Mirkwood's eastern edge, delved by Durin's Folk from T.A. 1999 into the Kingdom under the Mountain. Smaug the dragon seized it in T.A. 2770; Bilbo and Thorin's Company reclaimed it in T.A. 2941 after the dragon's death and the Battle of Five Armies, and it remained a Dwarf-kingdom into the Fourth Age.

chronicle.description: Thráin I founds the Kingdom under the Mountain
Smaug sacks Erebor and Dale
Smaug is slain and the mountain is reclaimed after the Battle of Five Armies

records.name: Kingdom under the Mountain
records.description: The Dwarf-kingdom of Durin's Folk within Erebor, founded by Thráin I in T.A. 1999 after he found the Arkenstone. It grew wealthy through mining and trade with Dale until Smaug destroyed it in T.A. 2770; Dáin II Ironfoot restored it in T.A. 2941, and his son Thorin III Stonehelm ruled after Dáin fell defending Dale in T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: King Dáin I is slain by a cold-drake, prompting Thrór to move the throne to Erebor
King Dáin II Ironfoot falls defending Dale and Erebor against Easterlings

records.name: Front Gate
records.description: The main entrance to Erebor, opening south onto the valley shared with Dale, wide enough for wagons and once guarded night and day by the Dwarves. Smaug used it as his own door after seizing the mountain, and it was sealed by fallen rock during his final battle with Bard over Lake-town.

records.name: The Secret Door
records.description: A hidden door on Erebor's western slope, known only to Thráin II and marked on Thrór's map, opening into a passage leading down to the Dwarves' halls. Bilbo Baggins used it in T.A. 2941 to enter the mountain unseen, speak with Smaug, and later to steal the Arkenstone.

chronicle.description: Bilbo enters Erebor through this door and converses with Smaug

records.name: Ravenhill
records.description: A rocky spur of Erebor overlooking Dale, home to the wise talking ravens who befriended the Dwarves and brought Roäc's news to Thorin's Company. It was one of two spurs held by the allied forces during the Battle of Five Armies in T.A. 2941, and an old watch-post stood upon it.

chronicle.description: Allied forces hold this spur during the Battle of Five Armies

records.name: Dale
records.description: A town of Men in the valley below Erebor's Front Gate, grown prosperous as Dwarves reopened the mountain and its markets flourished on trade in metalwork and Long Lake produce. Smaug destroyed it alongside Erebor in T.A. 2770, killing Lord Girion; Bard, his descendant, rebuilt it as King of Dale after T.A. 2941.

chronicle.description: Smaug destroys Dale, killing Lord Girion
Bard rebuilds Dale and becomes its King

records.name: Kingdom of Dale
records.description: The realm of the Bardings, refounded by Bard the Bowman three years after he slew Smaug in T.A. 2941, in close alliance with the restored Kingdom under the Mountain. Under Bard's grandson Brand its borders reached south and east toward the Carnen, until Brand fell defending Dale against Easterlings during the War of the Ring.

chronicle.description: King Brand falls defending Dale against an army of Easterlings

records.name: Long Lake
records.description: A great lake fed by the Forest River and drained by the River Running, south of Erebor. Esgaroth stood on stilts in its waters. In T.A. 2941 Bard shot Smaug with the Black Arrow while defending the burning town; the dragon fell into the lake.

chronicle.description: Bard slays Smaug over the lake with the Black Arrow

records.name: Esgaroth
records.description: A town of Men built on great piles driven into the Long Lake, connected to shore by a single bridge, ruled by an elected Master. Thorin's Company was welcomed here in T.A. 2941 before assaulting Erebor; Smaug burned much of the town in retaliation before Bard slew him, and it was later rebuilt.

chronicle.description: Smaug destroys much of the town before being slain by Bard

records.name: Celduin
records.description: A river flowing from the Long Lake south-east to the Sea of Rhûn, forming much of the eastern border of Dale's realm and receiving the Carnen from the Iron Hills. Long used as a trade route between Esgaroth, Dale and the wine-country of Dorwinion beyond its mouth.

records.name: Desolation of Smaug
records.description: The blackened, barren waste around Erebor and Dale left by Smaug's fiery rampage in T.A. 2770, where nothing grew but broken, charred stumps for over a hundred years. After the dragon's death in T.A. 2941 the land slowly recovered, showing grass, birds and blossom again by the time Dale was rebuilt.

records.name: Battle of Five Armies
records.description: Fought in the valley of Dale below Erebor's Front Gate in late autumn T.A. 2941, when armies of Dwarves, Elves and Men, arrayed on two spurs of the mountain, were nearly overwhelmed by a host of Orcs and Wargs from the Misty Mountains until Beorn and the Eagles turned the tide. Thorin Oakenshield died of his wounds.

chronicle.description: Dwarves, Men and Elves defeat an Orc army; Thorin Oakenshield is mortally wounded

records.name: Battle of Dale
records.description: In March T.A. 3019, Easterlings crossed the Carnen and drove Brand back to Dale. After days of fighting, Brand and Dáin II fell on 17 March; the survivors took refuge in Erebor. On 27 March, after Sauron's fall, Bard II and Thorin III broke the siege.

chronicle.description: 17 March: Brand and Dáin II fall. On 27 March, Bard II and Thorin III break the siege.

records.name: Grey Mountains
records.description: A long, cold range north of Mirkwood and the Iron Hills, colonised by Durin's Folk after the fall of Moria but abandoned around T.A. 2589-2590 when cold-drakes bred in the Withered Heath slew King Dáin I and drove the Dwarves out to Erebor and the Iron Hills. Orcs later infested its caves.

chronicle.description: King Dáin I is slain by a cold-drake at his own door

records.name: Withered Heath
records.description: A blasted, barren valley in the eastern Grey Mountains where dragons bred for centuries, their fire scorching the land beyond recovery. Smaug himself was hatched here before growing great enough to fly south and seize Erebor in T.A. 2770, and lesser cold-drakes from the Heath harried Durin's Folk for generations.

records.name: Scatha's Lair
records.description: The stinking den of Scatha the cold-drake somewhere in the Grey Mountains, heaped with a vast hoard of Dwarf- and Man-wrought treasure and grim trophies of his victims. Fram, son of Frumgar of the Éothéod, slew Scatha here and won his hoard, later sending the Dwarves who claimed it a necklace of the dragon's teeth in mockery.

chronicle.description: c. Fram slays Scatha and wins his hoard

records.name: Dwarf-delvings of the Grey Mountains
records.description: Halls and mines founded by Durin's Folk who fled Moria after T.A. 1981, growing rich for a time until dragons bred in the nearby Withered Heath began preying on them. King Dáin I was killed at his own door by a cold-drake in T.A. 2589, and within a year his son Grór led survivors to found a new lordship in the Iron Hills.

chronicle.description: Dáin I is slain, prompting the Dwarves' exodus to Erebor and the Iron Hills

records.name: Iron Hills
records.description: A range rich in iron ore north-east of Erebor, settled by Grór and his followers in T.A. 2590 after leaving the Grey Mountains. Its Dwarves, led by Dáin II Ironfoot, marched to Erebor's aid at the Battle of Five Armies in T.A. 2941, after which Dáin became King under the Mountain and the Iron Hills' importance waned.

chronicle.description: Grór founds a Dwarf-lordship in the Iron Hills
Dáin Ironfoot marches from the Iron Hills to the Battle of Five Armies

records.name: Halls of the Iron Hills
records.description: The stronghold of the Lords of the Iron Hills, delved by Grór after T.A. 2590 and later home to Dáin II Ironfoot before he became King under the Mountain in T.A. 2941. From here Dáin answered Thorin Oakenshield's summons with five hundred armoured Dwarves, arriving just in time for the Battle of Five Armies.

records.name: Carnen
records.description: A river flowing south from the Iron Hills to join the Celduin, its name meaning 'Redwater' for the iron-red stain of the ore-rich hills it drains. It formed part of the eastern marches of the Kingdom of Dale under King Brand, and Easterlings crossed it to besiege Dale in T.A. 3019.

records.name: Dorwinion
records.description: A land of Men on the western shores of the Sea of Rhûn, famed throughout Wilderland for its strong red wine, shipped up the Celduin to Thranduil's halls and Esgaroth. Little else is recorded of its people or history, though its wine features in the song of the barrel-escape from Mirkwood.

records.name: Sea of Rhûn
records.description: A great inland sea in the east of Wilderland, fed by the Celduin and Carnen, with the vine-lands of Dorwinion on its western shore and the wide country of Rhûn stretching away east and south of it. Little is told in any surviving account of what lies along its farther shores.

records.name: Rhûn
records.description: The broad eastern lands beyond the Sea of Rhûn, home to many peoples of Men loosely called Easterlings, largely unknown to the West. From here came the Wainriders and Balchoth who invaded Rhovanion and Gondor in earlier centuries, and Easterling hosts who marched to Sauron's banner in the War of the Ring.

records.name: Easterlings
records.description: The general name given by Gondor to the many Mannish peoples dwelling in and beyond Rhûn, most of whom fell under Sauron's sway across the ages. Successive Easterling nations, including the Wainriders and Balchoth, warred against Gondor and Rhovanion's Northmen, and their descendants fought at the Pelennor Fields and at Dale in T.A. 3019.

records.name: Wainriders
records.description: A confederacy of Men from the lands east and around Rhûn who fought from great wains, or wagons. They invaded Rhovanion and Gondor from T.A. 1851, killing King Narmacil II at the Battle of the Plains in 1856 and King Ondoher in 1944, before Gondor's general Éarnil ambushed and broke their power near the Dead Marshes.

chronicle.description: Battle of the Plains: the Wainriders kill King Narmacil II
The Wainriders are routed by Éarnil after killing King Ondoher

records.name: Balchoth
records.description: A fierce people from east of the Sea of Rhûn who migrated into the plains between Mirkwood and the River Running, growing strong on plunder and Sauron's secret aid. In T.A. 2510 they invaded Calenardhon with Orc allies and nearly destroyed Gondor's army, until Eorl the Young's Éothéod turned the battle at the Field of Celebrant.

chronicle.description: The Balchoth are destroyed at the Battle of the Field of Celebrant

records.name: Lothlórien
records.description: The hidden Elven realm between the Celebrant and the Anduin, ruled by Celeborn and Galadriel from Caras Galadhon beneath golden-leaved mallorn trees, protected by Galadriel's power from Sauron's sight. The Fellowship rested and was gifted here in T.A. 3019 after Gandalf's fall in Moria, before its passing overseas in the Fourth Age.

chronicle.description: The Fellowship of the Ring rests here after the loss of Gandalf in Moria

records.name: Caras Galadhon
records.description: The chief city of Lothlórien, built in the branches of great mallorn trees within a double ring of walls and ditches, seat of Celeborn and Galadriel. Here Frodo looked into the Mirror of Galadriel and the Fellowship received gifts before departing down the Anduin in February T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: Frodo and Sam look into the Mirror of Galadriel

records.name: Cerin Amroth
records.description: A great mound crowned with white niphredil and golden elanor flowers within two rings of trees, the ancient heart of Lothlórien where Amroth once dwelt. Here Aragorn and Arwen plighted their troth in T.A. 2980, and here the Fellowship rested in T.A. 3019 while Frodo felt the fabric of time itself.

chronicle.description: Aragorn and Arwen become betrothed here
The Fellowship rests here on their way to Caras Galadhon

records.name: Nimrodel
records.description: A clear, cold stream falling from the Misty Mountains' eastern slopes to join the Silverlode near Lothlórien's western border, named for the Elf-maid Nimrodel who once dwelt beside it and was lost fleeing south before the fall of Eregion. Its waters were said to ease sorrow and bring forgetting of care.

records.name: Falls of Nimrodel
records.description: The point where the Nimrodel tumbles down from the hills into the plain at Lothlórien's western eaves, a favourite resting place of travellers of old. The Fellowship of the Ring bathed and rested here in January T.A. 3019 before crossing the Silverlode into the Golden Wood.

chronicle.description: The Fellowship rests here before entering Lothlórien

records.name: Silverlode
records.description: A swift river flowing from Mirrormere in the Misty Mountains through Lothlórien to join the Anduin, giving the Field of Celebrant its name. The Fellowship crossed it on ropes near the Nimrodel's mouth to enter the Naith of Lórien, and later floated down it into the Great River in Elven boats.

records.name: Egladil
records.description: The most densely settled part of Lothlórien, the wedge of land between the Silverlode and the Anduin containing Caras Galadhon itself. Its Sindarin name means 'Elven-point'. Here on 16 February T.A. 3019 the Fellowship held its parting feast before Celeborn's boats bore them away down the Great River.

chronicle.description: The Fellowship's parting feast is held here before leaving Lothlórien

records.name: The Tongue
records.description: The narrow spear-shaped tip of Egladil where the Silverlode's bright waters meet the darker flood of the Anduin, marking the southern point of Lothlórien's angle of land. Elven boats were launched from near here when the Fellowship continued its journey south in T.A. 3019.

records.name: Mirror of Galadriel
records.description: A silver basin fed by a stream from a spring, kept in a secluded hollow garden south of Caras Galadhon, into which Galadriel poured water to show visions of past, present and things that may yet be. Frodo and Sam both looked into it in T.A. 3019, Frodo seeing the Eye of Sauron.

chronicle.description: Frodo and Sam look into the Mirror

records.name: Fangorn Forest
records.description: An ancient, dark forest at the southern feet of the Misty Mountains, all that remained by the Third Age of the great woods that once covered Eriador. Home to Treebeard and the few remaining Ents, it was entered by Merry and Pippin fleeing Orcs in T.A. 3019, sparking the Ents' march on Isengard.

chronicle.description: Merry and Pippin meet Treebeard, leading to the Ents' assault on Isengard

records.name: Wellinghall
records.description: One of Treebeard's homes, set in the flanks of Methedras near the springs of the Entwash. Evergreen trees flank a roofless outer hall, and a stream falls across the entrance of an inner cave. Merry and Pippin stayed here with Treebeard before the Entmoot in T.A. 3019.

position.note: The text places the hall in the flanks of Methedras. The atlas uses that mountain as its anchor; the exact site within the slopes is not established.

chronicle.description: Treebeard shelters Merry and Pippin here

records.name: Treebeard's Hill
records.description: A hill in eastern Fangorn near Wellinghall, one of Treebeard's favourite outlooks over his forest and the plains of Rohan beyond, where he watched the weather and the doings of the wide world below.

records.name: Derndingle
records.description: A great natural hollow ringed by trees in southern Fangorn where the Ents held their solemn moots. Here in T.A. 3019, roused by Merry and Pippin's news of Saruman's treachery, Treebeard summoned the last Ents to an Entmoot that lasted three days and ended in the March on Isengard.

chronicle.description: The Ents hold an Entmoot here and decide to march on Isengard

records.name: Entwash Source
records.description: The springs on Fangorn's southern slopes, near the foot of Methedras, where the River Entwash rises before flowing out across Rohan's plains to the Anduin. Treebeard knew every stream of his forest, including these headwaters close by his own home at Wellinghall.

records.name: Emyn Muil
records.description: A tangled, rocky highland straddling the Anduin south of Nen Hithoel, hard going with sharp ridges on the west bank and a sheer drop to the Dead Marshes on the east. Frodo and Sam wandered lost here for days after leaving the Fellowship in T.A. 3019 until Gollum found and began to guide them.

chronicle.description: Frodo and Sam are found and led by Gollum after wandering lost

records.name: Sarn Gebir
records.description: Dangerous rapids where the Anduin churns between rocky banks north of the Argonath, forcing all river-traffic to portage around them on the western shore. The Fellowship narrowly avoided disaster here in February T.A. 3019 when Orc-arrows forced them to land and carry their boats past the rapids by night.

chronicle.description: The Fellowship portages around the rapids under Orc attack

records.name: North Stair
records.description: A flight of ancient steps cut into the cliffs of Emyn Muil's western edge, part of a lost road that once linked Rohan and Gondor along the Anduin. Aragorn, Legolas and Gimli searched here in T.A. 3019 while tracking the Orcs who had captured Merry and Pippin.

chronicle.description: Aragorn's company searches here for signs of Merry and Pippin

records.name: Argonath
records.description: Two colossal statues of Isildur and Anárion, raised by Rómendacil II around T.A. 1248 to mark ancient Gondor's northern boundary, standing like a gate where the Anduin narrows before Nen Hithoel. The Fellowship passed awestruck between them in February T.A. 3019, on their way to Parth Galen and the breaking of the Fellowship.

chronicle.description: The Fellowship passes between the Pillars of the Kings

records.name: Nen Hithoel
records.description: A calm, misty lake formed where the Anduin widens beyond the Argonath, bounded by the Emyn Muil's East and West Walls of rock and ending at Tol Brandir and the Falls of Rauros. The Fellowship made their last camp together on its western shore at Parth Galen before the company broke apart in T.A. 3019.

records.name: West Wall of Rock
records.description: The cliffs of Emyn Muil forming Nen Hithoel's western shore, broken only at Parth Galen and beneath Amon Hen, where the Fellowship camped and Boromir tried to take the Ring from Frodo in T.A. 3019.

records.name: East Wall of Rock
records.description: The sheer eastern cliffs of Emyn Muil bordering Nen Hithoel, rising below Amon Lhaw opposite the shore where the Fellowship camped. No landing was possible along this shore, forcing all traffic on the lake to the western side.

records.name: Amon Hen
records.description: A hill on Nen Hithoel's western shore crowned with an ancient stone seat built by Gondor's kings, from which one could see for many leagues. Here Frodo, wearing the Ring, glimpsed the Eye of Sauron in T.A. 3019 and chose to leave the Fellowship, while Boromir fell defending Merry and Pippin below.

chronicle.description: Frodo puts on the Ring atop the Seat of Seeing and resolves to go on alone; Boromir dies defending the hobbits nearby

records.name: Amon Lhaw
records.description: A hill on Nen Hithoel's eastern shore, twin to Amon Hen, also crowned with a seat of Gondor's kings from which sounds from far away could be heard. It stood empty and unvisited when the Fellowship passed by on the lake in T.A. 3019.

records.name: Tol Brandir
records.description: A tall, sheer-sided island of rock standing between Amon Hen and Amon Lhaw at the head of the Falls of Rauros, unclimbed and untrodden by any foot save birds. Frodo considered and rejected it as a refuge before deciding to cross the Anduin alone toward Mordor in T.A. 3019.

records.name: Parth Galen
records.description: A green sward on Nen Hithoel's western shore below Amon Hen, where the Fellowship of the Ring made its last camp together on 26 February T.A. 3019. Here Boromir tried to seize the Ring, Frodo fled alone, and Merry and Pippin were captured by Uruk-hai, ending the Fellowship as one company.

chronicle.description: The Fellowship of the Ring is broken here

records.name: Falls of Rauros
records.description: The great cataracts where the Anduin plunges over a sudden cliff south of Tol Brandir in a roar of white spray, audible for miles. Boromir's funeral boat, laid with his weapons, passed over the falls whole in T.A. 3019, sent by Aragorn, Legolas and Gimli in tribute after his death.

chronicle.description: Boromir's funeral boat passes over the falls

records.name: Nindalf
records.description: A wide, flat marshland where the Entwash spreads into countless channels and reed-pools before reaching the Anduin below Emyn Muil. Frodo, Sam and Gollum skirted its edge in T.A. 3019 on their way toward the Dead Marshes and the Morannon, finding it treacherous but less deadly than the marshes beyond.

records.name: Dead Marshes
records.description: A vast, foul fen east of the Emyn Muil that grew up over the battlefield of Dagorlad, its pools showing the ghostly faces of slain Men, Elves and Orcs beneath the water. Gollum led Frodo and Sam through it in T.A. 3019, warning them not to look at the corpse-candles or touch the dead.

chronicle.description: Gollum guides Frodo and Sam through the marshes

records.name: Noman-lands
records.description: A bleak, ash-strewn waste between the Dead Marshes and the Morannon, pitted and scarred by ancient war and Mordor's poisonous industry, where nothing grew and no bird sang. Frodo and Sam crossed its choking desolation with Gollum in T.A. 3019 on the last stage of their approach to the Black Gate.

records.name: Dagorlad
records.description: A wide plain north of the Morannon where the Last Alliance of Elves and Men fought and defeated Sauron's armies in S.A. 3434, in the greatest battle of the Second Age, opening the way to the siege of Barad-dûr. The battlefield's dead sank into the ground and bred the Dead Marshes that later grew over its western edge.

chronicle.description: Battle of Dagorlad: the Last Alliance defeats Sauron's army

records.name: Rohan
records.description: The kingdom of the Rohirrim, horse-lords of the north, granted by Gondor's Steward Cirion to Eorl the Young in T.A. 2510 for his aid at the Field of Celebrant. Bounded by the Misty Mountains, the White Mountains and the Anduin, it is ruled from Edoras and bound to Gondor by the Oath of Eorl.

chronicle.description: Cirion grants Calenardhon to Eorl the Young, founding Rohan.
The Rohirrim ride to the Pelennor Fields and help break the siege of Minas Tirith.

records.name: Calenardhon
records.description: The old northern province of Gondor, thinly settled after plague and war drew its people south and east. Overrun by Balchoth and Orcs in T.A. 2510 until Eorl's Rohirrim relieved it at the Field of Celebrant; Steward Cirion then ceded the land to Eorl's people, who renamed it Rohan.

chronicle.description: Ceded by Cirion to Eorl the Young; renamed Rohan.

records.name: Edoras
records.description: Capital of Rohan since the days of King Brego, built upon a green hill where the White Mountains meet the plain at the mouth of Harrowdale. Crowned by the golden hall of Meduseld, it is the seat of King Théoden and later King Éomer, reached by a long stair and a guarded gate.

chronicle.description: Brego completes Meduseld and moves the capital here from Aldburg.
Gandalf frees Théoden from Wormtongue's counsel in Meduseld.

records.name: Meduseld
records.description: The great hall of the Kings of Rohan atop the hill of Edoras, roofed with gold-hued thatch that gleams from afar. Built by Brego son of Eorl, it houses the throne of the Mark and the mead-benches of the King's household; here Gandalf broke Saruman's hold over Théoden in T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: Built by King Brego.
Gandalf heals Théoden of Wormtongue's poison.

records.name: Aldburg
records.description: A fortified town in the Folde, the first capital of Rohan, founded by Eorl the Young soon after T.A. 2510. When Brego moved the throne to Edoras, Aldburg remained the seat of the Third Marshal of the Mark; Éomund and his son Éomer dwelt here before the War of the Ring.

chronicle.description: c. Founded by Eorl the Young as the first capital of Rohan.

records.name: Dunharrow
records.description: An ancient refuge of the Rohirrim on a great shelf of rock in the White Mountains above Harrowdale, reached by a hairpin road guarded by carved stone Púkel-men. Built by the Men of the Mountains before the Rohirrim came, it served as the muster-point for Théoden's host in T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: Rohan's host musters here before riding to Minas Tirith; Aragorn takes the Paths of the Dead from the Dimholt nearby.

records.name: Firienfeld
records.description: The green mountain field above Dunharrow, a wide upland shelf ringed by standing stones and overshadowed by the Dwimorberg. Here Théoden's tents were pitched before the ride to Minas Tirith, and here Aragorn, Legolas and Gimli said farewell to Éowyn before entering the Paths of the Dead.

chronicle.description: Aragorn's Grey Company camps here before entering the Paths of the Dead.

records.name: Dimholt
records.description: A dark stand of trees at the foot of the Dwimorberg above Firienfeld, held in dread by the Rohirrim as haunted. Within it stands the Door of the Dead, entrance to the Paths of the Dead; the Rohirrim shunned the place, believing the spirits of the Dead Men of Dunharrow still lingered there.

records.name: Dwimorberg
records.description: The 'Haunted Mountain' rising above Dunharrow and the Dimholt, beneath which run the Paths of the Dead. Its name recalls the Rohirrim's dread of the Sleepless Dead said to dwell within; no Rider of the Mark would willingly go near it before Aragorn passed beneath it in T.A. 3019.

records.name: Paths of the Dead
records.description: A haunted road running beneath the White Mountains from the Door of the Dead at the Dimholt to the Stone of Erech in Gondor, home to the Oathbreakers who forsook Isildur. Only Isildur's Heir may lawfully summon them; Aragorn passed this way with the Grey Company in T.A. 3019 to hold the Dead to their broken oath.

chronicle.description: Aragorn leads the Grey Company through the Paths and holds the Dead to their oath.

records.name: Harrowdale
records.description: A deep, steep-walled dale of the White Mountains where the Snowbourn descends toward Edoras, sheltering the villages of Underharrow and Upbourn and giving access to Dunharrow above. Éowyn ruled here in Théoden's absence, and from this valley the Rohirrim rode to war in T.A. 3019.

records.name: Upbourn
records.description: A small village of the Rohirrim in Harrowdale, on the Snowbourn between Edoras and Dunharrow. It lay along the road taken by Théoden's riders as they mustered from Edoras up the dale to the Hold of Dunharrow before the ride to Gondor.

records.name: Underharrow
records.description: A village of Harrowdale hidden in a fold of the valley beneath Dunharrow, passed by Théoden's company on their ride up to the Hold. Like Upbourn, its folk served the muster of Rohan in the War of the Ring.

records.name: Starkhorn
records.description: A great peak of the White Mountains standing above Dunharrow at the head of Harrowdale, its bare stone shoulder overlooking the Hold. Together with Irensaga it frames the valley in which Dunharrow lies, part of the mountain wall dividing Rohan from Gondor.

records.name: Irensaga
records.description: A jagged peak of the White Mountains east of Starkhorn, its saw-toothed ridge giving it the name 'Iron Saw'. Between Irensaga and the Dwimorberg lies the dark ravine leading up to Dunharrow and the Firienfeld.

records.name: Snowbourn
records.description: A river rising in the White Mountains above Dunharrow, flowing down through Harrowdale past Edoras and eastward across the Eastemnet to join the Entwash. Its cold, swift waters give Harrowdale its name and water the fields around Edoras.

records.name: Helm's Deep
records.description: A narrow, high-walled ravine cutting into the White Mountains in the Westfold, named for King Helm Hammerhand who took refuge here in the Long Winter. Guarded by the Hornburg and the Deeping Wall, it withstood Saruman's great assault in T.A. 3019, the Battle of the Hornburg.

chronicle.description: King Helm Hammerhand withstands siege here through the Long Winter.
The Battle of the Hornburg: Théoden's garrison holds against Saruman's army until Gandalf and the Huorns arrive.

records.name: Hornburg
records.description: An ancient fortress of Gondorian build standing on the Hornrock at the mouth of Helm's Deep, later held by the Kings of Rohan. Its horn, said to echo through the Deep, gives it its name; Erkenbrand's men and Théoden's riders defended it against Saruman's army at the Battle of the Hornburg.

chronicle.description: Held by Erkenbrand's men and Théoden's company through Saruman's siege.

records.name: Helm's Dike
records.description: A great trench and rampart, older than Rohan itself, thrown across the mouth of the Deeping-coomb to bar the way to Helm's Deep. In T.A. 3019 it was overrun in the dark by Saruman's host before the defenders fell back to the Hornburg and the Deeping Wall.

chronicle.description: Overrun by Saruman's army on the night of the Battle of the Hornburg.

records.name: Deeping-coomb
records.description: The wide upper valley opening onto Helm's Deep, walled by cliffs and closed at its mouth by Helm's Dike. Through it a road runs from the Hornburg down to the Westfold Vale, and along it Saruman's army advanced under cover of darkness in the Battle of the Hornburg.

records.name: Deeping-stream
records.description: A small stream flowing down the Deeping-coomb from Helm's Deep, past the Hornburg and out into the Westfold Vale toward the Isen. Its course through the ravine is overlooked by the Deeping Wall and the caves of Aglarond.

records.name: Deeping Wall
records.description: A great wall of ancient, smooth-fitted stone joining the Hornburg to the cliffs of the coomb, with a single culvert for the Deeping-stream. In T.A. 3019 it was breached by Saruman's blasting-fire, but the defenders held the breach until Gandalf's return broke the siege.

chronicle.description: Breached by Orthanc-fire during the Battle of the Hornburg.

records.name: Hornrock
records.description: A jutting spur of rock at the mouth of the Deeping-coomb on which the Hornburg is built, thrust out from the cliffs like a ship's bow between the ravine and the Deeping Wall. It gives the fortress its name and commands the approach to Helm's Deep.

records.name: Aglarond
records.description: The Glittering Caves behind Helm's Deep, a labyrinth of jewel-like caverns of many-coloured stone that so moved Gimli after the Battle of the Hornburg that he later led a colony of Dwarves to dwell and delve there, gifting Rohan their craftsmanship in return for the wonder of the caves.

chronicle.description: Gimli discovers the caves after the Battle of the Hornburg and vows to bring Dwarves to settle them.

records.name: Thrihyrne
records.description: A three-peaked mountain of the White Mountains rising above the Westfold near Helm's Deep, its horned summits visible for many miles and giving it its name, Rohirric for 'three horns'. It stands as a landmark over Erkenbrand's country and the approach to the Hornburg.

records.name: Westfold
records.description: The western fold-land of Rohan, between the Isen and the White Mountains, ruled from Helm's Deep by Erkenbrand as its lord in T.A. 3019. Home to the folk who fled to Helm's Deep before Saruman's invasion, and site of Isengard's assault on the Fords of Isen at its western edge.

records.name: Westfold Vale
records.description: The broad vale of the Westfold below Helm's Deep, watered by the Deeping-stream, where the refugees of the Westfold gathered their herds and wains before Saruman's assault. It lies between the mountains and the road running from the Fords of Isen toward Edoras.

chronicle.description: Westfold folk flee here with their goods before Saruman's army, then on to Helm's Deep.

records.name: Eastfold
records.description: The eastern fold-land of Rohan, lying between the Folde and the Mering Stream at Gondor's border, in the shadow of the White Mountains. Its people mustered at Edoras with the rest of the Riddermark for the ride to the Pelennor Fields in T.A. 3019.

records.name: Folde
records.description: A fold-land of central Rohan around Aldburg and Edoras, home ground of the House of Eorl and the mustering land of the Eastmark under the Third Marshal. Éomer's folk and lands lay chiefly within the Folde.

records.name: Westemnet
records.description: The western plain of the Emnet, open grassland of central Rohan between the Westfold and the Entwash, grazed by the great horse-herds of the Rohirrim. Éomer's éored rode here in pursuit of the Uruk-hai bearing Merry and Pippin in T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: Éomer's éored destroys the Isengard Orcs on the Westemnet near Fangorn.

records.name: Eastemnet
records.description: The eastern plain of the Emnet, rolling grassland between the Entwash and the Wold, grazed by Rohan's horse-herds and patrolled by the Riders of the Mark. It borders Fangorn Forest to the north and the Mouths of Entwash to the east.

records.name: Entwash
records.description: A river flowing out of Fangorn Forest south and east across the plains of Rohan, past the ford at Entwade, spreading into the marshes of the Wetwang before it joins the Anduin at the Mouths of Entwash.

records.name: Entwade
records.description: A ford across the Entwash on the road between Edoras and Minas Tirith, where the river runs broad and shallow among reeds and sallows. Travellers between Rohan and Gondor customarily crossed here before continuing east into the Eastemnet and Anórien.

records.name: Mouths of Entwash
records.description: The reedy delta where the Entwash breaks into many channels through the Wetwang before joining the Anduin, close to the Brown Lands and the borders of the Wold. A wild, trackless country of marsh and reed-bed avoided by travellers.

records.name: Fords of Isen
records.description: The chief crossing of the river Isen on the road from Isengard into the Westfold, defended by Rohan against Saruman's forces in two hard-fought battles in T.A. 3019. Prince Théodred died defending the first crossing; the second saw Erkenbrand's men forced back before regrouping at Helm's Deep.

chronicle.description: First Battle of the Fords of Isen (25 February): Prince Théodred is slain.
Second Battle of the Fords of Isen (2 March): Saruman's army forces the crossing.

records.name: Isen
records.description: A river rising below Isengard and flowing south then west through the Gap of Rohan to the Sea, forming the western boundary between Rohan and Enedwaith. Its fords below Isengard were bitterly contested by Saruman's armies and the Rohirrim in T.A. 3019.

records.name: Gap of Rohan
records.description: The wide gap between the southern end of the Misty Mountains and the northern end of the White Mountains, through which the Isen flows and the road runs from Dunland and Isengard into Rohan. A strategic passage fought over during Saruman's war on Rohan.

records.name: Isengard
records.description: A great circular fortress made by the Men of Númenor within the ring of Nan Curunír to guard the Gap of Rohan, later given over to the Wizard Saruman as its keeper. In T.A. 3019 Saruman's industry turned it into an armed camp, until the Ents stormed and flooded it after the Battle of the Hornburg.

chronicle.description: Steward Beren gives the keys of Orthanc and lordship of Isengard to Saruman.
Saruman fortifies Isengard and closes it to all but his own servants.
The Ents storm and flood Isengard, ending Saruman's power there.

records.name: Orthanc
records.description: The unbreakable tower of black stone at the heart of Isengard, made by the Men of Númenor in the Second Age and never taken by force. Saruman made it his stronghold, until Treebeard's Ents penned him within it after the storming of Isengard, and it later held one of the seeing-stones.

chronicle.description: Saruman fortifies Orthanc, shutting himself within Isengard.
Saruman is besieged within Orthanc by the Ents; Gandalf breaks his staff here.

records.name: Nan Curunír
records.description: The valley at the southern end of the Misty Mountains in which Isengard stands, once green and fair, called the Wizard's Vale for Saruman's long dwelling there. By T.A. 3019 Saruman's mines and furnaces had blackened it to a wasteland of pits and slag before the Ents' flood renewed it.

records.name: Dol Baran
records.description: The southernmost hill of the Misty Mountains, bare-topped and heather-clad, about a mile from the road between Isengard and the Fords of Isen. Here Théoden's company camped on the night Pippin stole and looked into Saruman's palantír, drawing the eye of Sauron and a passing Nazgûl.

chronicle.description: Pippin looks into the palantír of Orthanc at the camp below Dol Baran.

records.name: Mering Stream
records.description: A small stream flowing down from the Firien Wood on the White Mountains' northern slopes, marking the ancient boundary between Rohan and Anórien in Gondor. The Great West Road crosses it on the way from Edoras to Minas Tirith.

records.name: Firien Wood
records.description: A dark wood of fir and pine clothing the slopes of the Halifirien on the border between Rohan and Anórien, called Everholt in Rohirric and famed as the haunt of a great boar hunted by King Folca. The Mering Stream rises within it, marking the frontier of the two realms.

chronicle.description: King Folca dies hunting the great boar of Everholt.

records.name: Great West Road
records.description: The ancient highway linking the Grey Havens and the Shire in the west to Minas Tirith in the east, running through Tharbad, the Gap of Rohan and Edoras before crossing the Mering Stream into Anórien. Along its Rohan and Gondor stretch armies, embassies and refugees travelled throughout the Third Age.

records.name: Fenmarch
records.description: A marshy borderland of eastern Rohan near the Mering Stream and the Firien Wood, home to the captain Grimbold, who fought at the Fords of Isen and led the men of the Fenmarch to the Pelennor Fields in T.A. 3019.

records.name: Firien-dale
records.description: A deep cleft separating the hallowed hill of Halifirien from the northward spur of the White Mountains, part of the wooded Firien country on the border of Rohan and Anórien.

records.name: Gondor
records.description: The southern realm of the Dúnedain in exile, founded by Isildur and Anárion at the end of the Second Age, stretching from the Gap of Rohan and the mouths of Anduin to Ithilien. Ruled by the Stewards since the line of Kings failed in T.A. 2050, until Aragorn's return and crowning in T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: Founded by Elendil's sons Isildur and Anárion.
The line of Kings fails with Eärnur; the Stewards rule thereafter.
Aragorn Elessar is crowned King, reuniting Gondor and Arnor.

records.name: Minas Tirith
records.description: The capital of Gondor since Osgiliath's ruin, a seven-tiered white city built into the root of Mount Mindolluin, crowned by the Citadel and the White Tower of Ecthelion. Besieged by the Witch-king's host at the Battle of the Pelennor Fields in T.A. 3019, it was relieved by the Rohirrim and Aragorn's fleet.

chronicle.description: Founded by Anárion as Minas Anor.
Becomes the capital of Gondor after Osgiliath is abandoned.
Besieged and relieved at the Battle of the Pelennor Fields; Aragorn is crowned before its gates.

records.name: White Tower
records.description: The tall white tower atop the Citadel of Minas Tirith, first raised by King Calimehtar and rebuilt by Steward Ecthelion I, whose name it thereafter bore. It holds the great bell and the chamber where the Stewards kept watch, and later the palantír of Minas Tirith.

chronicle.description: c. First built by King Calimehtar.
Rebuilt by Steward Ecthelion I; renamed the Tower of Ecthelion.

records.name: Court of the Fountain
records.description: A paved court before the White Tower in the Citadel of Minas Tirith, where a fountain played beside the dead White Tree, kept in memory of the line of Kings until a new sapling was found. Here Gandalf and Pippin looked out over the city, and here Aragorn later planted the new White Tree.

chronicle.description: Aragorn finds and plants a sapling of the White Tree here after his crowning.

records.name: Rath Dínen
records.description: The silent street of the dead on the sixth level of Minas Tirith, lined with the domed halls of the House of Kings and the House of the Stewards. Closed to the living but for funerals, it was here that Denethor, in madness, tried to burn himself and Faramir alive in T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: Denethor attempts to burn himself and Faramir on a pyre in the House of the Stewards.

records.name: House of the Kings
records.description: The oldest and greatest of the tomb-halls of Rath Dínen in Minas Tirith, holding the sepulchres of the Kings of Gondor from Elendil's line down to Eärnur, the last King before the Stewards' rule. It stands apart from the later House of the Stewards along the Silent Street.

records.name: House of the Stewards
records.description: A domed tomb-hall of Rath Dínen built to house the sepulchres of the Ruling Stewards of Gondor, since none but Kings might lie in the older House of the Kings. Here in T.A. 3019 the mad Denethor laid himself and the fevered Faramir on a pyre, to be burned as the heathen Kings of old, until Gandalf and Beregond broke in and saved Faramir.

chronicle.description: Denethor attempts to burn himself and Faramir alive here; Gandalf and Beregond intervene.

records.name: Houses of Healing
records.description: The healing-houses of Minas Tirith on its sixth circle, set among gardens on the northern side of the city. Here Aragorn used athelas and his king's healing hands to save Faramir, Éowyn and Merry from the Black Breath after the Battle of the Pelennor Fields.

chronicle.description: Aragorn heals Faramir, Éowyn and Merry of the Black Breath.

records.name: Great Gate
records.description: The single great gate of Minas Tirith's outer wall, facing east toward the Pelennor and Osgiliath. Broken by the Witch-king's battering-ram Grond during the siege of T.A. 3019, it was later replaced with new gates of mithril and steel, graven by the Dwarves at Aragorn's command.

chronicle.description: Broken by Grond under the Witch-king's assault.

records.name: Merethrond
records.description: The great Hall of Feasting in Minas Tirith, used for state banquets and celebrations. Here, after the Ring's downfall, Aragorn Elessar and Arwen Undómiel were wed at Midsummer T.A. 3019, uniting the lines of the Dúnedain and the Half-elven.

chronicle.description: Wedding feast of Aragorn and Arwen.

records.name: Fen Hollen
records.description: The 'Closed Door' at the head of Rath Dínen in Minas Tirith, opened only by the Steward, the King, or the keeper of the tombs. Through it Denethor carried Faramir to the House of the Stewards, and through it Gandalf and Pippin burst to prevent Faramir's burning in T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: Gandalf forces the door to stop Denethor's pyre.

records.name: Rath Celerdain
records.description: The Lampwrights' Street on the first circle of Minas Tirith, near the Great Gate, where torches and lamps were made. Pippin lodged nearby at the Old Guesthouse in the care of Beregond and his son Bergil during the siege of T.A. 3019.

records.name: Bridge of Osgiliath
records.description: The great bridge carrying the road across the Anduin at Osgiliath, built in Gondor's glory and broken in later wars. Its ruined piers still divided the city's east and west banks when Faramir's rangers contested the crossing against Sauron's forces in T.A. 3019.

records.name: Mount Mindolluin
records.description: The great mountain of the White Mountains against whose knee Minas Tirith is built, its snow-capped heights holding the hallowed refuge of Meneldil above the city. It was upon its slopes that Aragorn found a sapling of the White Tree in T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: Aragorn finds a sapling of the White Tree on Mindolluin's slopes.

records.name: Pelennor Fields
records.description: The walled farmland encircling Minas Tirith within the Rammas Echor, tilled fields and orchards feeding the city. Here, on 15 March T.A. 3019, was fought the Battle of the Pelennor Fields, the greatest battle of the War of the Ring, where the Witch-king fell and Théoden died.

chronicle.description: Battle of the Pelennor Fields: the Witch-king is slain by Éowyn and Merry; Théoden dies; Aragorn's fleet arrives from the south.

records.name: Rammas Echor
records.description: The long defensive wall built with great labour after Ithilien fell under the Enemy's shadow, encircling the Pelennor Fields to guard Minas Tirith's farmland. Only partly repaired and manned by T.A. 3019, it was broken through in the north by Sauron's forces before the main assault on the city.

chronicle.description: Breached by Sauron's forces before the siege of Minas Tirith.

records.name: Harlond
records.description: The haven of Minas Tirith on the Anduin below the city, where ships from the southern fiefs docked. In T.A. 3019 Aragorn's captured Corsair fleet, bearing the Grey Company and levies from the south, landed here to relieve the siege at the Battle of the Pelennor Fields.

chronicle.description: Aragorn's fleet from Pelargir lands here during the Battle of the Pelennor Fields.

records.name: Causeway Forts
records.description: Twin forts guarding the causeway where the road from Minas Tirith to Osgiliath passes through the Rammas Echor. Held by Boromir and later Faramir's men, they were overrun by the forces of Mordor as Sauron's army advanced onto the Pelennor in T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: Overrun as Faramir's rearguard retreats from Osgiliath.

records.name: Osgiliath
records.description: The ancient capital of Gondor spanning the Anduin, founded by Isildur and Anárion and once graced by the domed Dome of Stars. Ruined in the Kin-strife and depopulated by plague and war, by T.A. 3019 it was a contested ruin held in part by Gondor's rangers under Faramir against Sauron's forces.

chronicle.description: Ruined during the Kin-strife; the Dome of Stars burns and its palantír is lost in the Anduin.
Faramir's rangers are driven from the city by Sauron's advancing army.

records.name: Dome of Stars
records.description: The great domed hall built by King Meneldil at Osgiliath to house the city's palantír, its ceiling wrought to resemble the night sky. Burned during the Kin-strife in T.A. 1437, when the stone was lost in the waters of the Anduin.

chronicle.description: Burned; the Osgiliath palantír lost in the Anduin.

records.name: Cair Andros
records.description: A long, ship-shaped island in the Anduin north of Minas Tirith, fortified to guard the river approach to the city. Captured briefly by forces from Mordor before the Battle of the Pelennor Fields in T.A. 3019, it was retaken soon after by Gondorian and Rohirric forces.

chronicle.description: Taken by Sauron's forces before the siege of Minas Tirith, then retaken.

records.name: Anórien
records.description: The northern fief of Gondor between the White Mountains and the Anduin, called Sunlending, holding Minas Tirith, the beacon-hills and the Drúadan Forest. The Rohirrim rode through it via the Stonewain Valley to reach the Pelennor unseen in T.A. 3019.

records.name: Drúadan Forest
records.description: A remnant of the great forests that once covered Anórien, home to the reclusive Drúedain led by Ghân-buri-Ghân, who guided Théoden's Rohirrim through the hidden Stonewain Valley to bypass Sauron's roadblocks and reach the Pelennor Fields in time for the battle.

chronicle.description: Ghân-buri-Ghân guides the Rohirrim through the forest to the Pelennor Fields.

records.name: Stonewain Valley
records.description: A long, straight valley deep within the Drúadan Forest, holding the overgrown quarry-road once used to haul stone for Gondor's beacon-towers. Forgotten by T.A. 3019, it was revealed to Théoden by Ghân-buri-Ghân, letting the Rohirrim skirt Sauron's roadblocks to reach Minas Tirith.

chronicle.description: Used by the Rohirrim to bypass the blocked Great West Road.

records.name: Grey Wood
records.description: A wood in Anórien between Mindolluin and Amon Dîn, passed by the Rohirrim on their approach to the Pelennor Fields in T.A. 3019. Its boundaries and precise position are reconstructed.

position.note: The wood lies between Amon Din and Mindolluin. The marker identifies the wooded area, not a precisely located boundary or a measured entrance.

records.name: Amon Dîn
records.description: The easternmost of Gondor's seven beacon-hills, nearest to Minas Tirith, its warning-beacon first lit in T.A. 3019 to summon aid from Rohan against Sauron's assault. Pippin watched its flame kindle from the White Tower on the night the beacons were lit.

chronicle.description: First of the beacons to be lit, summoning Rohan to Gondor's aid.

records.name: Eilenach
records.description: The second beacon-hill of Gondor's chain, rising in the Drúadan Forest of Anórien, lit in T.A. 3019 to carry the summons for aid onward from Amon Dîn toward Nardol and the west.

chronicle.description: Lit in the beacon-chain to summon Rohan.

records.name: Nardol
records.description: The third of Gondor's seven beacon-hills, its name meaning 'fire-top', standing in the line running west from Minas Tirith. It was lit in T.A. 3019 as part of the beacon-chain calling Rohan to war.

chronicle.description: Lit in the beacon-chain.

records.name: Erelas
records.description: The fourth of Gondor's seven beacon-hills, standing in the chain of Anórien between Nardol and Min-Rimmon. It was kindled in T.A. 3019 to pass the alarm westward as Sauron's armies marched on Minas Tirith, summoning the Rohirrim to Gondor's aid.

chronicle.description: Lit in the beacon-chain.

records.name: Min-Rimmon
records.description: The fifth of Gondor's beacon-hills, named for the greater peak Rimmon which it echoes, lit in T.A. 3019 to relay the summons for the Rohirrim onward to Calenhad and Halifirien.

chronicle.description: Lit in the beacon-chain.

records.name: Calenhad
records.description: The sixth beacon-hill of Gondor, standing near the border of Anórien and Rohan, lit in T.A. 3019 to carry the warning to the last beacon at Halifirien and thence to Rohan itself.

chronicle.description: Lit in the beacon-chain.

records.name: Halifirien
records.description: The seventh and westernmost of Gondor's beacon-hills, and holiest: Isildur hallowed it as the secret Tomb of Elendil and named it Amon Anwar. Long unbeaconed while the palantíri sufficed, a watch-beacon was raised there after the Rohirrim settled nearby; it stands within the Firien Wood on Rohan's border.

chronicle.description: Isildur hallows the hill as the Tomb of Elendil, naming it Amon Anwar.
Lit as the last of the seven beacons, seen by Rohan's outriders.

records.name: Lossarnach
records.description: A fertile vale of Gondor south of Minas Tirith below the White Mountains, famous for its orchards and flowers, home of Forlong the Fat who led its men to the muster of Gondor in T.A. 3019. Imloth Melui lies within its bounds.

records.name: Imloth Melui
records.description: A vale renowned for its roses in Lossarnach, birthplace of Ioreth, the old wise-woman of the Houses of Healing, who recalled its rose-gardens even amid the horrors of the War of the Ring.

records.name: Lebennin
records.description: A fief of southern Gondor between the White Mountains and the sea, watered by its five rivers Erui, Sirith, Celos, Serni and Gilrain, and home to the port of Pelargir. Its men mustered for the defence of Minas Tirith in T.A. 3019.

records.name: Erui
records.description: The easternmost of the five rivers of Lebennin, flowing from the White Mountains to the Anduin near Pelargir. Its crossing on the ancient road to Pelargir was the site of the Battle of the Crossings of Erui in T.A. 1447, the climax of the Kin-strife.

chronicle.description: Battle of the Crossings of Erui: King Eldacar slays the usurper Castamir.

records.name: Crossings of Erui
records.description: A ford where the road from Minas Tirith to Pelargir crosses the river Erui, some fifty miles south of the city. Here in T.A. 1447 King Eldacar, returned from exile among the Northmen, defeated and slew the usurper Castamir, ending the Kin-strife.

chronicle.description: Eldacar defeats and kills Castamir, ending the Kin-strife.

records.name: Sirith
records.description: One of the five rivers of Lebennin, rising in the White Mountains and flowing south past the Celos to join the sea near the Ethir Anduin, watering the fields of southern Gondor.

records.name: Celos
records.description: One of the five rivers of Lebennin, flowing from the White Mountains between the Sirith and the Serni down to the sea. A lesser-known stream of Gondor's southern farmland, it is named among the rivers that Faramir's fief was said to hold.

records.name: Serni
records.description: One of the five rivers of Lebennin, flowing south from the White Mountains between the Celos and the Gilrain, joining the sea near the wide mouths of the Anduin at Ethir Anduin.

records.name: Gilrain
records.description: The westernmost of the five rivers of Lebennin, rising near Lamedon and flowing south past Linhir, where it is joined by the Ringló, to reach the sea in the Bay of Belfalas.

records.name: Pelargir
records.description: A great port city founded by Númenórean mariners even before the Downfall, later Gondor's chief haven on the Anduin. Held partly by Umbar's Corsairs before T.A. 3019, it was retaken by Aragorn and the Army of the Dead, whose captured fleet then relieved the siege of Minas Tirith.

chronicle.description: Founded by Númenórean mariners.
Aragorn and the Army of the Dead capture the Corsair fleet here, then sail to relieve Minas Tirith.

records.name: Ethir Anduin
records.description: The broad delta where the Anduin meets the Bay of Belfalas, a maze of channels, marshes and the island of Tolfalas, guarded from Umbar's Corsairs by the ships of Pelargir and Dol Amroth.

records.name: Tolfalas
records.description: An island lying in the Bay of Belfalas at the mouth of the Anduin, the southernmost point of Gondor proper, sparsely peopled and often threatened by raids from Umbar's Corsairs.

records.name: Linhir
records.description: A town of southern Gondor on the borders of Lebennin and Lamedon, built where the Gilrain is joined by the Ringló. Its men, alongside those of Lamedon, mustered late to the defence of Minas Tirith after a Corsair raid delayed them in T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: Its levies are delayed by a Corsair raid before marching to the Pelennor.

records.name: Lamedon
records.description: A hill-region of southern Gondor along the river Ciril, between Morthond and Lebennin, whose folk of Calembel and Ethring rode to war beside Aragorn's Grey Company as it swept up the Corsairs' rear in T.A. 3019.

records.name: Calembel
records.description: The chief town of Lamedon, standing above the river Ciril near the Hill of Erech. Here in T.A. 3019 the folk of the region, terrified of the Oathbreakers, fled from their houses as Aragorn led the Dead Men past on his march to Pelargir.

chronicle.description: Aragorn's Grey Company and the Dead Men pass by, causing the townsfolk to flee.

records.name: Ciril
records.description: A river of Lamedon flowing past Calembel down to join the Ringló, one of the streams that Aragorn's host crossed on the ride from the Stone of Erech to Pelargir in T.A. 3019.

records.name: Ringló
