records.description: A river of southern Gondor flowing down from the Ringló Vale past Ethring to join the Gilrain near Linhir, watering the fief of Ringló Vale in the hills above Lamedon before the combined waters reach the Bay of Belfalas.

records.name: Ringló Vale
records.description: A fief of Gondor in the hills of the upper Ringló, whose men, led by Dervorin son of the Lord of Ringló Vale, marched to the muster of Gondor before the siege of Minas Tirith in T.A. 3019.

records.name: Ethring
records.description: A village of Lamedon on the river Ringló, where the road from Linhir crosses toward Calembel. Aragorn's host passed near it in the swift ride from the Stone of Erech toward Pelargir in T.A. 3019.

records.name: Tarnost
records.description: A place in southern Gondor named on Tolkien's later maps, set between the Gilrain and Dol Amroth near a crossing of the Ringló; scholars have suggested it may be an earlier name for Ethring. It appears only in Tolkien's posthumously published notes and maps, not in the text of The Lord of the Rings.

records.name: Morthond
records.description: The 'Blackroot' river, rising in a cave below the Hill of Erech in the White Mountains and flowing south through its namesake vale to the sea near Edhellond, giving its name to the fief of the Morthond Vale.

records.name: Morthond Vale
records.description: The long vale of the river Morthond in the White Mountains, a fief of Gondor whose lord Duinhir led its bowmen and his sons Duilin and Derufin to the defence of Minas Tirith in T.A. 3019, where the brothers fell before the Great Gate.

chronicle.description: Duilin and Derufin of the Morthond Vale die in the Battle of the Pelennor Fields.

records.name: Stone of Erech
records.description: A great black stone, said to have fallen from the sky, set by Isildur atop the Hill of Erech at the head of the Morthond Vale. Here the King of the Mountains swore his broken oath to Isildur; here Aragorn summoned the Dead Men of Dunharrow to fulfil it at last in T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: Aragorn calls the Oathbreakers to the Stone and holds them to their ancient oath.

records.name: Belfalas
records.description: The coastal fief of southern Gondor along the Bay of Belfalas, seat of the Princes of Dol Amroth, renowned for its seafaring and its part-Elvish nobility descended from the mariners of Edhellond.

records.name: Dol Amroth
records.description: The chief city of Belfalas, seat of its Princes who claim descent from the Elves of Edhellond, on a headland above the Bay of Belfalas. Prince Imrahil led its swan-knights to the defence of Minas Tirith in T.A. 3019, distinguishing himself in the Battle of the Pelennor Fields.

chronicle.description: Imrahil's knights ride to relieve Minas Tirith and fight on the Pelennor.

records.name: Edhellond
records.description: A haven of the Grey-elves and Noldor built in the bay of Cobas Haven near Dol Amroth, whence Elves sailed west in the later Third Age. Long fallen into disuse by T.A. 3019, it left its memory in the part-Elvish blood claimed by the Princes of Dol Amroth.

records.name: Cobas Haven
records.description: The sheltered inlet of the Bay of Belfalas near Dol Amroth in which the Elven haven of Edhellond was built. Its quiet waters once saw the ships of the Eldar depart Middle-earth westward in the later Third Age.

records.name: Bay of Belfalas
records.description: The great bay of the southern coast of Gondor, into which the Anduin empties at the Ethir, bounded by the Andrast headland in the west and stretching toward Umbar and Near Harad in the south.

records.name: Pinnath Gelin
records.description: A range of green hills in western Gondor between Anfalas and Belfalas, thinly peopled but sending companies of archers clad in green to the muster of Gondor at Minas Tirith in T.A. 3019, among the last and least of the fiefs to arrive.

records.name: Anfalas
records.description: A long, thinly peopled coastal fief of Gondor west of Belfalas, called Langstrand, whose folk under old Golasgil marched far and late to answer Gondor's muster before the siege of Minas Tirith in T.A. 3019.

records.name: Andrast
records.description: The 'long cape', the westernmost headland of Gondor's White Mountains where they meet the sea, bordering the wild Drúwaith Iaur. Sparsely settled and remote, it marked the western limit of Gondor's authority.

records.name: Drúwaith Iaur
records.description: The 'Old Púkel-land', a wild, thinly peopled region between Anfalas and Enedwaith around the Cape of Andrast, home to a remnant of the reclusive Drúedain before most withdrew to the Drúadan Forest of Anórien.

records.name: White Mountains
records.description: The great mountain range forming Gondor's northern wall against Rohan and sheltering its southern fiefs, running from Andrast in the west to Mindolluin above Minas Tirith in the east. Beneath it run the haunted Paths of the Dead, and along its northern face burn the seven beacon-hills.

records.name: Ithilien
records.description: The fair, wooded fief of Gondor east of the Anduin, once its garden, held after T.A. 2901 only by rangers and outlaws after Minas Ithil fell to the Nazgûl. Faramir's rangers waged a hidden war here against Sauron's forces until its liberation in T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: Formally abandoned as a permanent settlement after Minas Ithil's fall, though Gondor continues to contest it.
Frodo and Sam pass through Ithilien on the way to Mordor; it is liberated after the War of the Ring.

records.name: North Ithilien
records.description: The northern half of Ithilien, forested and hilly, holding Henneth Annûn and the Forbidden Pool, where Faramir's rangers lay hidden and where Frodo and Sam were taken captive before being freed to continue toward Mordor in T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: Faramir's rangers ambush a Haradrim column, witnessed by Frodo and Sam.

records.name: South Ithilien
records.description: The southern half of Ithilien, extending south from the Morgul Vale toward the Poros. The Harad Road carried Southron armies north through this contested region. After the War of the Ring, Ithilien became Faramir's princedom.

records.name: Henneth Annûn
records.description: A hidden refuge behind a waterfall in North Ithilien, secret base of Faramir's rangers, its cave-mouth curtained by falling water that catches the setting sun. Here Frodo and Sam were sheltered and questioned by Faramir in T.A. 3019 before continuing toward Mordor.

chronicle.description: Frodo and Sam are given refuge and food by Faramir.

records.name: Forbidden Pool
records.description: A pool below the falls of Henneth Annûn, forbidden to any stranger on pain of death by Faramir's law. Here Sméagol was caught fishing by Faramir's rangers, forcing Frodo to bring him in and so preserve his life and Sméagol's fragile trust.

chronicle.description: Sméagol is captured here by Faramir's rangers.

records.name: Cross-roads
records.description: A meeting of ancient roads in Ithilien around a great fallen statue of a king of Gondor, its head crowned in mockery by Orcs, until Frodo saw a wreath of white and gold flowers had grown about the fallen head. The road to Minas Morgul branches here from the road south.

chronicle.description: Frodo and Sam pass the Cross-roads and see the king's statue crowned with flowers, a sign of hope.

records.name: Emyn Arnen
records.description: A range of hills in South Ithilien east of the Anduin, given as a princedom to Faramir and Éowyn after the War of the Ring, becoming the seat of the Stewards' line and Princes of Ithilien in the Fourth Age.

chronicle.description: c. Aragorn grants Emyn Arnen to Faramir as Prince of Ithilien.

records.name: Field of Cormallen
records.description: A green field in North Ithilien near Cair Andros and the Anduin, named for its golden-flowered culumalda trees. Here the Host of the West camped after the Ring's destruction, and here on 8 April T.A. 3019 Frodo and Sam were honoured before all the assembled armies of the West.

chronicle.description: The Ringbearers are praised before the Host of the West after the fall of Sauron.

records.name: Poros
records.description: A river flowing from the mountains on Mordor's border through South Ithilien to join the Anduin, forming Gondor's southern boundary with Harondor. Its crossing was fought over in T.A. 2885 and again by Sauron's forces marching north in T.A. 3019.

records.name: Crossings of Poros
records.description: The main ford of the river Poros on the Harad Road, where in T.A. 2885 Haradrim invaders crossed into Ithilien and were defeated by Gondor and Rohan in the Battle of the Crossings of Poros, though the Rohirric princes Folcred and Fastred fell there.

chronicle.description: Battle of the Crossings of Poros: Steward Túrin II and Rohirric princes defeat a Haradrim invasion; Folcred and Fastred are slain.

records.name: Harondor
records.description: The disputed southern region of Gondor beyond the Poros, once a settled province but reduced by T.A. 3019 to a debatable borderland fought over with Umbar and Harad for centuries, its old settlements long abandoned or fallen to the enemy.

records.name: Harad Road
records.description: The long South Road from the Cross-roads in Ithilien southward over the Crossings of Poros, across Harondor to the ford of the Harnen and on into Near Harad. Built by Gondor in the days of its southern empire, it is the highway by which Hyarmendacil marched to conquer Harad and by which the Haradrim later march north. In March T.A. 3019 Faramir's rangers ambushed a Southron column coming up it into Ithilien.

chronicle.description: Hyarmendacil I marches south along the road to subdue Harad.
The Haradrim come up the road and cross the Poros into Ithilien.
7 March: Faramir's rangers ambush Southrons marching north on the road near Henneth Annûn.

records.name: Barrowfields
alternateNames: Mounds of the Kings of Rohan
records.description: Rows of green mounds outside Edoras where the Kings of Rohan lie buried, planted with the white star-shaped flower simbelmynë, 'ever-mind', that blooms there in every season. Théoden's own mound was raised here after his body was brought home from the Pelennor Fields in T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: Théoden King is laid in the eighth mound after his death at the Pelennor Fields.

records.name: The Hallow
records.description: An ancient hallowed enclosure high on the shoulder of Mount Mindolluin above Minas Tirith, sacred since the days of the Kings and forbidden to all but the King and those he brought with him. Here in T.A. 3019 Aragorn and Gandalf found a sapling of the White Tree growing in the snow.

chronicle.description: Aragorn finds the sapling of the White Tree here.

records.name: Citadel
records.description: The walled seventh and uppermost circle of Minas Tirith, entered through the Tower Gate and holding the White Tower, the Court of the Fountain, and the guarded houses of the city's high officers. Its guard, the Tower Guard, wear the ancient livery of Elendil's line.

records.name: Old Guesthouse
records.description: A house in the Rath Celerdain on the first circle of Minas Tirith, home of the guardsman Beregond and his son Bergil. Pippin Took lodged here as Beregond's guest during the siege of T.A. 3019, and the two became friends.

chronicle.description: Pippin lodges with Beregond and Bergil here during the siege of Minas Tirith.

records.name: Battle of the Camp
records.description: A disastrous battle of T.A. 1944 in southern Gondor near the Poros, where a great camp of King Ondoher's army was overrun by night by allied Wainriders and Haradrim, and Ondoher and both his sons were slain. The same year Eärnil turned the tide with victory at the Crossings of Poros, and was afterward made King.

chronicle.description: King Ondoher and his sons fall when Wainriders and Haradrim destroy his camp by night.

records.name: Doors of Orthanc
records.description: The black doors of the tower of Orthanc, at the top of a stair before which Gandalf, Théoden and their companions parleyed with the imprisoned Saruman in T.A. 3019, and from which Wormtongue hurled down the palantír of Orthanc that struck near Gandalf's feet.

chronicle.description: Saruman is confronted here by the Company; Wormtongue casts down the palantír.

records.name: Gate of Isengard
records.description: The single great gate of iron and stone in the ring-wall of Isengard, its arched tunnel the only way through to the plain within. Torn down and cast aside by the Ents during the storming of Isengard in T.A. 3019, after which Treebeard set his own watch there.

chronicle.description: Broken open by the Ents during the storming of Isengard.

records.name: Mordor
records.description: The realm of Sauron the Dark Lord in the south-east of the known lands, walled on three sides by mountains: the Ered Lithui to the north and the Ephel Dúath to the west and south. Within lie the ash-plains of Gorgoroth and Lithlad, the slave-tilled fields of Nurn about the Sea of Núrnen, and the Dark Tower of Barad-dûr. Orcs, Trolls, the Nazgûl and armies of enslaved Men fill it at the end of the Third Age.

chronicle.description: c. Sauron chooses Mordor as his stronghold and begins building Barad-dûr.
Sauron overthrown by the Last Alliance; Gondor sets a watch on Mordor.
The Witch-king comes to Mordor and gathers the Nazgûl there.
Sauron returns in secret to Mordor; in 2951 he declares himself openly.
25 March: the One Ring is destroyed and the power of Mordor ends.

records.name: Barad-dûr
records.description: The Dark Tower, Sauron's stronghold and seat of power, rising from the Plateau of Gorgoroth east of Mount Doom beneath a spur of the Ered Lithui. Built with the power of the One Ring, its foundations cannot be destroyed while the Ring endures. It is a vast fortress of iron and adamant, courts, dungeons and pinnacles; from the Window of the Eye near its summit Sauron keeps watch. A road runs west over an iron bridge toward Orodruin.

chronicle.description: c. Sauron begins the building of Barad-dûr.
c. Barad-dûr completed after the forging of the One Ring.
Razed to its foundations after the seven-year siege of the Last Alliance.
Sauron begins the rebuilding of Barad-dûr.
25 March: Barad-dûr falls in ruin when the Ring is destroyed.

records.name: Mount Doom
records.description: The volcano of Mordor, standing alone on the Plateau of Gorgoroth west of Barad-dûr. Its broken base rises some three thousand feet above the plain and its cone half as high again. Sauron forged the One Ring in its fires, and only there can the Ring be unmade. Sauron's Road climbs its eastern face to the Sammath Naur. It burst into flame again at Sauron's return and is stilled only with the Ring's destruction.

chronicle.description: c. Sauron forges the One Ring in the fires of Orodruin.
The last combat of the Last Alliance is fought on its slopes; Isildur cuts the Ring from Sauron's hand.
Mount Doom bursts into flame again; the last folk of Ithilien flee.
25 March: the Ring is destroyed in the Sammath Naur and the mountain erupts.

records.name: Sammath Naur
records.description: The Chambers of Fire: a long tunnel and high-roofed cavern cut into the cone of Mount Doom, entered by a dark door on its eastern face at the end of Sauron's Road. A short way within, the floor is split by the Cracks of Doom, a chasm glowing with the mountain's fire. Here Sauron forged the One Ring c. S.A. 1600, and here on 25 March T.A. 3019 the Ring was unmade.

chronicle.description: c. The One Ring is forged here.
25 March: Frodo claims the Ring; Gollum bites it from his hand and falls into the fire.

records.name: Cracks of Doom
records.description: The great fissure cutting across the floor and walls of the Sammath Naur, a short way inside the door: a deep chasm filled with fire, the very heart of Orodruin where the One Ring was forged and where alone it could be destroyed. Isildur refused to cast the Ring into it in S.A. 3441; on 25 March T.A. 3019 Gollum fell into it with the Ring, and the Ring was unmade.

chronicle.description: Isildur, urged by Elrond and Círdan, refuses to cast the Ring into the fire.
25 March: Gollum falls into the Cracks of Doom with the One Ring.

records.name: Destruction of the One Ring
records.description: The site of the ending of the Quest of the Ring, in the Sammath Naur on 25 March T.A. 3019. Frodo, at the Cracks of Doom, claimed the Ring for his own; Gollum seized him, bit the Ring from his finger and, dancing on the brink, fell with it into the fire. The Ring was unmade, Barad-dûr and the Black Gate fell, Sauron passed into the shadow, and Mount Doom erupted. The Eagles bore the hobbits from the ruin.

chronicle.description: 25 March: the One Ring is destroyed; Sauron and his realm fall.

records.name: Plateau of Gorgoroth
records.description: The high, barren plateau of north-western Mordor, enclosed by the Ered Lithui and the Ephel Dúath, on which stand Mount Doom and Barad-dûr. A land of ash, cinder and pitted craters, riddled with orc-camps, arms-deeps and slave-pits, it is crossed by Sauron's roads running from the Morannon, the Isenmouthe and the Morgul Pass to the Dark Tower. Frodo and Sam crossed it to Orodruin in March T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: The Last Alliance enters Gorgoroth and lays siege to Barad-dûr.
19–24 March: Frodo and Sam cross the plain from the Isenmouthe road to Mount Doom.

records.name: Lithlad
records.description: The 'Plain of Ash', a mournful plain of eastern Mordor lying south of the Ered Lithui and east of the Plateau of Gorgoroth, stretching away toward Rhûn. Together with Gorgoroth it is walled about by the two great mountain ranges of Mordor. It is named only once, in the account of Frodo's approach to the Black Gate, and nothing is told of who or what dwells there.

records.name: Nurn
records.description: The southern and eastern lowlands of Mordor about the Sea of Núrnen, far from the fumes of Mount Doom. Unlike the ash-deserts of the north, Nurn is fertile: its great fields are tilled by slaves from Sauron's conquered peoples to feed the armies of Mordor. Its rivers flow down from the Ephel Dúath and from a spur of the Ered Lithui. After the War of the Ring King Elessar frees the slaves and gives them Nurn as their own.

chronicle.description: King Elessar frees the slaves of Mordor and gives them the lands about Lake Núrnen.

records.name: Sea of Núrnen
records.description: A great bitter inland sea in the south-east of Mordor, in the land of Nurn, fed by four rivers from the Ephel Dúath and the Ered Lithui. Its Sindarin name means 'sad water', and its dark waters are not fit to drink, yet the lands about it are fertile enough to bear the vast slave-tilled fields that feed Sauron's armies. After the War of the Ring these lands are given to the freed slaves.

chronicle.description: After the fall of Sauron, King Elessar gives the lands about Núrnen to the freed slaves of Mordor.

records.name: Ered Lithui
records.description: The Ash Mountains, the long grey range that walls Mordor on the north. From the Morannon, where it meets the Ephel Dúath, it runs eastward for hundreds of miles toward the Sea of Rhûn, and a spur reaches south toward Núrnen. Barad-dûr stands beneath its western end, and in its shadow lie the plains of Gorgoroth and Lithlad. Its gullies and passes are guarded by the orc-holds of Sauron.

records.name: Ephel Dúath
records.description: The Mountains of Shadow, the great western and southern fence of Mordor. From the Morannon they run south along the border of Ithilien, then bend east to enclose Nurn. Their outer wall is cleft by the Morgul Vale and the high pass of Cirith Ungol; behind their northern stretch runs the lesser ridge of the Morgai. The Harnen rises on their southern slopes. Orc-holds such as Durthang and the Tower of Cirith Ungol guard them.

records.name: Morannon
records.description: The Black Gate of Mordor: a rampart of stone with a single great gate of iron, built by Sauron across the mouth of Cirith Gorgor, the Haunted Pass, where the Ered Lithui and the Ephel Dúath meet. It is flanked by the Towers of the Teeth and faces the battle-plain of Dagorlad. Frodo turned aside from it in March T.A. 3019; on 25 March the Host of the West fought its last battle before it, and it fell in ruin.

chronicle.description: The Last Alliance forces the pass after its victory on Dagorlad.
5 March: Frodo and Sam hide in sight of the Morannon and turn south at dusk.
25 March: the Battle of the Morannon; the Gate is cast down at the Ring's destruction.

records.name: Towers of the Teeth
records.description: The two towers, Narchost and Carchost, standing on the hills either side of the Morannon. The Men of Gondor built them early in the Third Age to keep watch on Mordor after Sauron's fall, but the watch failed after the Great Plague and Sauron's servants repaired and garrisoned them. From their windows sleepless eyes watch the Desolation before the Gate. They crash down in the earthquake of 25 March T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: c. Gondor's garrisons abandon the towers after the Great Plague.
25 March: the Towers of the Teeth fall as the Ring is destroyed.

records.name: Narchost
records.description: The western of the two Towers of the Teeth, standing on the height west of the Morannon at the mouth of Cirith Gorgor. Raised by Gondor after the War of the Last Alliance to watch the gate of Mordor, it was long abandoned and then reoccupied and repaired by Sauron's Orcs. With its twin Carchost it crashes into ruin when the Ring is destroyed on 25 March T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: 25 March: Narchost falls in the earthquake that follows the Ring's destruction.

records.name: Carchost
records.description: The eastern of the two Towers of the Teeth, standing on the height east of the Morannon at the mouth of Cirith Gorgor. Like its twin Narchost it was built by Gondor early in the Third Age to guard against Sauron's return, fell into decay when the watch was abandoned, and was garrisoned again by Orcs. It falls in ruin on 25 March T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: 25 March: Carchost falls in the earthquake that follows the Ring's destruction.

records.name: Cirith Gorgor
records.description: The Haunted Pass, the narrow gap where the Ered Lithui and the Ephel Dúath meet at Mordor's north-western corner, and the chief entrance to the Black Land. The Morannon bars its mouth and the Towers of the Teeth stand on the heights either side; behind it opens the valley of Udûn. Through it Sauron's armies march out to Dagorlad and Ithilien, and through it the Host of Mordor issued on 25 March T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: The Last Alliance passes through into Mordor after the Battle of Dagorlad.
25 March: the armies of Mordor pour out through the pass against the Host of the West.

records.name: Udûn
records.description: A deep, wide valley just inside the Black Gate, enclosed by arms of the Ered Lithui and the Ephel Dúath. Through it the road runs from Cirith Gorgor south-east to the Isenmouthe and so to Gorgoroth. Udûn is a vast armed camp of Mordor, ringed with tunnels, arms-deeps and orc-holds such as Durthang on the heights above; its Sindarin name means 'hell'. Sauron's armies mustered here before the Battle of the Morannon.

chronicle.description: March: the hosts of Mordor gather in Udûn before issuing from the Black Gate.

records.name: Isenmouthe
records.description: The 'Iron Jaws': the narrow gap between arms of the Ered Lithui and the Ephel Dúath where the valley of Udûn opens onto Gorgoroth. It is barred by an earthen wall and a great ditch spanned by a single bridge, closed by a fence of pointed iron posts and watched by forts on the rocky spurs. Frodo and Sam were swept toward it among orc-troops on 18 March T.A. 3019, escaping in the dark at the road-meeting.

chronicle.description: 18 March: Frodo and Sam, in sight of the Isenmouthe, are overtaken by Orcs on the road from Durthang.
19 March: the hobbits escape in the confusion at the road-meeting and take the road toward Barad-dûr.

records.name: Durthang
records.description: An old castle perched high in the northern Ephel Dúath, on the heights north-west of the Isenmouthe, overlooking the valley of Udûn. Perhaps once a fortress of Gondor's watch on Mordor, by the end of the Third Age it is one of the many orc-holds of Sauron; its Sindarin name means 'dark oppression'. A steep road winds from it down to the Isenmouthe, along which an orc-company drove Frodo and Sam on 18 March T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: 18 March: Frodo and Sam rest in sight of Durthang and are overtaken by its Orcs at nightfall.

records.name: Morgai
records.description: The 'Black Fence', a lower, jagged ridge running parallel to the Ephel Dúath along the inner side of Mordor's western wall, from near the Isenmouthe south past Cirith Ungol. Between the two lies a narrow trough-valley with a stream-bed, brambles and grey grass, the only living things in northern Mordor. Frodo and Sam walked north along this valley from 15 to 18 March T.A. 3019 to avoid the open plain of Gorgoroth.

chronicle.description: 15–18 March: Frodo and Sam journey north along the Morgai valley from Cirith Ungol.

records.name: Cirith Ungol
records.description: The 'Pass of the Spider', a high secret pass over the Ephel Dúath from the Morgul Vale into Mordor, north of the Morgul Pass. It is climbed by the Straight Stair and the Winding Stair, then a tunnel through Torech Ungol, the lair of Shelob, to the Cleft at the summit beneath the Tower of Cirith Ungol. Frodo and Sam, led by Gollum, crossed it on 12–13 March T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: 12 March: Gollum leads Frodo and Sam into Shelob's Lair.
13 March: Frodo is captured by the Orcs of Cirith Ungol.

records.name: The Cleft
records.description: The narrow notch at the summit of the pass of Cirith Ungol, between two horns of rock beyond the tunnel of Torech Ungol, from which the path drops down into Mordor beneath the Tower. Here Sam fought Shelob and found Frodo stung and bound on 13 March T.A. 3019, and here he took the Ring and the Phial before the Orcs of Shagrat and Gorbag carried Frodo away.

chronicle.description: 13 March: Sam wounds Shelob in the Cleft and takes the Ring from the stung Frodo.

records.name: Tower of Cirith Ungol
records.description: A fortress of three tiers and a turret built against the cliff on the Mordor side of the pass of Cirith Ungol, above the road down to the Morgul Pass. Gondor raised it after the Last Alliance to watch Mordor, but it has long been an orc-hold, its gate guarded by the Two Watchers. Here Shagrat's orcs held Frodo captive on 13–14 March T.A. 3019 until Sam, after the garrisons had slain one another, rescued him.

chronicle.description: 13 March: Frodo is carried captive into the Tower.
14 March: Sam passes the Watchers and rescues Frodo after the orc-fight.
15 March: Frodo and Sam escape into the Morgai valley.

records.name: Two Watchers
records.description: Two great three-bodied figures with vulture faces, seated on thrones either side of the arched gate of the Tower of Cirith Ungol. Filled with an evil vigilance, their unseen will bars the gate against any who would pass. Sam broke through it with the Phial of Galadriel on 14 March T.A. 3019; as the hobbits fled the next day the keystone of the arch fell and the Watchers wailed, summoning a Nazgûl.

chronicle.description: 14–15 March: Sam and Frodo pass the Watchers by the light of the Phial; the gate-arch collapses.

records.name: Undergate
records.description: A gate of brazen doors closing the Under-way, the tunnel that leads from Shelob's Lair beneath the pass up into the lowest floor of the Tower of Cirith Ungol. Through it the Orcs carried the stung and bound Frodo on 13 March T.A. 3019; Sam, following, found it locked and had to turn back through Torech Ungol and climb to the Tower by the outer gate.

chronicle.description: 13 March: the Orcs bear Frodo through the Undergate; Sam is shut out.

records.name: Torech Ungol
records.description: Shelob's Lair: a stinking tunnel and warren of caverns beneath the summit of the pass of Cirith Ungol, where Shelob the Great, last child of Ungoliant, has dwelt since before Sauron came to Mordor. The Orcs of the Tower use its side-passages at need. On 12–13 March T.A. 3019 Gollum led Frodo and Sam into it; Frodo was stung and bound, and Sam wounded Shelob with Sting and the Phial of Galadriel.

chronicle.description: 12 March: Gollum leads the hobbits into Torech Ungol.
13 March: Shelob stings Frodo; Sam drives her off, wounded.

records.name: Stairs of Cirith Ungol
records.description: Two great stairways cut into the northern wall of the Morgul Vale, by which a secret path climbs from the Morgul-road toward the pass of Cirith Ungol. The Straight Stair rises almost sheer up the cliff; above it, after a long climbing path, the Winding Stair twists up through the crags to the tunnel of Torech Ungol. Gollum led Frodo and Sam up them on 10–11 March T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: 10–11 March: Frodo, Sam and Gollum climb the Stairs after the Morgul-host sets forth.

records.name: Straight Stair
records.description: The lower of the two stairs of Cirith Ungol: a steep, almost vertical flight of many hundreds of worn steps cut into the cliff of the Morgul Vale's northern wall, climbing from near the Morgul-road up into a fold of the Ephel Dúath. Frodo, Sam and Gollum climbed it in the darkness on the night of 10 March T.A. 3019, after watching the Morgul-host march out.

chronicle.description: 10 March: the hobbits climb the Straight Stair by night.

records.name: Winding Stair
records.description: The upper of the two stairs of Cirith Ungol: a long, twisting stairway climbing through the crags of the Ephel Dúath above the Straight Stair, ending near the summit before the dark tunnel of Torech Ungol. Frodo and Sam climbed it on 11 March T.A. 3019, and near its top they rested and spoke of the tales they were in while Gollum crept away to Shelob.

chronicle.description: 11 March: Frodo and Sam climb the Winding Stair; Gollum visits Shelob.

records.name: Minas Morgul
records.description: The Dead City: once Minas Ithil, Tower of the Rising Moon, built by Isildur as Gondor's eastern fortress in a valley of the Ephel Dúath facing Minas Anor. Taken by the Nazgûl in T.A. 2002, it became Minas Morgul, the Tower of Sorcery, seat of the Witch-king. Its walls glow with a corpse-pale light, its gate gapes like a mouth, and a bridge of hideous statues crosses the Morgulduin before it. Its host marched on Minas Tirith in T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: Isildur founds Minas Ithil as the eastern fortress of Gondor.
Sauron captures Minas Ithil; it is recovered after his fall.
The Nazgûl take Minas Ithil and its palantír; it becomes Minas Morgul.
King Eärnur rides to its gate to answer the Witch-king's challenge and is never seen again.
10 March: the Morgul-host under the Witch-king marches out to besiege Minas Tirith.

records.name: Fall of Minas Ithil
records.description: Site of the two captures of Minas Ithil. In S.A. 3429 Sauron seized the city and burned the White Tree, driving Isildur to seek Elendil; it was recovered after the Last Alliance. In T.A. 2000 the Nazgûl, leading masterless Men out of Mordor, besieged it in the reign of Eärnil II, and in 2002 they took it with its palantír. Thereafter it was Minas Morgul, and Gondor's kings ended with Eärnur in 2050.

chronicle.description: First fall: Sauron captures Minas Ithil.
The Nazgûl issue from Mordor and besiege Minas Ithil.
Second fall: Minas Ithil taken by the Nazgûl; the Ithil-stone captured.

records.name: Morgul Vale
records.description: The valley of the Morgulduin in the western Ephel Dúath, opening westward into Ithilien; at its mouth stands Minas Morgul. Once fair, it is now a place of dread: meads of pale, luminous, evil-smelling flowers line the steaming river, and its fumes daze the mind. The Morgul-road climbs the vale to the Morgul Pass. On 19 March T.A. 3019 the Host of the West halted here, burned the meads and broke the bridge.

chronicle.description: The valley falls under the Nazgûl and becomes Imlad Morgul.
10 March: Frodo, Sam and Gollum cross the vale as the Morgul-host marches out.
19 March: the Host of the West halts in the vale, fires the meads and breaks the bridge.

records.name: Morgulduin
records.description: The stream of the Morgul Vale, rising in the Ephel Dúath and flowing west past Minas Morgul, beneath the statue-lined bridge of the Morgul-road, out into Ithilien and thence to the Anduin south of Osgiliath. Within the vale its waters are poisoned and give off cold, deadly vapours; Faramir warned the hobbits to drink of no water that flows from Imlad Morgul. Below the vale it runs through the woods of Ithilien.

records.name: Morgul Pass
records.description: The main pass over the Ephel Dúath at the head of the Morgul Vale: a great ravine through which the Morgul-road climbs from Minas Morgul into Mordor and descends toward the plain of Gorgoroth. It is the road of the Nazgûl and of the Morgul-host, and the orc-road from the Tower of Cirith Ungol comes down to join it. In March T.A. 3019 the Host of the West guarded the Cross-roads against enemies coming over it.

chronicle.description: 10 March: the Morgul-host passes over the Morgul Pass toward Minas Tirith.

records.name: Morgul-road
records.description: The ancient road from Osgiliath east across Ithilien through the Cross-roads to Minas Morgul, and thence up the Morgul Vale and over the Morgul Pass into Mordor. Built by Gondor when Minas Ithil was its fortress, it is now the wraith-road by which the Nazgûl and the Morgul-host ride to war. Frodo, Sam and Gollum followed it warily from the Cross-roads to the bridge before Minas Morgul on 10 March T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: 10 March: the hobbits follow the road to Minas Morgul; the Morgul-host marches west along it.

records.name: Sauron's Road
records.description: The road from the western gate of Barad-dûr, across a vast iron bridge over a deep chasm, west over the plain of Gorgoroth to Mount Doom, up a long causeway on its eastern slope, and winding round the cone to the door of the Sammath Naur. Broad and paved with beaten ash and rubble, it is kept clear by orc-labour after every eruption. Sam carried Frodo up it on 25 March T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: 25 March: Sam carries Frodo up Sauron's Road to the door of the Sammath Naur.

records.name: Window of the Eye
records.description: An opening high in the topmost tower of Barad-dûr, facing west toward Mount Doom, from which the Eye of Sauron looks out over Gorgoroth and the lands beyond. From the slopes of Orodruin on 25 March T.A. 3019 Sam saw it revealed for a moment through the shadow-mantle of the fortress, a red flame stabbing northward, before Sauron's gaze turned to the Morannon.

chronicle.description: 25 March: Sam glimpses the Window of the Eye from the slopes of Mount Doom.

records.name: Slag-hills
records.description: Great mounds of crushed rock and fire-blasted, poison-stained earth, heaped up by the Orcs over long years before the Black Gate in the Desolation of the Morannon. On 25 March T.A. 3019 Aragorn drew up the Host of the West on two of these hills, where it was surrounded by the armies of Sauron and held out until the Ring was destroyed and the enemy fled.

chronicle.description: 25 March: the Host of the West stands on the Slag-hills at the Battle of the Morannon.

records.name: Desolation of the Morannon
records.description: The dead land immediately before the Black Gate, south of the Dagorlad: a waste of ash-choked pools, slag-mounds and cones of poisoned earth, defiled by the labour of Sauron's slaves and lifeless for miles about. Frodo and Sam looked on the Morannon from its edge on 5 March T.A. 3019, and the Host of the West camped in it on 24 March before its last battle upon the Slag-hills.

chronicle.description: 5 March: Frodo and Sam creep through the Desolation to spy on the Black Gate.
24 March: the Host of the West camps in the Desolation of the Morannon.

records.name: Battle of the Morannon
records.description: The last battle of the War of the Ring, fought on 25 March T.A. 3019 before the Black Gate. Aragorn led some six thousand men of Gondor and Rohan to the Slag-hills to draw Sauron's Eye from Frodo; after the parley with the Mouth of Sauron the Gate opened and the host was surrounded by Orcs, Trolls, Easterlings and Haradrim. As the Eagles came the Ring was destroyed, Sauron's power failed, and his armies fled or perished.

chronicle.description: 25 March: the Host of the West is surrounded on the Slag-hills; the Ring is destroyed and Mordor's army breaks.

records.name: Siege of Barad-dûr
records.description: The seven-year siege of the Dark Tower by the Last Alliance of Elves and Men, from S.A. 3434, after their victory on Dagorlad, until S.A. 3441. The host of Gil-galad and Elendil camped on the plain of Gorgoroth and suffered great loss; Anárion was slain by a stone from the Tower in 3440. At last Sauron came forth and was overthrown on the slopes of Orodruin, though Gil-galad and Elendil fell, and Isildur cut the Ring from his hand.

chronicle.description: The Last Alliance enters Mordor and begins the siege of Barad-dûr.
Anárion is slain by a stone cast from the Tower.
Sauron overthrown; Gil-galad and Elendil slain; Barad-dûr razed.

records.name: Frodo and Sam's Road through Mordor
records.description: The way of the Ring-bearer, 15–25 March T.A. 3019. Escaping the Tower of Cirith Ungol, Frodo and Sam went north along the trough between the Morgai and the Ephel Dúath, climbed to the orc-road from Durthang to the Isenmouthe, were swept along it in an orc-troop and escaped at the road-meeting, then followed the Barad-dûr road east across Gorgoroth. On 22 March they turned south over the plain, cast away their gear, and reached the Sammath Naur on 25 March.

chronicle.description: 15 March: the hobbits escape the Tower and turn north along the Morgai.
18–19 March: driven along the Durthang road toward the Isenmouthe; escape at the road-meeting.
22 March: they leave the road and turn south toward Orodruin.
24 March: the last march to the feet of Mount Doom.
25 March: they climb Sauron's Road to the Sammath Naur.

records.name: Harad
records.description: The vast hot lands south of Gondor and Mordor beyond the river Harnen, divided into Near Harad and Far Harad; their bounds to the east and south are unknown in the North. The Haradrim or Southrons are many warring tribes and kingdoms, dark-skinned and fierce, who ride to war with mûmakil. Long dominated by Umbar and by Sauron, they fight Gondor at the Poros, the Pelennor and the Morannon. Hobbits call it the Sunlands.

chronicle.description: Hyarmendacil I crosses the Harnen and forces the kings of Harad to acknowledge Gondor.
The Haradrim join the Wainriders and Khand in the assault on Gondor.
The Haradrim cross the Poros and are defeated with the help of Rohan.
The Haradrim fight for Sauron at the Pelennor and the Morannon.
King Elessar makes peace with the peoples of Harad.

records.name: Near Harad
records.description: The northern part of Harad, lying south of the Harnen and of Gondor's lost province of Harondor, between the Bay of Belfalas and Umbar in the west and Khand in the east; the Harad Road runs into it from the north. Its Haradrim are brown-skinned with black hair and dark eyes, and camels roam its dry lands. Its kings warred with Gondor, allied with the Wainriders and Khand in T.A. 1944, and sent men and mûmakil to Sauron's wars.

chronicle.description: The Men of Near Harad, with Khand and the Wainriders, attack Gondor; their army is destroyed in South Ithilien.
Warriors of Near Harad march north to the siege of Minas Tirith.

records.name: Far Harad
records.description: The distant, little-known south of Harad, far beyond Near Harad: a land of great heat, dark forests, apes, and the mûmakil or oliphaunts that the Southrons train for war. Its peoples are black-skinned, described by the men of Gondor at the Pelennor as like half-trolls with white eyes and red tongues. Warriors of Far Harad fought for Sauron at the Battle of the Pelennor Fields on 15 March T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: 15 March: men of Far Harad fight in the Battle of the Pelennor Fields.

records.name: Haradwaith
records.description: 'The South-folk's land', the name written across the southern lands on the maps of Gondor, also rendered Sutherland. It is the country of the Haradrim south of the Harnen and of Mordor's southern mountains, embracing both Near Harad and Far Harad. Beyond the reach of Gondor's later kings, its many tribes are ruled by their own lords, and at the end of the Third Age most are subject to Sauron.

chronicle.description: King Ciryandil of Gondor falls in battle in Haradwaith.

records.name: Harnen
records.description: 'South-water', the great river that bounds Harad on the north. It rises on the southern slopes of the Ephel Dúath and flows some five hundred miles south-west and then west, through a wide delta into the Bay of Belfalas midway between the Mouths of Anduin and Umbar. Since the Kin-strife it marks the southern border of Harondor, the debatable land between Gondor and the Corsairs. The Harad Road fords it above its westward bend.

chronicle.description: Ciryaher crosses the Harnen and utterly defeats the Men of Harad, taking the name Hyarmendacil.
After the Kin-strife the Harnen becomes the contested southern bound of Gondor.

records.name: Ford of the Harnen
records.description: The crossing where the Harad Road fords the river Harnen on its way south from the Crossings of Poros through Harondor into Near Harad, some way upstream of the river's westward bend. Once Gondor's highway to its southern dominions, by the end of the Third Age it is the route of the Haradrim marching north to Sauron's wars. No name is recorded; only the crossing is shown on the maps of the West.

records.name: Hyarmendacil's Conquest of Harad
records.description: The campaign of T.A. 1050 in which Ciryaher of Gondor, having bided his time after his father Ciryandil fell at Umbar, came down from the north by land and sea, crossed the river Harnen and utterly defeated the Men of Harad. Their kings acknowledged Gondor's overlordship and their sons were sent as hostages to Osgiliath; Ciryaher took the name Hyarmendacil, 'South-victor', and Gondor reached the height of its power.

chronicle.description: Ciryaher crosses the Harnen and defeats the Haradrim; he takes the name Hyarmendacil.

records.name: Umbar
records.description: The realm of the Corsairs on the coast south of Gondor: a great cape and the lands about the land-locked firth of the Haven of Umbar. Númenórean since the Second Age and a home of the King's Men, it was won by Gondor in T.A. 933, lost to Castamir's rebels after the Kin-strife, retaken by Telumehtar and lost again. Its Corsairs, mingled with the Haradrim, harry Gondor's coasts and sail for Sauron in the War of the Ring.

chronicle.description: Umbar is made into a great fortress of the Númenóreans.
Eärnil I of Gondor takes Umbar by land and sea.
The sons of Castamir seize Umbar after the Kin-strife; the Corsairs arise.
Telumehtar Umbardacil storms Umbar and drives out the Corsairs.
13 March: the Corsair fleet is taken by Aragorn at Pelargir.

records.name: Havens of Umbar
records.description: The great natural harbour of Umbar, a land-locked firth sheltered by a long peninsula, with the City of the Corsairs at its eastern end. First fortified by Númenor in S.A. 2280 and long a stronghold of the King's Men, it became Gondor's chief southern haven under the Ship-kings and later the pirate stronghold of the Corsairs. Here Thorongil burned their fleet in T.A. 2980, and hence sailed the black ships defeated at Pelargir in T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: The Númenóreans fortify the Haven of Umbar.
Eärnil I captures Umbar; it becomes a great haven and fortress of Gondor.
The Haradrim besiege Umbar; Ciryandil is slain.
Thorongil burns a great part of the Corsairs' ships in the Haven.
The Corsair fleet sails against Gondor and is captured at Pelargir.

records.name: Cape of Umbar
records.description: The long headland of Umbar, thrusting west from the southern coast of the Bay of Belfalas and bending south to enclose the firth of the Haven. On its highest hill stood the white pillar of Ar-Pharazôn. In the days of the Ship-kings the realm of Gondor ran south along the coast to the peninsula and haven of Umbar; at the end of the Third Age the cape and its harbours are held by the Corsairs.

records.name: Firth of Umbar
records.description: The land-locked inlet of the sea enclosed by the cape of Umbar, with a narrow entrance from the Bay of Belfalas, forming the finest natural harbour on the southern coasts. Númenórean ships have used it since the Second Age; the fleets of the Ship-kings of Gondor and later of the Corsairs lie here. Off its mouth Eärnil I perished with many ships in a great storm in T.A. 936.

chronicle.description: Eärnil I is lost with many ships in a storm off Umbar.

records.name: Monument of Ar-Pharazôn
records.description: A white pillar with a crystal globe, built by Gondor after its capture of Umbar in T.A. 933 to commemorate Ar-Pharazôn's landing in S.A. 3261 and Sauron's submission. It was thrown down after Sauron's renewed ascendancy. The exact years of construction and destruction are not recorded.

chronicle.description: The later monument commemorates Ar-Pharazôn's landing and Sauron's submission.

records.name: Capture of Umbar
records.description: The siege by land and sea in which Eärnil I, second of the Ship-kings of Gondor, took the Haven of Umbar from the King's Men of Númenórean descent who had held it since the Downfall, making it a great haven and fortress of Gondor. The lords driven out fled to the Haradrim and stirred them to war, and Eärnil himself was lost in a storm off Umbar three years later.

chronicle.description: Eärnil I takes Umbar with great force by land and sea.

records.name: Siege of Umbar
records.description: The long investment of Gondor's fortress at Umbar by the Men of Harad, led by the lords who had been driven from it. King Ciryandil fell in battle in Haradwaith in T.A. 1015, but the Haven could not be taken because of Gondor's sea-power. For thirty-five years it was beset, until in 1050 Ciryaher came down by land and sea, crossed the Harnen and crushed the Haradrim, taking the name Hyarmendacil.

chronicle.description: The Haradrim invest Umbar; Ciryandil slain.
Ciryaher relieves Umbar and defeats Harad.

records.name: Thorongil's Raid on Umbar
records.description: The night attack of T.A. 2980 in which Thorongil, the captain of Gondor who was Aragorn in disguise, brought a small fleet to Umbar, burned a great part of the ships of the Corsairs, and slew the Captain of the Haven in battle upon the quays before withdrawing with little loss. He then left Gondor's service; the blow long lessened the Corsairs' threat to the coasts.

chronicle.description: Thorongil burns the Corsairs' ships and overthrows the Captain of the Haven on the quays.

records.name: Khand
records.description: A land south-east of Mordor and east of Near Harad, home of the Variags, fierce Men allied with Sauron. Little is known of it in the West, and its name is one of the few recorded words of the eastern tongues. The Variags joined the Wainriders and Near Harad in the great assault on Gondor in T.A. 1944, and Variags of Khand fought in the Morgul-host at the Battle of the Pelennor Fields in T.A. 3019.

chronicle.description: The Variags of Khand join the Wainriders and Near Harad against Gondor.
15 March: Variags of Khand fight at the Battle of the Pelennor Fields.

records.name: Breredon
records.description: A small hobbit village of Buckland on rising ground behind the Grindwall hythe of the Withywindle, in the narrow strip of land between the High Hay and the Baranduin. Also called Briar Hill, it stands near Haysend. Hobbit lore remembers its folk as good-humoured neighbours who teased boaters passing on the river below.

records.name: Grindwall
records.description: A small hythe on the north bank of the Withywindle, just outside the protection of the High Hay, fenced by a grind driven into the water to guard the landing. Breredon stands on the rise behind it. Hobbit tradition tells how Tom Bombadil moored his boat here while visiting Farmer Maggot, only for otters to carry it off upstream.

records.name: Elvet-isle
records.description: A small island in the Withywindle within the Old Forest, home to a company of nesting swans; its name is Old Hobbitish for 'swan'. Tom Bombadil passed it while boating downriver toward the Shire, as recalled in hobbit verse, a short way downstream from his own house among the willows.

records.name: Windle-reach
records.description: A rushing, bubbling stretch of the Withywindle running from the Withy-weir down to the Grindwall hythe at the edge of Buckland. Tom Bombadil's boat came foaming into this reach on its journey down from the Old Forest, according to the hobbit poem 'Bombadil Goes Boating' that preserves its whimsical name.

records.name: Withy-weir
records.description: A weir across the Withywindle above Windle-reach, near the edge of the Old Forest, probably raised by hobbits of Buckland to manage the river's flow. Tom Bombadil's boat rushed over it on his journey downriver in the tale told in 'Bombadil Goes Boating', foaming on into Windle-reach beyond.

records.name: Battle Pit
records.description: An old sand-pit near Bywater in the Westfarthing, used as a mass grave for some seventy Ruffians slain in the Battle of Bywater on 3 November T.A. 3019. The nineteen Hobbits who died were buried apart on a nearby hillside beneath a memorial stone, around which a garden of remembrance later grew.

chronicle.description: About seventy Ruffians killed in the Battle of Bywater are buried here in a former sand-pit.

records.name: Bridge Inn
records.description: An inn that once stood at the western end of the Brandywine Bridge, the last lodging before travellers crossed into Buckland. Under Lotho Sackville-Baggins' rule the Ruffians tore it down and raised an ugly guard-house in its place, where Frodo, Sam, Merry, and Pippin were briefly held by Shirriffs on their return in 3019.

chronicle.description: Demolished by Sharkey's Ruffians and replaced with a guard-house.

records.name: Mithe
records.description: The outflow of the Shirebourn into the Brandywine in the Eastfarthing, marked by a landing-stage called the Mithe Steps. A lane climbs from the Steps to join the Causeway near Deephallow. Hobbit verse tells how Tom Bombadil climbed the Steps at sunset on his way home after visiting the Shire.

records.name: The Causeway
records.description: A high-banked road of the Eastfarthing running north from Deephallow through Rushey and Stock to meet the East Road, tracing the Shire side of the Brandywine opposite Buckland. Frodo Baggins rode part of its length in Farmer Maggot's wagon on the night of 26 September 3018, on the way toward Bucklebury Ferry.

records.name: Old Grange
records.description: A granary that once stood in Hobbiton just below Bag End, north of the Water and west of the Hobbiton Road. Sharkey's Ruffians tore it down during their occupation of the Shire in 3019 and put up rows of tarred sheds in its place, one of the small industrial scars Sam mourned on his return.

chronicle.description: Demolished and replaced by tarred sheds during Sharkey's rule of the Shire.

records.name: South Lane
records.description: A lane in the Westfarthing running a quarter mile south from the Bywater Road to the farmlands of the Cotton family, between Hobbiton and Bywater. During the Battle of Bywater in 3019 Sam proposed making a stand here, an idea Merry rejected as poor tactics in favour of the trap sprung on the Bywater Road itself.

records.name: Town Hole
records.description: A great hobbit-hole in Michel Delving serving as the residence of the Mayor of the Shire, the one office elected by the whole Shire. Some years before the War of the Ring it partly collapsed on Mayor Will Whitfoot, who crawled out unhurt but coated head to foot in white dust, earning the name 'Flourdumpling.'

chronicle.description: c. 3013–3018: The Town Hole partly collapses on Mayor Will Whitfoot, who earns the nickname 'Flourdumpling.'

records.name: The Party Tree
records.description: A great tree in the middle of the Party Field south of Bag End, beneath which Bilbo Baggins held his farewell party and vanished in 3001. Sharkey's Men felled it in 3019; the next spring Samwise Gamgee planted a mallorn seed from Galadriel in its place, which grew into the Golden Tree, the only mallorn west of the Misty Mountains.

chronicle.description: Bilbo holds his Farewell Party beneath the tree and vanishes using the One Ring.
Sharkey's Men cut the tree down during their occupation of the Shire.
Sam plants a mallorn seed here; it flowers the next April as the Golden Tree.

records.name: Ferry Lane
records.description: A short lane, some hundred yards long and marked by tall white posts, running from the Causeway down to the Bucklebury Ferry landing opposite Buck Hill. Merry caught up with Frodo, Sam, and Pippin at its entrance on 26 September 3018, and a Black Rider chased them down it to the ferry itself.

chronicle.description: A Black Rider chases Frodo and his companions down the lane to the ferry landing.

records.name: New Row
records.description: A row of hobbit-holes built on the southern face of Hobbiton Hill after the War of the Ring, replacing Bagshot Row, which Sharkey's Men had pulled down. Hobbits wryly nicknamed it 'Sharkey's End', for Saruman was slain nearby. The Gaffer took Number Three, with Sam living there until his marriage to Rose Cotton.

chronicle.description: Built to rehouse the families displaced when Bagshot Row was destroyed.

records.name: Shirriff-house
records.description: A row of plain brick barrack-buildings at the western end of Frogmorton, hastily raised under Lotho Sackville-Baggins to quarter the enlarged Shirriffs who policed the Shire for Sharkey. Similar houses stood in other villages; all were pulled down once the Ruffians were driven out at the close of 3019.

chronicle.description: Torn down once the Scouring of the Shire ends Sharkey's rule.

records.name: Water-valley
records.description: The broad, gentle valley of the River Water, through which the East Road runs past Hobbiton, Bywater, Frogmorton, and Whitfurrows. One of the most settled and populous stretches of the Shire, it was a favourite walk of Bilbo Baggins, who often wandered its lanes with the young Frodo before his own departure.

records.name: North Moors
records.description: A wild, empty moorland along the northern border of the Northfarthing, the one part of the Shire where heavy snow was common and no elms grew. Around 3018 the hobbit Halfast Gamgee claimed to have seen a giant or tree-like being beyond its bounds, one of the few hints of the wide world's dangers to reach the Shire.

chronicle.description: c. 3018: Halfast Gamgee reports seeing a huge, tree-like figure beyond the moors.

records.name: Mugworth
records.description: A village of the Southfarthing appearing only in an early draft of 'The Road to Isengard', home to a hobbit named Elias Tobiasson, credited there with first bringing pipe-weed into the Shire. Cut from the published text of The Two Towers, it survives only among Christopher Tolkien's notes in The War of the Ring.

records.name: Bywater Road
records.description: A high-banked road branching west from the East Road near the Three-Farthing Stone, running through Bywater toward Little Delving. On 3 November 3019 Meriadoc Brandybuck used its steep banks to trap a hundred Ruffians between wagons drawn across either end, winning the decisive Battle of Bywater.

chronicle.description: Site of the Battle of Bywater, where Merry traps the Ruffians between wagons on the road's banked stretch.

records.name: Hill Road
records.description: A road in Hobbiton leading up over Hobbiton Hill past Bag End to Overhill. Walking here on the evening of 23 September 3018 while awaiting Gandalf, Frodo Baggins overheard a sinister black-cloaked stranger questioning old Hamfast Gamgee near Bagshot Row about the whereabouts of 'Baggins'.

chronicle.description: A Black Rider questions the Gaffer here about Frodo's whereabouts.

records.name: Stock Road
records.description: A road running from the village of Stock through the Woody End and the Green Hills toward the heart of the Shire. Here, on 22 September 3021, Frodo and Sam met the three Elven Ring-bearers, Elrond, Galadriel, and Gandalf, riding quietly toward the Grey Havens on one of the last journeys of the Third Age.

chronicle.description: Frodo and Sam meet the Elven Ring-bearers riding toward the Havens.

records.name: Hobbiton Road
records.description: A once tree-lined road branching from the East Road at Bywater and running to Hobbiton, continuing by some accounts around the Hill to Overhill. Its shading trees were felled and its verges built over with new sheds during Sharkey's occupation of the Shire, a change Sam and his friends found bitter on their return in 3019.

records.name: Little Lune
records.description: A tributary of the River Lune rising in the northern Ered Luin and flowing east to join it, its valley marking the northern boundary of Elvish Lindon against the Dwarf-holds beyond. Old mines near its source sheltered King Arvedui and his men after the fall of Fornost in T.A. 1974, before they pressed on to the Ice-bay of Forochel.

chronicle.description: Arvedui and his remaining followers shelter in Dwarf-mines near the river after Fornost's fall, before setting out for Forochel.

records.name: The Forgotten Villages
records.description: The scattered early settlements of the Hobbits across Eriador after they crossed the Misty Mountains and before the founding of the Shire: Harfoots dwelt between Weathertop and the mountains, Stoors between Tharbad and Dunland, with wandering Fallohides among both. By Bilbo's day all had vanished save the hobbits still living around Bree.

chronicle.description: The last hobbits gather into the newly founded Shire, and these older settlements fade from memory.

records.name: Adorn
records.description: A river rising in the western White Mountains and flowing northwest to join the Isen some hundred and fifty miles west of the Gap of Rohan, on the borders of Enedwaith. With the Isen it marked Rohan's disputed western march; around T.A. 2758 the half-Dunlending lord Freca held lands on both its banks before his death at Edoras.

chronicle.description: Freca, a lord holding lands on both banks of the Adorn, is slain by King Helm Hammerhand at Edoras.
Lord Freca, who held lands on both banks of the Adorn, quarrels with King Helm Hammerhand at Edoras and is slain

records.name: Fall of Cardolan
records.description: The Witch-king's conquest of Cardolan in T.A. 1409, following swiftly on the fall of the watch-tower of Amon Sûl. With its king slain and its defences broken, Cardolan never recovered as an independent realm; the Great Plague of 1636 finished what Angmar had begun, and its line of lords died out entirely.

chronicle.description: Angmar overruns and ravages Cardolan after the fall of Amon Sûl.

records.name: Fall of Amon Sûl
records.description: The siege and burning of the Dúnedain watch-tower on Weathertop by the Witch-king's forces in T.A. 1409, in which King Arveleg I of Arthedain was slain. The tower's fall opened the way for Angmar's armies to overrun Cardolan; its palantír was saved only by hasty flight south to Fornost.

chronicle.description: Amon Sûl is besieged, burned, and razed; King Arveleg I falls in its defence.

records.name: Fall of Fornost
records.description: The Witch-king captured Fornost in T.A. 1974, ending Arthedain. Arvedui fled north and drowned the following spring. The Witch-king occupied Fornost until Eärnur's allied host defeated his army on the plain west of the city in 1975.

chronicle.description: The Witch-king takes Fornost; King Arvedui flees north and Arthedain falls.

records.name: Second Siege of Imladris
records.description: An assault by Angmar's forces on Elrond's refuge of Rivendell, c. T.A. 1400, during the long war that also destroyed Cardolan and the tower of Amon Sûl. Elrond held the valley and, with reinforcements from Lothlórien, helped drive Angmar's armies back, keeping Rivendell an unconquered stronghold throughout the wars of the North.

chronicle.description: c. 1400: Angmar besieges Rivendell; Elrond holds the valley with aid from Lothlórien.

records.name: Battle of the Gwathló
records.description: In the final campaign of the War of the Elves and Sauron, c. S.A. 1700–1701, the allies defeated Sauron's army near Tharbad on the Gwathló. Ciryatur sent troops ashore at Lond Daer to attack from the south-west while Elves and other Númenóreans advanced from the north. The fleet arrived in 1700; Eriador was cleared in 1701.

chronicle.description: By 1701, victory near Tharbad and the ensuing pursuit clear Eriador of Sauron's forces.

records.name: Elvenking's Gate
alternateNames: Great Doors of the Elvenking's Halls
records.description: The great stone doors that form the main entrance to Thranduil's underground halls in northern Mirkwood, closed by a spell and opened only at the Elvenking's word. Thorin and Company were brought before Thranduil through this gate in T.A. 2941 after their capture in the forest, distinct from the water-gate used later for their escape.

chronicle.description: Thorin and Company are brought captive through the gate before King Thranduil.

records.name: Thranduil's Throne Room
records.description: A great pillared hall carved from living rock deep within Thranduil's halls, where the Elvenking sits in judgement and holds his feasts. Here Thorin was brought and interrogated after his capture in T.A. 2941, refusing to answer the king's questions about his errand into the forest.

chronicle.description: Thranduil questions the captured Thorin Oakenshield here.

records.name: Dungeons of the Elvenking's Halls
records.description: The lower prison-cells of Thranduil's halls, cut into the rock below the main chambers. Thorin was held here alone in the innermost cell after refusing to speak, and later his twelve companions were separately imprisoned here until Bilbo Baggins freed them for their escape by barrel in T.A. 2941.

chronicle.description: Thorin and his companions are held prisoner here before their escape in empty wine-barrels.

records.name: Cellars of the Elvenking's Halls
records.description: The lowest storerooms of Thranduil's halls, built over an underground stream that flows out to join the Forest River. Empty wine-barrels from Dorwinion were stacked here awaiting return downriver; in T.A. 2941 Bilbo Baggins used the cellars to smuggle Thorin's company out of the halls inside the empty casks.

chronicle.description: Bilbo hides the dwarves in empty wine-barrels here for their escape down the Forest River.

records.name: Gollum's Cave
records.description: A dark subterranean lake at the very roots of the Misty Mountains, beneath the tunnels of Goblin-town, reached only by a narrow passage. Here Gollum dwelt alone for centuries in a small boat, feeding on blind fish and stray goblins; it was on its shore that Bilbo Baggins found the One Ring in T.A. 2941 and later won the Riddle-game.

chronicle.description: Bilbo Baggins finds the One Ring here and plays the Riddle-game with Gollum.

records.name: Dungeons of Dol Guldur
records.description: The pits beneath the Necromancer's fortress of Dol Guldur, where captives were imprisoned and tormented. The Dwarf-lord Thráin II, driven mad and separated from his Ring, was held and tortured here for years before Gandalf found him dying in T.A. 2850 and learned the location of Erebor's map and key.

chronicle.description: Thráin II is captured and imprisoned in the dungeons of Dol Guldur.
Gandalf finds the dying Thráin here and receives the map and key to Erebor.

records.name: Great Chamber of Thrór
records.description: A great chamber within Erebor near the Front Gate, used by King Thrór for feasts and councils of the Dwarves of Durin's Folk before the coming of Smaug in T.A. 2770. It stood among the upper halls of the Lonely Mountain, close to the great forges and treasuries.

chronicle.description: Thorin and Company pass through the ruined chamber toward the Front Gate.

records.name: Great Hall of Thráin
records.description: A vast hall deep within the Lower Halls of Erebor, at the root of the mountain, from which a secret passage led up to the hidden Back Door. It was through this chamber that Thorin's company crept in T.A. 2941 to spy upon the sleeping dragon Smaug in the treasury beyond.

chronicle.description: Bilbo Baggins passes through on his way to first speak with Smaug.

records.name: Fall of Erebor
records.description: In T.A. 2770 the dragon Smaug descended on the Lonely Mountain out of the north, slew the dwarves who came out to face him at the Front Gate, and seized the hoard of King Thrór for himself. He then fell upon the town of Dale below, burning it and killing Lord Girion, though Girion's wife and infant son escaped downriver to Esgaroth.

chronicle.description: Smaug attacks and conquers Erebor, then destroys the town of Dale.

records.name: Bridge of Dale
records.description: A bridge over the River Running on the approach to Dale and Erebor. After Smaug's death in T.A. 2941, the Men of Lake-town and the Wood-elves approached the Mountain to seek a share of its treasure. Its precise position on this map is reconstructed.

records.name: Bridge of Esgaroth
records.description: The long wooden bridge on piles connecting Lake-town to the western shore of the Long Lake, the only way onto the town by land. A guard-hut stood at its landward end and gates at the lake-ward end, and the bridge could be broken down in times of danger to seal the town off from attack.

records.name: Market-place of Esgaroth
records.description: The wide central square of Lake-town, built around a round pool linked to the lake by a waterway for boats, ringed by wooden quays, ladders, and the greatest houses of the town including the Master's own dwelling. Bilbo and the dwarves were welcomed here with feasting in T.A. 2941 before continuing on to the Lonely Mountain.

chronicle.description: Thorin's company is feasted here by the Master and people of Lake-town.

records.name: Master's House
records.description: The Master's dwelling beside Lake-town's market-place. The Master welcomed Thorin's company in T.A. 2941. After Smaug destroyed the town, that same Master stole gold Bard had given for relief and fled into the wild, where he died of hunger. Bard became King of Dale, never Master of Lake-town.

records.name: Battle of the Field of Celebrant
records.description: Fought on 15 April T.A. 2510 when the Balchoth, having crossed the Anduin, overwhelmed the forces of Gondor's Steward Cirion on this grassy plain between the Silverlode and the Limlight. At the crisis, Eorl the Young and the Éothéod, having ridden south in answer to Cirion's plea, crossed at the Undeeps and fell upon the Balchoth's rear, destroying them and saving Gondor; Cirion afterward granted Calenardhon to the Éothéod as the new realm of Rohan.

chronicle.description: Eorl the Young and the Éothéod ride to Gondor's rescue and destroy the Balchoth.

records.name: Battle of the Plains
records.description: Fought in T.A. 1856 on the plains south of Mirkwood, where the Wainriders defeated Gondor and its Northmen allies. Narmacil II was slain; Marhari died defending the retreat. The survivors withdrew through Dagorlad into Ithilien. Gondor abandoned its other lands east of the Anduin.

chronicle.description: The Wainriders defeat Gondor and King Narmacil II is slain.

records.name: Ring of Isengard
records.description: The great circular wall of hard, unweathering rock that ancient Gondorian builders raised to enclose the vale of Isengard, sheer and impregnable with a single gate on its southern side. Within it Saruman bred his Uruk-hai army; in T.A. 3019 the Ents breached and flooded the Ring, tearing down its walls to make way for the Treegarth of Orthanc.

chronicle.description: The Ents breach the Ring and flood Isengard, ending Saruman's power

records.name: Treegarth of Orthanc
records.description: The grove of trees and Huorns the Ents planted within the levelled Ring of Isengard after Saruman's overthrow, guarding Orthanc so none might enter without Treebeard's leave. Treebeard first called it the Watchwood, then the Treegarth of Orthanc, when Gandalf and the Ring-bearers passed through on their homeward journey that autumn.

chronicle.description: Founded by the Ents on 22 August, after the Battle of Isengard

records.name: Dor-en-Ernil
records.description: "The Land of the Prince," the fief of the Princes of Dol Amroth in southern Gondor, bounded on the east by the river Gilrain and the town of Linhir and on the west by the hills above the havens of Belfalas. The name appears on the Map of Rohan, Gondor and Mordor and on the Unfinished Tales map, though its exact bounds are never fixed in the texts.

records.name: Lefnui
records.description: The westernmost of the five rivers of southern Gondor and, of them, the longest and broadest, rising in the White Mountains and winding southwest past the hills of Pinnath Gelin before emptying into the Bay of Belfalas through a long, narrow firth. Beyond it lay the promontory of Andrast, which the Númenóreans never permanently settled.

records.name: Tarlang's Neck
records.description: A pass over a southern spur of the White Mountains separating the Blackroot Vale (Morthond) from Lamedon. Aragorn led the Grey Company and the Army of the Dead over Tarlang's Neck on their ride from the Stone of Erech to Pelargir in March T.A. 3019. Gondorian folk-legend told that the pass was the broken neck of a fallen giant, Tarlang.

chronicle.description: The Grey Company crosses Tarlang's Neck with the Army of the Dead, bound for Pelargir

records.name: Dol Tarlang
records.description: The northernmost of three small peaks forming the mountain spur at Tarlang's Neck. Gondorian legend held it to be the severed head of the giant Tarlang, who broke his neck falling from the ridge above; the pass below was said to be his neck.

records.name: Cûl Veleg
records.description: The larger of two lesser peaks beside Dol Tarlang on the ridge of Tarlang's Neck, named in Gondorian nomenclature as one of the great stones the giant Tarlang was said to have been carrying when he fell.

records.name: Cûl Bîn
records.description: The smaller of two stones named beside Dol Tarlang on the ridge of Tarlang's Neck, said in local legend to be a burden dropped by the giant Tarlang when he fell and broke his neck, forming the pass below.

records.name: Haudh in Gwanûr
records.description: A mound raised high on the bank of the river Poros above the Crossings, where the twin sons of King Folcwine of Rohan, Folcred and Fastred, were laid side by side after falling in battle against the Haradrim in T.A. 2885. For centuries afterward, Gondor's enemies were said to fear passing the mound.

chronicle.description: Folcred and Fastred of Rohan are buried here after the Battle of the Crossings of Poros

records.name: Variags of Khand
records.description: The warlike men of Khand, southeast of Mordor, shorter of stature and shorter-lived than the Dúnedain. Long allied with Sauron, the Variags joined the Wainriders' invasion of Gondor in T.A. 1944 and fought at the Battle of the Pelennor Fields in T.A. 3019, held in reserve at Osgiliath before being routed by the Knights of Dol Amroth.

chronicle.description: The Variags join the Wainrider invasion in which King Ondoher is killed
The Variags fight at the Battle of the Pelennor Fields and are driven back

records.name: Púkel-men
records.description: Ancient, weathered statues of squatting, big-bellied figures set at every turn of the climbing road up to Dunharrow, carved long ago by the Drúedain who once dwelt in these vales of the White Mountains. The Rohirrim, who had forgotten who made them, named them and rode past undisturbed on their way to war in T.A. 3019.

records.name: Tomb of Elendil
records.description: A hidden mound raised by Isildur on the treeless summit of the hill later called Halifirien, hallowing it as the resting place of his father Elendil. In T.A. 2510 Steward Cirion led Eorl the Young here to swear the Oath binding Gondor and Rohan, revealing the ancient tomb and declaring the hill sacred to both peoples thereafter.

chronicle.description: Isildur raises the tomb of Elendil on the hill of Amon Anwar
Cirion and Eorl swear their Oath of friendship beside the tomb

records.name: Battle of the Pelennor Fields
records.description: The greatest battle of the War of the Ring, fought on the Pelennor before Minas Tirith on 15 March T.A. 3019. The Rohirrim's charge broke the siege of the city; King Théoden fell to the Witch-king, who was in turn slain by Éowyn and Meriadoc Brandybuck; Aragorn's arrival with reinforcements from Pelargir turned the tide to a costly victory for Gondor and Rohan.

chronicle.description: Battle of the Pelennor Fields; Théoden and the Witch-king both fall

records.name: Battle of the Hornburg
records.description: Fought on the night of 3–4 March T.A. 3019, when Saruman's army of Uruk-hai and Dunlendings, over ten thousand strong, assailed King Théoden and some three thousand Rohirrim sheltering in the Hornburg. The defenders held until dawn, when Gandalf returned with Erkenbrand; the enemy, fleeing into Huorn-haunted Helm's Deep, was utterly destroyed.

chronicle.description: Battle of the Hornburg; Saruman's army is destroyed

records.name: First Battle of the Fords of Isen
records.description: Fought on 25 February T.A. 3019, when Saruman's forces struck across the Isen to break Rohan's western defence. Théodred, son of Théoden, was slain defending the crossing, achieving Saruman's chief aim and leaving Rohan's western marches open to invasion.

chronicle.description: First Battle of the Fords of Isen; Prince Théodred is killed

records.name: Second Battle of the Fords of Isen
records.description: Fought on 2 March T.A. 3019, days after the first battle, when Saruman sent a stronger force against the Rohirrim holding the Fords under Grimbold and Elfhelm. Heavily outnumbered, the defenders were driven back and Saruman's army won passage over the Isen into western Rohan.

chronicle.description: Second Battle of the Fords of Isen; Saruman's forces cross into Rohan

records.name: Battle of the Crossings of Poros
records.description: Fought in T.A. 2885 when the Haradrim, urged on by Sauron, invaded Ithilien and forced the crossings of the Poros. Steward Túrin II of Gondor, aided by Rohirrim sent by King Folcwine, defeated the invaders, though Folcwine's twin sons Folcred and Fastred fell side by side and were buried at the Haudh in Gwanûr.

chronicle.description: Gondor and Rohan defeat the Haradrim at the Crossings of Poros

records.name: Battle of Osgiliath
records.description: In T.A. 2475 a great force of Uruk-hai out of Mordor, a new and terrible breed of Orc, overran and sacked Osgiliath. Boromir, son of the Steward Denethor I, drove them out again, but the ruined city was never fully resettled, its western half held afterward only as a Gondorian outpost.

chronicle.description: Uruk-hai sack Osgiliath; Boromir I recaptures the city

records.name: Fall of Osgiliath
records.description: In June T.A. 3018 Sauron's forces struck across the Anduin and seized the eastern half of Osgiliath, breaking its last standing bridge. Some historians reckon this assault, which the Rangers of Ithilien could not prevent, as the true opening blow of the War of the Ring.

chronicle.description: Sauron's forces capture East Osgiliath and break the last bridge

records.name: Battle of the Crossings of Erui
records.description: The decisive battle of the Kin-strife, fought in T.A. 1447 where the road from Pelargir to Minas Tirith crosses the Erui. King Eldacar, backed by the Northmen of the inland fiefs, defeated and personally slew the usurper Castamir, though Castamir's sons escaped downriver to Pelargir with the remnant of his fleet.

chronicle.description: Eldacar defeats and slays Castamir at the Crossings of Erui

records.name: Siege of Pelargir
records.description: After his defeat at the Erui, King Eldacar besieged the sons of Castamir in Pelargir through T.A. 1447–1448. Lacking ships to close the river, Eldacar could not prevent their resupply, and after a year the rebels and their supporters sailed away to Umbar, where they founded an independent lordship hostile to Gondor for generations.

chronicle.description: Castamir's sons abandon Pelargir and sail away to found the rebel realm of Umbar

records.name: Battle of Cair Andros
records.description: On 10 March T.A. 3019, Sauron's forces captured Cair Andros and crossed into Anórien. After the Pelennor battle, Elfhelm's riders drove the invaders out of Anórien toward the island. On the march to the Morannon, Aragorn separately sent men back to retake and hold Cair Andros.

chronicle.description: Sauron's forces seize Cair Andros and cross into Anórien

records.name: Corsairs' Raid on Pelargir
records.description: In T.A. 1634, during the turmoil that followed the Kin-strife, the corsair brothers Angamaitë and Sangahyando, descendants of Castamir, led a fleet from Umbar to ravage Pelargir. King Minardil of Gondor, who was in the city, was slain in the attack, beginning generations of corsair war upon Gondor's coasts.

chronicle.description: Corsairs sack Pelargir and kill King Minardil

records.name: Siege of Gondor
records.description: After overrunning the Pelennor on 13 March T.A. 3019, the Witch-king's host besieged Minas Tirith on 14 March. Grond broke the Great Gate at dawn on 15 March, as the Rohirrim arrived. The allied victory at the Pelennor that day relieved the city.

chronicle.description: The Witch-king besieges Minas Tirith and breaks the Great Gate

records.name: Battle of Pelargir
records.description: On 13 March T.A. 3019, Aragorn and the Grey Company reached Pelargir with the Army of the Dead and captured the Corsairs' fleet. Aragorn released the Dead, gathered living reinforcements and sailed the captured ships up the Anduin, reaching Minas Tirith on 15 March.

chronicle.description: 13 March: Aragorn captures the Corsair fleet with the Army of the Dead.

records.name: Siege of the Hornburg (Long Winter)
records.description: During the Long Winter of T.A. 2758–2759, King Helm Hammerhand held out in the Hornburg and the ravine behind it against Wulf's Dunlendings after Edoras itself had fallen. Helm made terrifying solitary sorties against the besiegers before dying still standing at his post; the ravine has been called Helm's Deep ever since.

chronicle.description: King Helm Hammerhand is besieged in the Hornburg through the Long Winter
Helm dies at his post, giving the ravine its name, Helm's Deep

records.name: Wulf's Seizure of Edoras
records.description: In T.A. 2758 the Dunlending Wulf, aided by Corsair and Easterling attacks elsewhere on Gondor, overran Rohan and killed Prince Haleth defending Edoras, then sat in Meduseld proclaiming himself king. The following March, Fréaláf Hildeson rode from Dunharrow, surprised the Dunlendings, retook Edoras and slew Wulf, ending the occupation.

chronicle.description: Wulf the Dunlending seizes Edoras and Meduseld
Fréaláf Hildeson retakes Edoras and kills Wulf

records.name: Death of Aldamir
records.description: King Aldamir of Gondor fell in battle around T.A. 1540 during a long war against the Haradrim and the Corsairs of Umbar, who harried Gondor's southern lands; the precise site of his death goes unrecorded. His son Vinyarion avenged him and took the title Hyarmendacil II, "South-victor."

chronicle.description: King Aldamir is slain fighting the Haradrim and Corsairs

records.name: Breach of the Rammas Echor
records.description: In the early hours of 13 March T.A. 3019, Sauron's advancing host blasted breaches in the Rammas Echor at many points and wrecked the Causeway Forts, forcing Gondor's outlying defenders to flee across the Pelennor to the city. The wall's fall opened the way for the Siege of Gondor that began within hours.

chronicle.description: Sauron's forces breach the Rammas Echor before dawn
